\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/case_study:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat}} should be built via their static factory methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::at}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::slice}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::take}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::label}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::labels}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::span}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::where}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::all}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::name}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::at}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::names}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::take}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::slice}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::span}}) rather than by setting their fields directly — those
fields are an implementation detail of how the selector is dispatched internally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positional slices (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::slice}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::slice}}) are half\sphinxhyphen{}open, exclusive on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}
— the same convention as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}. Label\sphinxhyphen{}based ranges (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::span}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::span}})
are inclusive on both ends — a different convention, worth remembering when
switching between the two.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range single position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::at(row)}} after negative normalization) is a
validation error, matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}’s behavior, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s silent clamping.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}} overload only works on a frame with a named case axis from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}; on a frame using the plain default case label, use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::label(...)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::labels(...)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::span(...)}} instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}} on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}} generalizes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} to matching several
named levels simultaneously — every listed level must match its paired value for a
row to be included.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts selected features to a different scalar dtype, or to an entirely different
payload kind (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} numeric, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} calendar), while
leaving every other feature untouched. There are three ways to call it, in order of
increasing power:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dtype\sphinxhyphen{}only} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(name, ScalarType)}} pairs) — the same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}}:
recast a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature to a different concrete scalar type (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}, and so on) without changing its payload kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{cross\sphinxhyphen{}kind} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(name, ThreadCastTarget)}} pairs) — convert a feature to a different
payload kind entirely (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}), using default
parse/format behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{full control} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}CastSpec\textgreater{}}}) — the same cross\sphinxhyphen{}kind conversion, but with
an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastOptions}} per feature: a target \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{series\_dtype}}, a date
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format}} string, and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}} policy for unparseable text.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When two entries in one call target the same feature name, only the first is applied
and every subsequent one is silently skipped — not an error, just a quiet no\sphinxhyphen{}op for
the duplicate.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}CastSpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CastSpec\{feature, target, options\}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} is the column to convert (must exist;
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::cast: unknown feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} otherwise), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastTarget}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}) is the destination payload kind, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastOptions}}) carries:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{series\_dtype}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}ScalarType\textgreater{}}}): when casting \sphinxstyleemphasis{to} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, the
concrete numeric type to land on (defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} when converting from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} text or ticks, or left unchanged when the source is
already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): an explicit date\sphinxhyphen{}format string, consulted only when
casting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParseInvalid}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Raise}}): what happens to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} value that
fails to parse as a date under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Raise}} throws, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Null}} produces a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
cell instead.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_dtypes} (pairs of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(std::string\_view, ScalarType)}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Recast named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features to a different scalar dtype, exactly like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_targets} (pairs of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(std::string\_view, ThreadCastTarget)}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert named features to a different payload kind using default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastOptions}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{series\_dtype}} unset, no format string, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid = Raise}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested features cast; every untargeted feature is
preserved unchanged.

Example 4. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} with an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format}}: an unparseable value

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A duplicate feature name across multiple entries in one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}} call is not an
error — only the first entry for that name is applied, and later ones are silently
ignored.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} never raises on unparseable text; it always produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
instead. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} is the opposite: it raises by default
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParseInvalid::Raise}}) unless you set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.invalid = ParseInvalid::Null}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casting a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}detects whether the values look like
an integer\sphinxhyphen{}encoded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{YYYYMMDD}} calendar date (every valid value in the range
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10000101}}\textendash{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{99991231}}) or like raw epoch\sphinxhyphen{}nanosecond ticks, and interprets the whole
column accordingly — it does not support a mixed column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_dtypes}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}’s equivalent overload are literally the same
function under a different name — pick whichever reads better at the call site.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::clip}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:dataframe-clip}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{clip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clamps every numeric feature on the frame to the closed range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}min\_value, max\_value{]}}}:
a value below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}}, a value above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}} becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}}, and everything already inside the range is left untouched. This is a
whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame elementwise operation — there is no per\sphinxhyphen{}feature bounds parameter, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip()}}
applies one shared range across every numeric column on the frame in a single call.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The common use is capping outliers before a summary or a model input — a small number of
extreme values (a data\sphinxhyphen{}entry typo, a sensor spike) can otherwise dominate a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}} or a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}} far out of proportion to how much they should matter.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower bound. Any numeric cell below this value is replaced with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{max\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upper bound. Any numeric cell above this value is replaced with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every numeric feature clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}min\_value, max\_value{]}}}.
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) and null cells are left
exactly as they were.

first place.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip()}} applies one shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}min\_value, max\_value{]}}} range to \sphinxstylestrong{every} numeric
feature on the frame. If different features genuinely need different bounds, clip them
one at a time via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}} with a per\sphinxhyphen{}feature expression instead of a
single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip()}} call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nulls pass through unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip()}} is not a substitute for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}} should not exceed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}}; passing a backwards range collapses every
numeric cell to a single value, which is rarely the intent.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/round::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::round}}}}}}}: a different elementwise numeric cleanup, rounding
instead of clamping.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::fillnull}}}}}}}: handle missing values, which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip()}}
deliberately leaves alone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::replace}}}}}}}: swap specific values rather than clamping a whole
range.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Merges this frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} along the \sphinxstyleemphasis{case} axis (matched by case\sphinxhyphen{}label value, the
same way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}}}}}} matches rows), then decides what happens to each of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s features according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spec.op}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CombineOp::Features}}} (the default, via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine(other)}}): keep every feature
from this frame as\sphinxhyphen{}is, then bring in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s features too — a feature name that
doesn’t already exist is added outright; a feature name that collides with an
existing one is added under a disambiguated name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name + spec.collision\_suffix}},
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_right"}}, with a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_3}}, … suffix appended if that name is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{also} taken). Nothing from the left frame is ever overwritten in this mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CombineOp::Update}}}: only touch features that already exist on this frame —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}\sphinxhyphen{}only features are ignored entirely. For each shared feature, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spec.overwrite}}
decides whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s non\sphinxhyphen{}null cells replace the left’s values outright
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the default), or only fill in the left’s own missing cells while leaving
its existing values alone (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/join::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/update::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update()}}}}}}} are both thin convenience wrappers
around \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join(other, suffix)}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine(other, \{.op = Features, .collision\_suffix = suffix\})}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update(other, overwrite)}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine(other, \{.op = Update, .overwrite = overwrite, .cases = FrameMatchRule::KeepLeft\})}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame to combine with. Its cases are matched to this frame’s cases by
case\sphinxhyphen{}label value, not physical row position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{spec} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const CombineSpec\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CombineSpec\{\}}} via the plain overload)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CombineOp}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}}): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Update}}, as described
above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_suffix}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_right"}}): suffix appended to a
colliding feature name in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}} mode. Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty if any collision
actually occurs, or the call throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::combine(features): collision\_suffix must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty when duplicate features exist"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{overwrite}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Update}} mode, whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s
non\sphinxhyphen{}null values replace existing left values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or only fill left’s own nulls
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FrameMatchRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Unite}}): how the two frames’ case axes are
reconciled — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Unite}} (union of both sides’ case labels), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Common}} (only labels
present on both sides), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KeepLeft}} (exactly this frame’s case labels), or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KeepRight}} (exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s case labels).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
The combined frame, following the case\sphinxhyphen{}matching rule and feature policy above.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::combine(features): collision\PYGZus{}suffix must be non\PYGZhy{}empty when duplicate features exist
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} both have an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{age}} feature, so the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}} mode
needs to disambiguate one of them with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_suffix}} — leaving it empty
removes any way to do that safely, so the call rejects it up front rather than
guessing.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case matching is always by label value, never by physical row position — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}
row and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} row line up because they share a case label, not because they
occupy the same index.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}} mode never overwrites anything from the left frame; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Update}} mode never
introduces a feature the left frame didn’t already have. Pick the mode based on
which invariant you need.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{overwrite = false}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Update}} mode is a “fill gaps only” merge: only cells
that are already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} on the left get replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s value, and only if
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s value there is itself non\sphinxhyphen{}null.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature\sphinxhyphen{}name collision in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Features}} mode with an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_suffix}} throws
rather than silently dropping or overwriting either side’s column.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/compare:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A plain alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}}}}}}}: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compare()}} overload forwards straight
through to the matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}} overload with the same arguments, with no independent
behavior of its own. It exists as an alternate, more generic\sphinxhyphen{}sounding name for the
same not\sphinxhyphen{}equal comparison — some call sites read more naturally as “compare this
frame against a baseline” than “check where it’s not\sphinxhyphen{}equal to a baseline,” even though
the two produce byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte identical results.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
compare() is ne(), not a general comparator
Despite the generic name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compare()}} does not let you choose which relation to
evaluate — it is hardwired to not\sphinxhyphen{}equal. For any other relation, call
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} directly.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/compare:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (numeric scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned
frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). Identical in every respect

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compare()}}, unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/compare:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} overload here, unlike the rest of the comparison
family — text comparison must go through {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}}}}}}} (or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}})
directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing\sphinxhyphen{}value propagation is identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}}}}}}}: a cell compared against a
missing value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::conform}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:dataframe-conform}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{conform}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reshapes this frame to structurally match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, in two steps: first, its features
are reordered (never renamed or dropped) to exactly match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other.features()}}’s name
order — this requires both frames to have the \sphinxstyleemphasis{same number} of features, and every
name in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s feature list must exist verbatim on this frame, or the call throws.
Second, the reordered frame’s cases are reindexed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s exact case\sphinxhyphen{}label order,
via the same by\sphinxhyphen{}label matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}}}}}} uses (with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}, so any
label present in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} but absent from this frame becomes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} row).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conform()}} is the one\sphinxhyphen{}call version of “make my frame line up with this other frame’s
shape” — useful right before an operation like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}}
that checks structural correspondence (feature order and case count) rather than
matching by label itself, or simply to present two related frames with an identical
row and column order for a side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side report.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The reference frame whose structure (feature order and case\sphinxhyphen{}label order) this frame
should be reshaped to match. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s own \sphinxstyleemphasis{values} are irrelevant to the result —
only its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}} list and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().values()}} axis are consulted.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s feature order and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s case order. Feature count
must match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s exactly; case labels absent from this frame appear as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
rows, matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}’s no\sphinxhyphen{}fill behavior.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::conform: missing feature \PYGZsq{}c\PYGZsq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{raw2}} only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bad\_reference}} lists \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c}} doesn’t
exist on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{raw2}} at all, so the call rejects it before reordering anything.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both frames must have exactly the same number of features, and every name in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s feature list must already exist on this frame — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conform()}} reorders, it
never introduces or drops features the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignSpec}} can.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A duplicate name in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s feature list throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::conform: duplicate feature in target \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}}, and a name that
doesn’t exist on this frame throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::conform: missing feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}}.
In practice, only the second is reachable through normal construction: a real
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} can never actually hold two columns with the same name in the first
place (attempting it throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame: duplicate column name \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} at
construction time), so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other.features()}} can never itself contain a duplicate by
the time \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conform()}} sees it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case reindexing follows exactly the same by\sphinxhyphen{}label, no\sphinxhyphen{}fill rules as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::align(new\_label)}}}}}}} — a case label present in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} but
absent from this frame becomes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} row rather than an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conform()}} is purely structural — it never combines or merges values between the
two frames the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}} does.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::align}}}}}}}: the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level, single\sphinxhyphen{}axis alignment primitive
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conform()}}’s case\sphinxhyphen{}reindexing step is built on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::combine}}}}}}}: actually merge two frames’ values together,
once they’re already structurally compatible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reorder}}}}}}}: reorder features by an explicit name list
without also touching the case axis.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::copy}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:dataframe-copy}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{copy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write duplicate of the frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} is implemented as simply
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{return *this;}}, so the new handle initially shares the exact same underlying storage
as the source. This is safe and cheap because every mutating operation on a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} — the trailing\sphinxhyphen{}underscore methods like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/title_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title\_()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_()}}}}}}} — detaches from shared storage
first if it isn’t uniquely owned, transparently cloning before writing. In practice,
this means \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} behaves exactly like an independent deep copy from the caller’s
point of view: mutating the copy never affects the original, and vice versa. You
never need to reason about the sharing directly — it’s an implementation detail that
only exists to make \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} (and ordinary handle copies in general) cheap when no
mutation ever happens.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new handle to the frame’s data. Feature order, case labels, title, and every
cell value are preserved exactly.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Copy a frame before downstream experimentation.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{renamed.rename\_(...)}} mutates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{renamed}} in place — internally, this triggers a
copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write clone the moment it detects the underlying storage is still shared with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}} itself is completely unaffected.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} preserves feature order, case labels, title, and case\sphinxhyphen{}axis metadata exactly
alongside every cell value — nothing is normalized or reset.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The overwhelming majority of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s own methods are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} and already
return a new frame rather than mutating in place, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} is mainly useful right
before calling one of the trailing\sphinxhyphen{}underscore in\sphinxhyphen{}place mutators
({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/title_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title\_()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put\_()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}}}}}}}) on a value you want to keep a
pristine original of.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}} always returns a defined frame if called on a defined frame — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a correlation matrix across the frame’s numeric features and returns it as a
square \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}: one row and one column per participating feature, with cell
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, j)}} holding the correlation between feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} and feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{j}}. The diagonal is
always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (every feature correlates perfectly with itself), and the matrix is symmetric
— \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr(i, j) == corr(j, i)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}} is naturally the next step after {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} tells
you what each feature looks like in isolation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}} tells you how features move
together — useful for spotting redundant features before modeling, or for a quick check
that two columns that \sphinxstyleemphasis{should} be related (a price and a cost, a signal and its lagged
value) actually are.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned view. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} gives you explicit control over when and
how you render or print the result; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} allows the returned view to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in
temporary display contexts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{method} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CorrMethod}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The correlation statistic to compute:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}: ordinary linear correlation — sensitive to the actual magnitude and shape
of the relationship, and the right default when you expect roughly linear
relationships between numeric features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}: rank correlation — computed on the ranks of the values rather than the
values themselves, so it captures monotonic (not necessarily linear) relationships and
is less sensitive to outliers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}}: rank\sphinxhyphen{}concordance correlation — another rank\sphinxhyphen{}based measure, generally
more robust than Spearman on small samples at the cost of being more expensive to
compute.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit feature subset to correlate. Leave this out to let PlussMic infer every
numeric feature on the frame automatically; pass a subset when you only care about the
relationships among a handful of columns (especially useful on a wide frame, where the
full matrix would be large and mostly uninteresting).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A correlation matrix view whose rows and columns correspond, in the same order, to
the participating numeric features (either every numeric feature on the frame, or
the explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} subset you passed).

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values are unchanged here because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} are all monotonically related to
each other in this tiny sample — Pearson and Spearman only tend to diverge once a
relationship is monotonic but not linear (or once outliers are present), which four
clean points does not exercise. On real data with heavier tails or a non\sphinxhyphen{}linear\sphinxhyphen{}but\sphinxhyphen{}
monotonic relationship, expect Pearson and Spearman to disagree, sometimes
substantially.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Restrict the correlation matrix to an explicit feature subset.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}base}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=================
     | x     z   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
x    |  1    \PYGZhy{}0.4
z    | \PYGZhy{}0.4   1  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[2 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} is not just a display convenience — on a frame with many numeric
columns, computing the full N×N matrix and then slicing it down is wasted work compared
to naming the handful of columns you actually want compared.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. Combine an explicit subset with a non\sphinxhyphen{}default method.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}base}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{KendallTau}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===================================
     | x              z            
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
x    |  1             \PYGZhy{}0.3333333333
z    | \PYGZhy{}0.3333333333   1           
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[2 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Kendall’s tau reports a smaller magnitude (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}0.333}} vs. Pearson’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}0.4}}) for the same
pair of features — a reminder that “correlated” is method\sphinxhyphen{}dependent, and that the three
methods are not interchangeable numbers with the same scale, only the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}}
range and sign convention.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 5. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render = true}} and let the returned view print itself, with no
explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} at all.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}base}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=======================
     | x     y     z   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
x    |  1     1    \PYGZhy{}0.4
y    |  1     1    \PYGZhy{}0.4
z    | \PYGZhy{}0.4  \PYGZhy{}0.4   1  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same matrix as Example 1 — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_base.corr(false)}} versus this bare
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_base.corr(true);}} statement differ only in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}}. Every other example
on this page assigns the result to a variable and streams it explicitly; here,
the temporary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} is destroyed at the end of the statement without
ever being captured, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render = true}} is what makes that destruction print
automatically. With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render = false}}, this same bare statement
would produce no output.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are ignored even when they exist on the source frame — there is
no need to drop \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} columns manually before calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When you pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, only that subset participates in the matrix, and only those
columns need to be numeric.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All three methods report values in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} indicate a perfect
monotonic (Spearman/Kendall) or linear (Pearson) relationship, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} indicates none.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::corr\_with}}}}}}}: correlate one frame against one or more peer
frames instead of correlating a frame’s features against each other.

moving on to cross\sphinxhyphen{}feature correlation.

\sphinxstepscope




\subparagraph{DataFrame::corr\_with}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:dataframe-corr-with}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CorrMethod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{method}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{others}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CorrMethod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{method}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Correlates this frame against one or more \sphinxstyleemphasis{peer} frames, feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature under the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{same} name — the cross\sphinxhyphen{}frame counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}}’s within\sphinxhyphen{}frame,
feature\sphinxhyphen{}against\sphinxhyphen{}feature matrix. For each feature name shared by both frames (matched
by name, restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features on both sides), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_with()}}
computes a single correlation value between this frame’s column and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s
same\sphinxhyphen{}named column, treating each row (matched by case label, restricted to labels
present on both sides) as one paired observation. The result is a compact, one\sphinxhyphen{}value\sphinxhyphen{}
per\sphinxhyphen{}shared\sphinxhyphen{}feature summary — not a full N×N matrix, since there’s exactly one
sensible comparison per shared name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}frame overload returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose case labels \sphinxstyleemphasis{are} the shared
feature names; the multi\sphinxhyphen{}frame overload runs the same computation once per peer frame
and lays the results side by side as columns named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_1}}, … in the
order \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{others}} was given.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, single\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The one frame to correlate against, feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature under matching names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{others} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}}}, multi\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Several frames to correlate against in one call; each becomes one output column,
named positionally (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_1}}, …) rather than by any property of the
peer frame itself. Throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::corr\_with: expected at least one comparison frame"}} if empty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{method} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CorrMethod}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}} — the same three correlation statistics
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} supports, with the same tradeoffs described there.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimum number of paired, non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations required for a feature’s correlation
to be computed at all; must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 1}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
(single\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload) One value per feature name shared by both frames, case\sphinxhyphen{}
labeled by feature name. Throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::corr\_with: no common numeric     features"}} if this frame and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} share no numeric feature name at all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(multi\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload) One column per peer frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_1}}, …), each
holding the same per\sphinxhyphen{}feature correlation values as the single\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload would
for that one comparison — including the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"no common numeric features"}} throw,
per peer frame, since each column is computed via one single\sphinxhyphen{}peer call.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other\PYGZus{}run}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{this\PYGZus{}run}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{other\PYGZus{}run}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
x  0.981155781
y  0.8
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} correlates almost perfectly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.981...}}) between the two runs; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} correlates more
loosely (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.8}}). Each value compares \sphinxstyleemphasis{this frame’s} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} against \sphinxstyleemphasis{the other frame’s}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}, row\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}row — not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{this\_run.x}} against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{this\_run.y}}, which is what
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} would give you instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Correlate against two peer frames at once, one of which is a perfect
mirror\sphinxhyphen{}image (and therefore perfectly \sphinxstyleemphasis{anti}\sphinxhyphen{}correlated).

one sequence corresponds exactly to the same rank in the other, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}
(rank correlation) reports a perfect \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}} sees the same relationship

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{this\_run}} only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{disjoint}} only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} — with no shared
feature name at all, there is nothing to correlate, so the single\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload
rejects the call outright rather than returning an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. The
multi\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload separately rejects an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{others}} list before looking at
feature names at all.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr_with:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only features present, by name, on \sphinxstyleemphasis{both} frames participate; a feature unique to
either side is silently skipped, never padded with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows are matched by case\sphinxhyphen{}label value before the statistic is computed — this is a
case\sphinxhyphen{}aware comparison, not a blind positional zip of the two columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The multi\sphinxhyphen{}peer overload’s output columns are always named positionally
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_1}}, …); there is no way to have it adopt a peer frame’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title()}} or some other identifying name automatically.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::count}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:dataframe-count}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts non\sphinxhyphen{}missing entries along the requested axis and returns one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} counts. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}, and the other numeric
reducers, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}} does not skip non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features — every feature in the frame
participates, because counting present\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}missing cells doesn’t require numeric
semantics the way averaging or summing does. There is also no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} parameter:
counting \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} the null\sphinxhyphen{}aware operation, so there is nothing to toggle.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) counts down each feature’s cases,
producing one count per feature — how many of that column’s cells are non\sphinxhyphen{}null.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} counts across each row’s features instead, producing one count per
case — how many of that row’s cells (across every feature) are non\sphinxhyphen{}null.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} entry per feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or per case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}),
holding the number of non\sphinxhyphen{}missing cells counted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} column) appears in the result and reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, correctly excluding
its one missing entry at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}. Compare this to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} on the same frame: those methods would silently drop \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}}
from the result entirely rather than count it.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}’s result is labeled by feature name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or by case index
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced
from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature participates regardless of type — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} columns are all counted. This is the one numeric\sphinxhyphen{}style reducer that does
not restrict itself to numeric features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} parameter because there is nothing to skip: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}} always
reports the non\sphinxhyphen{}null count, never a poisoned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For counting distinct values rather than non\sphinxhyphen{}null ones, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct()}}}}}}}. For the most frequent values, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sum}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mean}}}}}}}: numeric\sphinxhyphen{}only reducers that
skip non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features rather than counting them.

\subparagraph{DataFrame::count\_by}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:dataframe-count-by}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{count\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a frequency table for a single feature: one row per distinct value of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}, paired with how many cases carry that value, sorted from most frequent to
least frequent (ties broken alphabetically by the value itself). It is a dedicated
shortcut for the single most common {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}}}}}} query — “how many of
each?” — without hand\sphinxhyphen{}writing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupSpec}} for a plain count.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature whose distinct values define the groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cap the result to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} most frequent groups after sorting. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the default)
keeps every group; a positive value truncates the (already count\sphinxhyphen{}sorted) result down
to that many rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether a missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} value is excluded from the count entirely (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the
default) or allowed to form its own group (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, following the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A two\sphinxhyphen{}column frequency table: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} (the distinct values) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}} (an
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} occurrence count), sorted by count descending, then by value ascending on
ties.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Tally every distinct value of a grouping feature.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sort is always count\sphinxhyphen{}descending, value\sphinxhyphen{}ascending\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}ties — there is no
parameter to reverse either ordering; pipe the result through
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values}}}}}}} afterward if you need a different order. A
missing key is never alphabetized against real values for tie\sphinxhyphen{}breaking; it
always sorts after every real value tied with it on count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}} gives a missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} value its own group in the count,
printed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the output, rather than excluding those rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} truncates \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} sorting, so it always keeps the most frequent groups, not
an arbitrary prefix of the unsorted data.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::covar}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:dataframe-covar}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{covar}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the pairwise covariance matrix across the frame’s numeric features — the
same square, symmetric, one\sphinxhyphen{}row\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}column\sphinxhyphen{}per\sphinxhyphen{}feature layout as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}},
but reporting raw covariance instead of a normalized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}} correlation coefficient.
The diagonal holds each feature’s own variance (covariance with itself); off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal
cell \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, j)}} holds the covariance between feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} and feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{j}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
features are silently excluded, exactly as in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}} answers “how strongly (and in what direction) do these features move
together, on a fixed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}} scale?”, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{covar()}} answers the same directional
question but on each feature’s own original scale — useful when the actual magnitude
of joint variation matters (for example, feeding a covariance matrix into a downstream
statistical model), at the cost of values that aren’t directly comparable across
feature pairs with different units or scales.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const StatisticOptions\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): “delta degrees of freedom” — the
covariance sum is divided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(paired\_count \sphinxhyphen{} ddof)}}. The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} gives the
usual sample covariance (Bessel’s correction); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} gives the population covariance,
dividing by the raw paired observation count instead. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): minimum number of paired,
non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations required before a cell is computed at all; cells that don’t
meet it come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, following the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A square covariance matrix over the frame’s numeric features, in the same feature
order as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} would produce for the same frame.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{B}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{C}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=======================
     | x     y     z   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
x    | 1.25  2.5   \PYGZhy{}0.5
y    | 2.5   5     \PYGZhy{}1  
z    | \PYGZhy{}0.5  \PYGZhy{}1    1.25
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With four paired observations, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} divides by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}, so every
value in Example 1’s matrix is scaled down by exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3/4}} here (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.666... * 0.75 = 1.25}}, and so on) — the same relationship as between a sample variance and a
population variance anywhere else in the library.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/covar:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never participate and are never padded into the matrix as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rows/columns — they simply don’t appear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} (population) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (sample, the default) differ by a constant
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(n\sphinxhyphen{}1)/n}} scaling factor for a given pair, assuming the same paired\sphinxhyphen{}observation
count for both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} instead when you want values on a fixed, comparable
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}} scale rather than each feature’s own units.

\end{itemize}
