\subparagraph{DataFrame::duplicated}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:dataframe-duplicated}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} mask, one entry per case, marking which rows are duplicates of an
earlier or later row when compared across the selected features. Rows are grouped by
the concatenated string value of every selected feature (missing cells compare as a
shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} placeholder, so two rows both missing the same feature are still
considered a match on that feature); any group with more than one row contributes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} entries according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}}. This returns the mask itself —
for the frame with those rows already removed, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_duplicates()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} cannot both be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at the same time — asking to keep
both the first and last occurrence exempt from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} is ambiguous when a group has
three or more rows, so the two flags are mutually exclusive.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features to compare when deciding whether two rows match. An empty range (the
default) compares \sphinxstylestrong{every} column in the frame — including any unique identifier
column, which means no two rows will ever match if such a column is present. Pass the
specific feature names that define a “duplicate” for your use case (for example, just
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"city", "product"\}}}, ignoring an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} column that is unique per row by design).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the first row encountered in each duplicate group is left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (not
flagged), and every later row in that group is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the last row encountered in each duplicate group is left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, and
every earlier row in that group is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Cannot be combined with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxstylestrong{every} row in a duplicate group
is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — including what would otherwise be the exempted first or last row —
useful when you want to identify entire duplicate groups rather than just the “extra”
occurrences.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} entry per case, labeled by case index and named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"duplicated"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} wherever that row is considered a duplicate under the current
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} policy.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Flag every occurrence after the first one in each duplicate group — the
default policy.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Phone}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Phone}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  false
1  true
2  false
3  true
4  false
5  true
Name: duplicated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} all share \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(Accra, Laptop)}}; case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} is the first occurrence
and stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} are flagged. Cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} share
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(Tema, Phone)}}; case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} is flagged. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi, Laptop}}) has no match anywhere else in the frame, so it is never flagged. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}
was deliberately left out of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} — including it would make every row unique
and nothing would ever be flagged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}} to exempt the \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} occurrence in each group
instead of the first.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes\PYGZus{}keep\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes\PYGZus{}keep\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  true
2  true
3  false
4  false
5  false
Name: duplicated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The flags flip relative to Example 1: within \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(Accra, Laptop)}}, cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} are
now flagged and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} (the last one) is exempt; within \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(Tema, Phone)}}, case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is
flagged and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} (the last one) is exempt.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for both flags to mark every row in a duplicate group,
including what would otherwise be the exempted first or last occurrence.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  true
2  true
3  true
4  false
5  true
Name: duplicated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every case belonging to a group with more than one member is now flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} —
there is no exempted representative — while case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} (the one group with a single
member) is still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, since a group of one is never a duplicate of anything.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s result is always named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"duplicated"}} and labeled by case index,
and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced from the source
frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grouping is done by comparing string representations of the selected features’
values, so it works uniformly across numeric, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
features in the same call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing cells compare as a shared placeholder, so two rows that are both missing the
same selected feature can still be grouped as duplicates of each other on that basis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}} together is a validation error.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::encode}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:dataframe-encode}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
New method
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::encode()}} did not exist prior to this page — it was added to close a real
gap in the categorical\sphinxhyphen{}encoding surface (see “What It Does” below) and is documented
here for the first time alongside its implementation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{encode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EncodeMode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EncodeMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{OneHot}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{EncodeOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encodes a single categorical feature into a machine\sphinxhyphen{}learning\sphinxhyphen{}friendly numeric form, in
one of two modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EncodeMode::OneHot}}} (the default): replaces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} with one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} indicator
column per distinct value — the standard “dummy variable” / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_dummies()}}\sphinxhyphen{}style
encoding. Each new column is named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{prefix\}\{value\}"}} and holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} exactly where
the source row equals that value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} elsewhere, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for any row where the
source itself was missing (every indicator column agrees on which rows are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} —
a missing category never silently reads as “none of the above”).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EncodeMode::Ordinal}}}: replaces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} in place with a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} column of
integer codes, one per distinct value — internally, this mode is a thin wrapper
around {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}}, keeping only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} and discarding the level
list \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}} would otherwise also give you.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}}, the closest existing tools were {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}} (which
returns a \sphinxstyleemphasis{separate} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding\{codes, levels\}}} pair rather than a modified
frame) and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note().indicate()}}}}}}} (which does genuine multi\sphinxhyphen{}label indicator
expansion for delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}separated tag strings, and returns only the new columns rather
than the whole frame). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} is the direct, single\sphinxhyphen{}call “turn this one column into
model\sphinxhyphen{}ready numbers, in place, on the whole frame” entry point either mode’s use case
was previously missing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to encode. Must exist on the frame; throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::encode: unknown feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} otherwise. Works on a feature of any
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) — “distinct value” is
determined the same way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}} determines it, not restricted to text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EncodeMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}}, as described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const EncodeOptions\&}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default empty, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} only): prefix for each new
indicator column’s name. Leave empty to default to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_first}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} only): omit the indicator column
for the first\sphinxhyphen{}encountered distinct value. Useful when you specifically need
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} indicator columns for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} categories (avoiding the “dummy variable trap” of
perfectly collinear indicators expected by some downstream linear models).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_levels}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, both modes): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default) orders distinct values
by first appearance in the frame; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} sorts them lexicographically instead. This
determines both the indicator\sphinxhyphen{}column order in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} mode and the code assignment
in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}} mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ordered}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}} only): forwarded directly to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}}’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ordered}} flag.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} replaced: by its indicator columns (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}}, inserted
at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s original position, expanding the frame by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{level\_count \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} columns,
or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{level\_count \sphinxhyphen{} 2}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_first}}) or by a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} code column
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}}, same column count as before). Every other feature is unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. One\sphinxhyphen{}hot encode a categorical feature with the defaults, including a
missing value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} mode only ever compares distinct\sphinxhyphen{}value \sphinxstyleemphasis{keys} (the same string\sphinxhyphen{}key
comparison {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}} uses via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify\_key\_parts}}), so it works on
numeric or calendar features too, not just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text — a small\sphinxhyphen{}cardinality
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} of status codes can be one\sphinxhyphen{}hot encoded exactly the same way.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing source value propagates as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} to every generated indicator column in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OneHot}} mode, and to the single code column in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}} mode — it is never
silently coerced into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} or into its own numeric code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_levels}} controls category order (and therefore both indicator\sphinxhyphen{}column order and
which value gets dropped by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_first}}, or which value gets code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}) — pass
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for a stable, data\sphinxhyphen{}independent ordering across repeated runs on frames whose
row order might change.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}} mode is a thin convenience wrapper: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{customers.encode(feature, EncodeMode::Ordinal, opts)}} is equivalent to taking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor(feature, opts.ordered, opts.sort\_levels).codes}} and splicing it back into the frame at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s position
— reach for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}}}}}} directly if you also need the level list.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise equality, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the
same shape as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}} is one of six comparison methods
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge}}) that share the same
overload set — a scalar, a string, another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} broadcast by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} — mirroring the arithmetic family’s shape (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}), except every
comparison method returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}} per feature instead of a numeric result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for the named method over the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{==}} operator when you want to chain it inline in
a pipeline, or when comparing against another frame with non\sphinxhyphen{}default alignment rules.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, in one of three shapes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}: one numeric scalar, compared against every numeric feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}: one text value, compared against every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature.
Comparing a non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature against a string is not a supported combination.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}: another frame, compared feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature and case\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}case
after the two frames are aligned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}: one column of values, broadcast according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand is broadcast — identical meaning to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (the default) supplies one value per
feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand is aligned to the current
frame before the comparison runs. Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared against a missing
value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A cell where either operand is missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the result, not
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — a missing value is never considered equal or unequal to anything, including
another missing value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
String comparison only applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features; attempting it against a
numeric feature is not a supported combination.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its full overload shape and alignment semantics with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} — see those pages for the
distinct relations, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the fuller explanation of the shared
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/equals:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame identity check — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} matches this frame in every
respect: same case count, same feature count, same feature names \sphinxstyleemphasis{in the same order},
same case\sphinxhyphen{}label dtype and validity pattern, and every cell’s payload kind, validity,
and value matching. Where {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} returns a per\sphinxhyphen{}cell boolean mask, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals()}}
collapses the whole comparison down to one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two comparison modes are available:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exact} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals(other)}}, the default): every value is compared via its formatted
string representation. No floating\sphinxhyphen{}point tolerance — two numerically\sphinxhyphen{}close\sphinxhyphen{}but\sphinxhyphen{}not\sphinxhyphen{}
identical floats do not compare equal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tolerant} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals(other, atol, rtol)}}): for numeric feature cells specifically,
values are compared with the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|a \sphinxhyphen{} b| \textless{}= atol + rtol * max(|a|, |b|)}} rule
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numpy.allclose}} uses, absorbing small floating\sphinxhyphen{}point discrepancies from independent
computation paths that should mathematically agree. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric cells (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, or a numeric/non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric mismatch) always fall back to exact
string comparison even in tolerant mode — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atol}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtol}} only relax numeric\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
comparisons.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case labels are always compared exactly, even in tolerant mode
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atol}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtol}} only relax the \sphinxstyleemphasis{feature cell} comparison. Case labels (and their dtype
and validity pattern) are always compared with exact string equality, regardless of
which overload you call.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No alignment happens before either check: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals()}} does not try to reorder features
or match case labels first the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} can with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} — the two frames are compared exactly as supplied. If you need to
compare two frames that carry the same data in a different feature or case order, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}}}}}}} (or the alignment\sphinxhyphen{}aware
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}) first.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/equals:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame to compare against. Compared exactly as given — feature order and case
order both matter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{atol} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, tolerant overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The absolute tolerance term. Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{rtol} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, tolerant overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The relative tolerance term, scaled by the larger of the two values being compared at
each cell. Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/equals:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} only when both frames have identical case count, feature count, feature
names (in order), case\sphinxhyphen{}label dtype and values, and every feature’s payload kind,
validity pattern, and cell values (exactly, or within \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atol}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtol}} for numeric
cells under the tolerant overload). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/equals:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals(other)}}) compares values via their formatted string
representation, with no floating\sphinxhyphen{}point tolerance — two numerically\sphinxhyphen{}close\sphinxhyphen{}but\sphinxhyphen{}not\sphinxhyphen{}
identical floats will \sphinxstylestrong{not} compare equal. Use the tolerant overload
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals(other, atol, rtol)}}) when small floating\sphinxhyphen{}point discrepancies from
independent computation paths should be treated as equal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The tolerant overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atol}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtol}} only apply to numeric\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature cell
comparisons; case labels, non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features, and any cell where one side isn’t
numeric always fall back to exact string comparison.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Under the tolerant overload, two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} values compare equal to each other (unlike
ordinary IEEE 754 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN != NaN}} semantics), and two infinities compare equal only if
they have the same sign.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature order matters: a frame with the same features in a different order is not
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals()}}\sphinxhyphen{}equal, even though {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Feature}} alignment would
happily compare them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missingness is part of the contract — a valid cell and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell at the same
position never compare equal, even if the underlying storage happens to hold the
same bit pattern.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} overload; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals()}} never re\sphinxhyphen{}aligns before comparing.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/equals:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::eq}}}}}}}: per\sphinxhyphen{}cell equality mask, with optional alignment via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}.

baseline before mutating and re\sphinxhyphen{}checking with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equals()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reorder}}}}}}}: normalize feature order before comparing two
frames that hold the same data in a different arrangement.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::exp}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:dataframe-exp}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies the natural exponential function (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}x}}) elementwise to every numeric feature,
leaving non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) unchanged — the same
delegation pattern as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/round::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}}}}}}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}float numeric
features are upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} first, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}x}} is rarely a whole number even for
integer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e}} raised to that value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Exponentiate a numeric feature.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==================
     | x          
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
a    | 1          
b    | 2.718281828
c    | 7.389056099
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}0 = 1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}1 ≈ 2.718281828}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}2 ≈ 7.389056099}} — exactly the inverse of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/log::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}}}}}}} applied to these same three results.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer\sphinxhyphen{}typed features are upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} before exponentiating; the result is
always a floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No domain restriction: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp()}} is defined for every finite input. Very large inputs
overflow to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}} following ordinary floating\sphinxhyphen{}point behavior, rather than throwing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp()}} is the inverse of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/log::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x.log().exp()}} reconstructs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (up to
floating\sphinxhyphen{}point precision) for every positive value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::extend}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:dataframe-extend}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{extend}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{FrameMatchRule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{FrameMatchRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Unite}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fresh\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reject\PYGZus{}repeated\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Appends \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s cases beneath this frame’s cases — a vertical “stack more rows on”
operation, as opposed to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}}, which merges two frames’
\sphinxstyleemphasis{features} side by side. The two frames’ feature sets are reconciled according to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} before stacking: features unique to one side are either kept (padded with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for the side that doesn’t have them) or dropped, depending on the rule. The
resulting case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis is, by default, simply this frame’s case labels followed by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s — unless \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fresh\_cases}} asks for a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..N\sphinxhyphen{}1}} index instead.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame whose cases are appended beneath this frame’s.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FrameMatchRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Unite}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How the two frames’ \sphinxstyleemphasis{feature} sets are reconciled before stacking:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Unite}}} (default): keep this frame’s feature order, then append any
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}\sphinxhyphen{}only features after it. A feature missing from one side is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for every
row that came from that side.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Common}}}: keep only features present, by name, on both sides — a feature unique
to either frame is dropped from the result entirely.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KeepLeft}}}: keep exactly this frame’s feature set, in this frame’s order,
discarding anything \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KeepRight}}}: keep exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s feature set, in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s order, discarding
anything unique to this frame.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fresh\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (default): the output case axis is this frame’s case labels followed by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s, unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: discard both sides’ original case labels and assign a fresh, contiguous
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ..., ncases()+other.ncases()\sphinxhyphen{}1}} index instead.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{reject\_repeated\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fresh\_cases}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}), throws if the concatenated case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis
would contain any label more than once — including a label that appears twice within
one side alone, or a label shared by both sides. The exact message is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::match: repeated cases on the combined frame require RepeatedCaseRule::PairInOrder"}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s cases stacked beneath this frame’s, and features
reconciled per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extend()}} stacks rows; it never merges two frames’ features into new combined
columns the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}} does. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extend()}} when you have “more
of the same kind of row” to append, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}} when you have “more columns
about the same rows” to bring in.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reject\_repeated\_cases}} only has an effect when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fresh\_cases}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — a fresh
index can never contain a repeated label, so there’s nothing to reject in that case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A duplicate case label across (or within) the two frames is otherwise allowed by
default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reject\_repeated\_cases = false}}); set it to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} only when you need a
guaranteed\sphinxhyphen{}unique case axis on the result and would rather fail loudly than silently
produce one with repeats.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head(0)}}}}}}} is a common way to get an empty\sphinxhyphen{}but\sphinxhyphen{}typed seed frame — same
features, zero cases — to repeatedly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extend()}} inside a loop.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::combine}}}}}}}: merge two frames’ \sphinxstyleemphasis{features} together instead
of stacking their cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::head}}}}}}}: often used to build an empty, correctly\sphinxhyphen{}typed seed
frame before a loop of repeated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extend()}} calls.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::conform}}}}}}}: reshape a frame’s structure to match another’s,
when the two don’t already share a compatible feature layout.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::factor}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:dataframe-factor}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{factor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ordered}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}levels}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{CategoryEncoding}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The lower\sphinxhyphen{}level label\sphinxhyphen{}encoding primitive: converts one feature’s distinct values into
integer codes, returning both the codes \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} the level list that maps each code back
to its original value — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding\{codes, levels, ordered\}}} struct rather than
a modified frame. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ordinal}} mode is a thin convenience
wrapper around exactly this call, discarding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}} and splicing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} back into
the frame in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}} directly (instead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode(feature, EncodeMode::Ordinal)}}) whenever you need the level list too — to
label a chart axis, to build a lookup table, or to apply the same code assignment to a
second frame later.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to factor. Works on any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind — “distinct value” is determined by
the same string\sphinxhyphen{}key comparison used throughout the categorical\sphinxhyphen{}encoding surface
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify\_key\_parts}}), not restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ordered} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Carried straight through into the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding::ordered}} flag. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}
itself does not change its own behavior based on this flag — it exists so downstream
code consuming the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding}} can know whether the level order is meaningful
(an ordinal scale) or arbitrary (a plain nominal category), a distinction \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor()}}
otherwise has no way to communicate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sort\_levels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default): distinct values are ordered by first appearance in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: distinct values are sorted lexicographically before codes are assigned.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This determines which value gets code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, and so on — and, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}i{]}}}
and code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} always correspond, it also determines the order of the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}}
thread.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding}}
A plain struct with three fields: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}, one entry per case,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} itself was missing), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, the distinct
values in code order — code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} corresponds to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}i{]}}}), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ordered}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}},
the value passed in). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding}} also exposes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.decode()}} method that
reconstructs a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} of original values from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Factor a text feature with the default first\sphinxhyphen{}seen ordering, including a
missing value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Bool}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===================
     | id    city  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

1    | 2     Accra 
2    | 3     Tema

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{factored}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{factor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{factored}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{levels}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  0
1  1
2  0
3  2
4  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  Tema
1  Accra
2  Kumasi
ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}} is the first distinct value encountered, so it gets code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}} (first
seen at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}} (first seen at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}) gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}’s
missing city stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} rather than becoming a fourth, spurious level.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}0{]}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}1{]}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}2{]}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Kumasi"}} — reading
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels{[}code{]}}} for any row recovers its original city.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Sort levels lexicographically instead of by first appearance.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted\PYGZus{}factor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{factor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*sort\PYGZus{}levels=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted\PYGZus{}factor}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted\PYGZus{}factor}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{levels}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2
1  0
2  2
3  1
4  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  Accra
1  Kumasi
2  Tema
ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The level order is now alphabetical (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra, Kumasi, Tema}}), so the codes shift to
match: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}} is now \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_levels}} is the right choice when the
code assignment needs to be stable and reproducible across separately\sphinxhyphen{}built frames
that might encounter their distinct values in a different order.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/factor:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} carries no case labels or display name of its own; it prints with a plain
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}} index, the same as a fresh \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} built directly from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} value always produces a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} code — it is never assigned to an
implicit “unknown” level, and it never appears in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/encode::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode(feature, EncodeMode::Ordinal, options)}}}}}}} is equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{factor(feature, options.ordered, options.sort\_levels).codes}}, spliced back into the
frame at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s original position — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} directly when you only need
the codes back inside the frame and don’t need \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CategoryEncoding::decode()}} reverses the process: given \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{codes}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels}}, it
reconstructs a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} equal to the original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} (missing codes decode back to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::feataxis}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:dataframe-feataxis}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{feataxis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameFeatureAxisAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters a small, dedicated accessor for selecting or renaming features by \sphinxstyleemphasis{name
pattern} or by \sphinxstyleemphasis{payload kind}, rather than by an explicit list. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis()}} itself
does nothing but bind the accessor to the current frame — the actual work happens on
the accessor it returns, which exposes exactly seven methods:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like(needle, case\_sensitive = true)}}: keep features whose name contains \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{needle}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match(pattern)}}: keep features whose name matches an ECMAScript regex.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{series()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{timeline()}}: keep features of one particular \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix(text)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{suffix(text)}}: rename \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the frame by prepending
or appending \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} to its name.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This complements {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(names)}}}}}}}, which selects an explicit,
already\sphinxhyphen{}known list of names — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis()}} is for the “I don’t want to spell out every
name” case: selecting all the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"score\_"}}\sphinxhyphen{}prefixed columns, or every numeric feature,
without listing them one by one.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis()}} itself takes no parameters. See each accessor method’s own signature
above for what it accepts.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameFeatureAxisAccessor}}
A lightweight accessor bound to the current frame. Every method it exposes returns
a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} (a selected subset, or the same columns under new names); the
source frame is never mutated.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Select every feature whose name contains a substring.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.timeline()}}, which are selective.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.like()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.match()}} operate on \sphinxstylestrong{feature names}, not on the text values inside
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} columns — pattern\sphinxhyphen{}matching a column’s text contents is a job for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}}}}}}}’s own text methods instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.prefix()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.suffix()}} rename every feature on the frame unconditionally; there is
no selective “rename only these columns” mode on this accessor — for that, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis()}} deliberately does not expose a name\sphinxhyphen{}existence check or a positional
setter; use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(name).has\_value()}}}}}}} to check whether a feature exists, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} for a full positional name replacement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid regex passed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.match()}} throws with the message
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::feataxis().match: invalid regex \textquotesingle{}\textless{}pattern\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}: \textless{}reason\textgreater{}"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/features:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Three genuinely different behaviors share this one overloaded name, distinguished
entirely by how many names you pass:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No arguments} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}} returns the frame’s ordered list of feature names,
as a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\&}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{One name} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features("sales")}} extracts a \sphinxstyleemphasis{single} feature as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, with
its case labels and display name attached (so printing it shows a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Name: sales, ptype: Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}style footer, exactly like other named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
results).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Several names} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(\{"id", "sales"\})}} (or the equivalent range/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StackArray}} overloads) projects the frame down to a \sphinxstylestrong{subset} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
containing just those columns, in the order you named them, with every case
preserved.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial name lookup throws if the name doesn’t exist on the frame.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/features:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The one feature to extract as a standalone \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StackArray}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}},
multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The features to project, in the order you list them — the result’s feature order
follows this list, not the source frame’s original order.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/features:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\&}} (no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload)
The frame’s feature names, in their current order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (single\sphinxhyphen{}name overload)
The named feature, with case labels and display name attached.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} (multi\sphinxhyphen{}name overload)
A new frame containing only the named features, in the order requested, with
every case preserved.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/features:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. List every feature name.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/features:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All three overload families throw if any requested name doesn’t exist on the frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The multi\sphinxhyphen{}name overload’s result order follows the order you list names in, not the
source frame’s order — use this to reorder columns as a side effect of selecting
them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}name overload’s returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} carries the source frame’s case labels
and the feature’s own name for display; the no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload returns a plain
name list with no such attachment.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::ffill}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:dataframe-ffill}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ffill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ffill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{FillOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Forward\sphinxhyphen{}fills missing values: each null cell is replaced by the last \sphinxstyleemphasis{observed} value
above it in the same feature, propagating downward. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}} works on every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
kind PlussMic supports — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — not just
numeric features.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A leading run of nulls with no earlier observed value in the same feature is left
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — there is nothing above it to carry forward.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of consecutive nulls to fill per run, counted starting from the null
closest to the last observed value and moving away from it.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} (the default): no limit, fill every null that has an earlier observed value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A non\sphinxhyphen{}negative value: fill at most that many nulls per run; any remaining nulls
further from the anchor stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FillOptions}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structured form for targeting a feature subset:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: the feature names to fill. Empty (the default) targets every feature on
the frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}: same meaning as the simple overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with nulls forward\sphinxhyphen{}filled in the targeted
features. Untargeted features are unchanged.

\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 2}}, only the first two nulls after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} (cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}) get filled;
case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, the third null in that same run, stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} because the run already used
up its two allowed fills.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}} propagates downward feature by feature; values never cross feature
boundaries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}} is not restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
features — it works on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} columns too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A leading run of nulls with no earlier observed value in that feature stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}},
no matter the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the opposite direction (propagating the next observed value backward), see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}}}}}}}. For numeric linear interpolation between two observed
neighbors, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a copy of the frame with missing values replaced by a fill value, and is the
main non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating entry point in the missing\sphinxhyphen{}data cleanup path — typically applied right
before a summary (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}), a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, or an export (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel}}), all of which either skip nulls silently or fail outright depending on the
destination format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The overload set exists because “the right fill value” depends on the column’s dtype:
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} fills numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} columns, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string\_view}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} fills \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
columns, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} fills the matching temporal column type. Passing
a scalar fills \sphinxstylestrong{every feature whose dtype matches that scalar’s type}, unless you
narrow the target with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} overload. When different columns need different
fill values or you want to mix dtypes in a single call, use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FillSpec}} overload
instead of chaining several single\sphinxhyphen{}value calls.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating — it returns a new frame and leaves the original untouched.
For an in\sphinxhyphen{}place variant, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}}}}}}} (note the trailing
underscore, the project\sphinxhyphen{}wide convention for mutating siblings of a non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating method).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Timeline\&}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::TimeIndex\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement value. Its type determines which columns are eligible: a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} only
ever fills numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features, a string only fills \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features, and so on.
Columns whose dtype does not match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}’s type are left completely unchanged, nulls
included — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(0.0)}} will never touch a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} column, even one that has missing
entries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricts the fill to an explicit subset of feature names. Omit this parameter (the
single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads) to apply the fill to every eligible feature on the frame.
Passing a feature name whose dtype does not match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}’s type is not an error — that
feature is simply left unaffected, same as if it had been excluded.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}FillSpec\textgreater{}}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}FillSpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A collection of per\sphinxhyphen{}feature fill instructions, each pairing a feature name with its own
fill value. Use this overload when different columns need different replacement values
in one call, for example filling a numeric column with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} while filling a sibling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} column with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Unknown"}} in the same expression.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested nulls replaced. Feature order, names, and dtypes are
unchanged; only cell values move from null to the supplied fill value.
