\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:dataframe-info-string}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{info\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DisplayOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Exactly {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}}}}}}’s two\sphinxhyphen{}part health\sphinxhyphen{}check report — the summary block plus
the feature inventory — returned as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}} instead of printed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stdout}}.
Both functions compute the identical content via the same underlying renderer; the
only difference is where the text ends up.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info\_string()}} when the report itself is the thing you need to work with
programmatically: embedding it in a log message, attaching it to a test failure,
writing it into a file alongside other diagnostics, or comparing it against an
expected string in a test.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const display::DisplayOptions\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same rendering options \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} accepts — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}}}}}}’s Parameters for
the full breakdown (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{terminal\_width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{terminal\_height}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}, and so on).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}
The rendered report, identical in content to what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} prints. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info\_string()}}
itself does \sphinxstylestrong{not} append a trailing newline; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} adds exactly one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}n\textquotesingle{}}}
after the same text when it prints. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} df.info\_string() \textless{}\textless{} \textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}n\textquotesingle{};}}
reproduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}’s exact terminal output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Append the report into a larger diagnostic message.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{diagnostic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Frame check failed for \PYGZsq{}orders\PYGZsq{}:}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{info\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info\_string()}} returns a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, it composes naturally with
ordinary string concatenation — useful for building a single diagnostic message that
combines the report with your own context, rather than printing the report and your
own message as two separate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} calls.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/info_string:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info\_string()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} are backed by the exact same renderer
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display::render\_info}}); there is no drift between what one prints and what the
other returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The only textual difference from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}’s printed output is the trailing newline:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} always appends one after the report, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info\_string()}} never does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}}}}}}’s own Notes for the meaning of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Null Case Rows}}, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Memory}}
estimate, and how the inventory table truncates on very wide frames — all of that
applies identically here.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::insert}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:dataframe-insert}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{insert}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}index}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{name}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adds one new feature at an explicit column position, shifting every feature already at
or past that position one slot to the right, and returns the resulting frame.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/place::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{place()}}}}}}} builds on this directly — it computes a position relative to an
existing “anchor” feature and calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert()}} internally when the target name doesn’t
already exist.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_index} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The zero\sphinxhyphen{}based position the new feature should occupy. Clamped into the valid range
automatically: a value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= 0}} prepends the feature as the new first column, and a value
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= nfeatures()}} appends it as the new last column — there is no bounds error for an
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range index, only clamping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new feature’s name. Must not be empty, and must not already exist on the frame —
both throw (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::insert: feature name cannot be empty"}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::insert: duplicate feature name \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} respectively). Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:set_features.md}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{myst}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_features()}}}}}}} instead when you want to \sphinxstyleemphasis{replace} an existing
feature’s values rather than add a new one.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new feature’s values. Must be defined, and — unless the frame currently has zero
features — must have exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} entries; throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::insert: case count mismatch"}} otherwise.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} inserted at the (clamped) requested position, every other
feature’s relative order preserved, and the same case axis as the source.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_index}} is silently clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, nfeatures(){]}}}; it is
never a validation error on its own.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} colliding with an existing feature \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} a validation error — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert()}} never
overwrites an existing column; use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert:set_features.md}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{myst}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_features()}}}}}}} for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_value}}’s length must match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} unless the frame currently has no
features at all (in which case the new feature also defines the frame’s case count
going forward).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fills numeric gaps by linear interpolation between the nearest observed value on each
side. For a null between two observed values, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}} computes a straight\sphinxhyphen{}line
value between them weighted by position — the middle of a two\sphinxhyphen{}cell gap gets exactly
the midpoint, a cell one\sphinxhyphen{}third of the way across the gap gets one third of the way
between the two neighbors, and so on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}} only ever operates
on numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features — passing a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature name explicitly throws.
A leading or trailing run of nulls with no observed value on \sphinxstyleemphasis{both} sides is left
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, because there is no second endpoint to interpolate toward.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature subset to interpolate. Leave empty (the default) to target every numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature on the frame automatically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of consecutive nulls to fill per gap, counted from the left edge of the
gap.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} (the default): no limit, fill every interior null that has observed values on
both sides.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A non\sphinxhyphen{}negative value: fill at most that many nulls per gap; any remaining nulls
further into the gap stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FillOptions}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structured form combining \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} in one object; equivalent to the
simple overload.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with interpolated values in the targeted
numeric features. Untargeted and non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}} only interpolates numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features. Passing a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
feature name in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A gap needs an observed value on \sphinxstyleemphasis{both} sides to be filled at all — leading and
trailing runs of nulls are always left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For copying a neighboring observation instead of computing a linear midpoint, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ffill}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::bfill}}}}}}}: propagate an

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/invalid:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A same\sphinxhyphen{}shape boolean mask, like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}, but broader for numeric

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/invalid:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

the “non\sphinxhyphen{}finite” extension only applies to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} data, since concepts like

\item {}

A masked\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} cell is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}} too, whatever its

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} whenever upstream numeric computation (division,
logarithms, and similar) could have produced \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infinity}} without an explicit
validity mask ever being attached.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a same\sphinxhyphen{}shape frame of booleans marking exactly which cells are missing: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
where the source cell is null, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where a value was observed. This is the
elementwise inspection primitive behind most of the missing\sphinxhyphen{}data workflow —
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}’s null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping
all answer questions that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} lets you answer explicitly and visually first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Leave \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} empty (the default) to check every feature on the frame; pass an
explicit subset when only certain columns matter for a downstream decision (a join key,
say, where nulls elsewhere on the frame are expected and irrelevant).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to check for missingness. Leave empty to check every feature on the frame;
pass a subset to restrict the resulting mask to just those columns.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A frame with the same case axis as the source and one boolean feature per checked
column, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} wherever that cell was null in the source.

Only two cells in the entire mask are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} at

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Restrict the check to one feature you specifically care about.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{price\PYGZus{}mask}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{price\_mask}} is a one\sphinxhyphen{}column frame — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s missingness, ignoring whether
anything else on the frame is null. This is the shape to reach for when you are about to
make a decision based on one specific column (skip a row in a loop, guard a downstream
calculation) and do not want to accidentally react to nulls elsewhere on the frame.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} never mutates the frame or changes which cells are null; it is a pure
read\sphinxhyphen{}only inspection.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine the result with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/any::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any(Axis::Case)}}}}}}} to collapse the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell mask down
to one boolean per row (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.isnull().any(pluss::table::Axis::Case)}}), which is
exactly how {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}}}}}} computes its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Null Case Rows}} count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}} are exact complements of each other,
cell\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}cell.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::join}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:dataframe-join}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{join}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{collision\PYGZus{}suffix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZus{}right}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Attaches every feature from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} onto a copy of the current frame, case\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}case, and
returns the combined frame. The two frames are aligned by their \sphinxstylestrong{case axis position}
— case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} is paired with case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of the current frame — not by matching the
values of a shared key column.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the most important thing to know before reaching for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}}: it is a
\sphinxstylestrong{positional} attach, appropriate for two frames that already line up case\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}case —
conceptually a horizontal concatenation of features, not a relational join. If you need
to combine two frames by matching values in a key column (an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{customer\_id}},
and so on) rather than by position, look at {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql()}}}}}}} /
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql()}}}}}}} for a key\sphinxhyphen{}based join expressed as SQL, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} itself
performs no key matching or row reordering at all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both frames must have a compatible number of cases for the result to make sense — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}}
does not reindex, sort, or fill in gaps between mismatched case axes.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame whose features are attached to the current frame. Every feature on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} is
appended, in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s existing feature order, after the current frame’s own features.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{collision\_suffix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_right"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Suffix appended to a feature name coming from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} when that name already exists on
the current frame. Only the colliding feature from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} is renamed; the current
frame’s original feature keeps its unsuffixed name. Pass a different suffix (for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_2"}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_new"}}) when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_right"}} would itself collide with an existing feature name,
or when it does not read well for your domain (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_prior\_year"}} for a year\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}year
join, for instance).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the current frame’s features first, followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s features
in order, with any name collisions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} renamed using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_suffix}}. The
case axis of the result matches the current frame’s case axis.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{logistics}} has no explicit relationship to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} beyond having the same number of

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} (“Accra”) purely because they occupy the same position. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{logistics}} had been
built or filtered independently and its rows were not already in the same order as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}, the join would silently pair the wrong rows together; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} has no way to
detect that for you.

frame you are attaching.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating: the current frame and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} are both left untouched, and a
new frame is returned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because alignment is positional, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} is cheap — it does not need to hash or sort
either frame’s case axis the way a key\sphinxhyphen{}based merge would.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you need to combine frames that are \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} already in matching case order — the
common “match customers across two tables by ID” scenario — build the relationship
explicitly first (for example by sorting or re\sphinxhyphen{}indexing both frames onto the same key
order, or using {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}}}}}}} for an actual key\sphinxhyphen{}based join) rather than calling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} directly on mismatched frames.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} does not deduplicate or validate that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} has the same number of cases as
the current frame; mismatched case counts are a programming error to avoid upstream,
not something \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} corrects for you.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/join:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::prep\_sql}}}}}}}: key\sphinxhyphen{}based joins
expressed as SQL, when rows need to be matched by value rather than by position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::assign}}}}}}}: add one or a few computed features instead of
attaching an entire second frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::conform}}}}}}}: align a frame’s case axis to another frame’s case
axis, which is often the right step to take \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} a positional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::kindelize}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:dataframe-kindelize}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Catalog}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{KindelizePolicy}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{policy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Catalog}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} into a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::kindle::Catalog}} — a keyed collection of
independent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}s, one per feature, rather than a single aligned table. This is
the bridge into the Kindle module’s stream\sphinxhyphen{}oriented API, useful when downstream code
wants to work with each feature as its own named, independently\sphinxhyphen{}sliceable stream
instead of as columns of one shared frame. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tabelize()}}}}}}} is the reverse
direction: it takes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} and rebuilds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} from it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, every feature on the frame becomes one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} entry, keyed by its
existing feature name, and each resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}} carries the frame’s case labels
along with it (so per\sphinxhyphen{}stream operations later can still refer back to which case each
value belonged to).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{policy} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::kindle::KindelizePolicy\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how the conversion is done. Omitting it entirely is equivalent to passing a
default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KindelizePolicy}}. Its fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{attach\_labels}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}} carries the
frame’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread alongside its values. Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} to build plain,
label\sphinxhyphen{}less streams instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{also} added as its own additional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} entry (keyed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_key}}), rather
than only being attached to each feature’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_key}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_label"}}): the key used for the
materialized label entry when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Catalog::kindelize: label key collides with existing feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}label\_key\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} if a
feature already uses that exact name.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::kindle::Catalog}}
A catalog with one entry per feature (keyed by feature name, in the frame’s
feature order), plus one extra \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_key}}\sphinxhyphen{}keyed entry when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{policy.materialize\_label}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{key}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{: }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{at}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{key}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ cases}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:id1}}

3
id: 3 cases
city: 3 cases
sales: 3 cases
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each of the three features becomes its own catalog entry, keyed by its original
feature name, and each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}} carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}’s three cases with it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Materialize the case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread as its own catalog entry.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{KindelizePolicy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{policy}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{policy}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{materialize\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kindelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{policy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nkeys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{has}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
4
true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label = true}}, a fourth entry appears — keyed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_label"}} by default
— holding the case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o1, o2, o3}}) as a stream in its own right, in
addition to it already being attached to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}’s individual
streams.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindelize()}} requires a defined frame; calling it on a default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::kindelize requires a defined DataFrame"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reverse conversion is {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tabelize(catalog, policy)}}}}}}} — a
static method that rebuilds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label}}’s label key collides\sphinxhyphen{}with\sphinxhyphen{}an\sphinxhyphen{}existing\sphinxhyphen{}feature check only runs
when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}; leaving it at the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} never performs
this check, since no extra entry is added.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::kurtosis}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:dataframe-kurtosis}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its (bias\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted) sample \sphinxstylestrong{excess} kurtosis — a
measure of how heavy a distribution’s tails are relative to a normal distribution —
returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names,
the same shape {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}}}}}}} returns. Because this is \sphinxstyleemphasis{excess} kurtosis (not raw
kurtosis), a normal distribution scores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}: a positive value describes heavier tails
and a sharper peak than normal, a negative value describes lighter tails and a flatter
peak. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are skipped entirely.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}}, nulls are always excluded from the moment computation — there is no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} parameter — and there is a hard statistical floor instead: a feature needs
at least \sphinxstylestrong{four} observed values before excess kurtosis is even defined (the fourth
moment’s bias correction divides by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(n \sphinxhyphen{} 2)(n \sphinxhyphen{} 3)}}, which is undefined below that).
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} can raise that floor further but never lower it below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one kurtosis value per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s
features instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations a feature must have before it is assigned
a real kurtosis value at all. Passing a value below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} has no effect — the method
always enforces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(4, min\_count)}} — but passing a larger value raises the bar.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s sample excess kurtosis.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the excess kurtosis of every numeric feature, the default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  \PYGZhy{}1.2
     units  \PYGZhy{}0.8591715976
unit\PYGZus{}price  \PYGZhy{}3.146074484
  discount  \PYGZhy{}1.988919668
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature here has negative excess kurtosis — flatter, thinner\sphinxhyphen{}tailed than normal
— which is typical of small, evenly\sphinxhyphen{}spread samples like these. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}’s six evenly
spaced values give it the most negative (most “platykurtic”) result of the four.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}}’s values are computed over their five observed values
only; the missing case in each (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}, case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}}) is
excluded from the moment computation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} above the statistical floor to require every case be
present.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  \PYGZhy{}1.2
     units  \PYGZhy{}0.8591715976
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} have all six values observed, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 6}} doesn’t change
their result. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} each have only five observed values, one
short of six, so both report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. See the hard floor in effect: a three\sphinxhyphen{}case frame can never produce a
kurtosis, no matter what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} is passed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt\PYGZus{}too\PYGZus{}small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{kurt\PYGZus{}too\PYGZus{}small}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  NULL
     units  NULL
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature has at most three observed values in this three\sphinxhyphen{}case slice, below the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(4, min\_count)}} floor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kurtosis()}} always enforces, so every feature comes back
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kurtosis()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither computed as an
error nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature whose values have zero variance reports a kurtosis of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} rather
than an undefined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0/0}}, the same zero\sphinxhyphen{}variance short\sphinxhyphen{}circuit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}} applies.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is \sphinxstylestrong{excess} kurtosis (normal distribution scores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}), not raw kurtosis
(normal distribution scores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}) — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}3.0}} term baked into the formula is what
makes it “excess.”

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::skew}}}}}}}: the asymmetry counterpart to this measure of tail
weight, sharing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} shape (with a floor of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} instead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::std}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::var}}}}}}}: the second\sphinxhyphen{}moment statistics
this method’s fourth moment builds on.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/label:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/label:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters a dedicated accessor for everything to do with the \sphinxstylestrong{case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis} — the
per\sphinxhyphen{}row index every frame carries alongside its features. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label()}} itself does
nothing but bind the accessor to the current frame; the accessor exposes around
thirty methods covering inspection (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.values()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.names()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.part()}}), promoting a
feature into the label axis and back (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.reset()}}), reordering
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sort()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.align()}}), set\sphinxhyphen{}style operations between two label threads (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.unite()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.intersect()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.diff()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.symdiff()}}), positional lookup (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.find()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.pos()}}), and
distinct/duplicate inspection (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.distinct()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.duplicated()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.repeated()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.freq()}}) — the label\sphinxhyphen{}axis counterparts of the same\sphinxhyphen{}named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} methods, but
operating on row labels instead of feature values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page previews the accessor’s most common entry points. Each accessor method gets
its own dedicated reference page under the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameLabelAccessor}} API reference.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/label:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label()}} itself takes no parameters. See each accessor method’s own signature for
what it accepts.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/label:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameLabelAccessor}}
A lightweight accessor bound to the current frame. Methods that inspect labels
return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}; methods that transform
the label axis or the frame return a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. The source frame is never
mutated.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/label:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label()}} is the dedicated surface for row\sphinxhyphen{}label operations, kept separate from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}} and the feature\sphinxhyphen{}axis surface (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis()}}), which operate on column
names instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set(feature, true)}} promotes a feature into the label axis and drops it from the
columns; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set(feature, false)}} (the default) keeps the source feature as an
ordinary column alongside the new label axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.reset(name)}} is the inverse of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set()}}: it materializes the current label axis
back into an ordinary feature under the given name.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{land}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{land}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise logical AND between every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed feature on this frame and the
matching value on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} is one of three logical methods
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}}) — each with a reflected counterpart
({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}}}}}}}) — that operate strictly
on boolean payloads, unlike the arithmetic and comparison families.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both operands must already be Bool Series
Every logical method requires each participating feature to be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} with a genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} scalar type. A numeric 0/1 column (even \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int64}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}}) is rejected — cast it first with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(..., pluss::ScalarType::Bool)}}}}}}} if it isn’t already boolean.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Much simpler overload shape than add()/eq()
Unlike the arithmetic family ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}) or the comparison family
({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}), the logical methods take no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} — there
are exactly two overloads: another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, or a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. See “Parameters”
below for what each one requires.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, in one of two shapes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}: another frame with the \sphinxstylestrong{exact same feature names, in the same
order}, and the \sphinxstylestrong{same number of cases}. Values are combined position\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}position
— there is no case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment step; only the feature\sphinxhyphen{}name list and the case
\sphinxstyleemphasis{count} are checked, not the case label values themselves.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}: a single boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose length matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}}. The
\sphinxstyleemphasis{same} thread is combined against \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature identically, position\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}position
— there is no per\sphinxhyphen{}feature broadcast the way the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overloads of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} support via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every feature holding the logical AND
of the source cell and the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} value.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. AND two boolean frames with identical feature names, case\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}case.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every cell is combined by position, not by case label: position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} (case
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}) is ANDed with position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}), and so on, even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p,q,r}} vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x,y,z}}) don’t overlap at all. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}
each have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} cases and the same two feature names (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}}) in the same order, which
is all \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land(DataFrame)}} requires — it never checks whether the case labels
themselves match.

The same three\sphinxhyphen{}value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask}} is combined against \sphinxstylestrong{both} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} at matching

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/land:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires a genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} scalar type on every participating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; a numeric
0/1 column throws rather than being treated as truthy.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land(const DataFrame\&)}} checks only that feature names match (in order) and that
case \sphinxstyleemphasis{counts} match — it does not verify or use the case label \sphinxstyleemphasis{values} for
alignment, unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}\sphinxhyphen{}based alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} computes the same cell values (AND is
commutative) and, since a fix to an earlier revision, the same case labels and title
too — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} are now fully interchangeable. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}}
for a worked comparison and a note on the earlier behavior this replaced.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering relation “less than or equal to”, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the
same shape as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} shares the same scalar/string/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
operand shapes as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}’s “What It Does” for the full
explanation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
le() has no independent implementation
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} overload is a thin wrapper: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.le(other, ...)}} always calls straight
through to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt(other, ..., /* strict = */ false)}}}}}}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}}
parameter on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} itself — if you need the strict “less than” relation on the same
call site, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}} directly instead.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for
the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell is less than or equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared
against a missing value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. “Less than or equal to” against a scalar threshold.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reshapes a wide frame into long form: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features}} are repeated (tiled) once per
value feature, and every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} is stacked into two new columns — one
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}}) recording which source feature each row came from, and one
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}}) holding the actual stacked values. This is the “melt” / “pivot longer”
direction of reshaping; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}}
build wide frames back out of long ones.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{id\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Features to keep as identifiers, repeated unchanged for every value feature’s block.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Features to stack together into one output value column. Leave empty (the default) to
use every feature not already listed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features}}. All selected value features
must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind — and, for numeric features, the same scalar dtype
and platform — since they end up concatenated into one homogeneous output column.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"feature"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output column name recording which source value feature each row came from.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output column name holding the actual stacked values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fresh\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): the output gets a fresh, contiguous \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}} case index.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the original case labels are repeated once per value\sphinxhyphen{}feature block, so a
case label can appear more than once in the output.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features.size() + 2}} columns and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases() * value\_features.size()}} rows (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases() * (nfeatures() \sphinxhyphen{}     id\_features.size())}} rows when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_features}} is left empty).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected value feature must share one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind (and, for numeric data,
the same scalar dtype and platform); mixing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} value feature with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
one in the same call is not supported, since they must concatenate into a single
homogeneous output column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any validity (null) mask on a stacked value feature is concatenated along with the
values, so missing cells in the source stay missing in the output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fresh\_cases = false}} deliberately produces a case axis with repeated labels (one
repeat per value\sphinxhyphen{}feature block) — pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default) unless you specifically
need to trace each output row back to its original case label.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A single, format\sphinxhyphen{}switched entry point that dispatches to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}} based on a
runtime string, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}}. Useful when the file format isn’t known until runtime
(config\sphinxhyphen{}driven pipelines, a generic “import this file” code path) — otherwise, calling
the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific loader directly is clearer and avoids the string\sphinxhyphen{}matching layer
entirely.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not every overload supports every format
Only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}}\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads dispatch across \sphinxstylestrong{all five} formats.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} overload and the positional (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines}}) overload only recognize \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} — passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} to either of those two
overloads throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“unsupported source type”}, even though the same string works fine
with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads. This is a real asymmetry in the overload set, not
an oversight in this documentation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{source\_type} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format selector, matched case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively. Recognized values:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} (the last three
only via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}} overloads — see the caution above). Anything else
throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“unsupported source type”}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle. Works with all five recognized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}}
values — each format’s own loader (for example {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overload) interprets the same key/value entries its dedicated loader would.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::ReadCsvOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A typed CSV\sphinxhyphen{}parsing options struct, for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} source types only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sep}, \sphinxstylestrong{ncases}, \sphinxstylestrong{usefeats}, \sphinxstylestrong{case\_col}, \sphinxstylestrong{on\_bad\_lines}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as the equivalent {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} positional parameters, for
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} source types only.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame, exactly as if you had called the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific loader
directly with equivalent settings.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}} never invents its own parsing or type\sphinxhyphen{}inference logic — it is purely a
string\sphinxhyphen{}keyed dispatch to the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific static loaders. Reading the dispatched
method’s own documentation ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}},
and so on) tells you exactly what a given call will do.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} and positional overloads are CSV/TXT\sphinxhyphen{}only; use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}
overload if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}} might resolve to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}}
at runtime.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}} can never return a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}} — even with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type = "excel"}}, it always calls the single\sphinxhyphen{}frame {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}}
overload. For multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet loading, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}} directly with its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_names}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_indices}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} overloads.

\end{itemize}
