\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  103.5
     units  2.833333333
unit\PYGZus{}price  551.5
  discount  0.08
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s mean (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{551.5}}) divides by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} — its one missing observation
(case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is excluded from both the running sum and the count used to divide it, the
same null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping rule {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} applies to its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}} row. These
are in fact the exact same numbers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} reports for this frame; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}} gives
you just that one statistic without computing the other seven.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. See a missing value poison the mean when null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping is disabled.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{averages\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{averages\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  103.5
     units  2.833333333
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, any feature that has even one missing value averages to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
rather than silently averaging over a smaller sample — useful when a missing value
should be a hard stop rather than something quietly absorbed into “however many values
happened to be observed.”


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}’s result is labeled by feature name, and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
(an index column plus a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype:}} footer), not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither averaged as an error
nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you need several statistics at once (mean, spread, quartiles), reach for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} instead of calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}} separately.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean_by:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Groups rows by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} and computes the mean of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} within each
group, returning a compact three\sphinxhyphen{}column summary (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mean\_" + value\_feature}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}) sorted by mean descending, ties broken
alphabetically by group key. This is a focused convenience for the single most common
group\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}summarize question — “what’s the average X per Y” — without building a full
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}}}}}}} pipeline for it. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_by()}}}}}}} is the
sibling convenience for counting rows per group instead of averaging a value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean_by:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{group\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature whose distinct values define the groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The numeric feature averaged within each group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} groups with the highest mean, after sorting. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the default)
keeps every group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A group needs at least this many observations of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} to appear in the
result at all; groups with fewer observations are dropped entirely, not shown with a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} mean.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull\_group} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether a missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} value forms its own group (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) or is excluded
entirely (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the default).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean_by:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A frame with one row per surviving group, columns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mean\_" + value\_feature}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}, sorted by mean descending (ties broken
alphabetically by group key ascending).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean_by:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The output column is always named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mean\_" + value\_feature}} (for example,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean\_amount}}), never just the plain feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting is always mean descending, ties broken alphabetically by group key
ascending — the same tie\sphinxhyphen{}break convention used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A group excluded by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} is dropped entirely, not shown with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} mean —
there is no way to distinguish “excluded by min\_count” from “never existed” in the
output alone.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::median}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:dataframe-median}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{median}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its median, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose entries line
up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} return. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are skipped entirely rather than coerced
into a statistic that wouldn’t mean anything.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}, the median is not pulled toward an unusually large or small value in the
data — it is the middle observation once the feature’s values are sorted (or the average
of the two middle observations, for a feature with an even number of observed values).
That makes it a useful cross\sphinxhyphen{}check against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}} on a feature you suspect has extreme
values on one side, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} in the example below.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one median per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s features
instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that feature’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded before sorting, so the median is
computed only from the observed values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value in a feature poisons that feature’s result, which comes
back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s median.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the median of every numeric feature, skipping missing values (the
default).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  103.5
     units  2.5
unit\PYGZus{}price  320
  discount  0.08
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s median (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{320}}) sits much closer to the bulk of its values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{45.5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{42.0}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{320.0}}) than its mean of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{551.5}} (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}’s Example 1) does — the two
large values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1200.0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1150.0}} pull the mean upward but only shift the median by one
sorted position. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} has an even count of observed values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}), so its median
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.5}}) is the average of the two middle sorted values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}), not one of the
original observations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{middles\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{median}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{middles\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  103.5
     units  2.5
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} — the two features with a missing
value — come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely rather than a median computed from a reduced set of
observations. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, with no missing values, are unaffected either way.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither sorted as an error
nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a feature with an even number of observed values, the median is the arithmetic
average of the two central sorted values — it will not necessarily equal any actual
observation in the data, the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}’ median of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.5}} does not appear in its
source values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{2, 5, 1, 3, 4, 2\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}} is a special case of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}}}}}}} at the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} point;
reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}} directly when you also need the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}} quartiles in the
same call.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/median:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mean}}}}}}}: the corresponding average, more sensitive to extreme
values than the median.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::percentiles}}}}}}}: the median generalized to any quantile, not
just the midpoint.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe}}}}}}}: reports the median as its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}} row alongside
several other statistics in one call.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::min}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:dataframe-min}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its smallest observed value, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
whose entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/max::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} return. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
features are skipped entirely rather than compared as an error.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one minimum per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s features
instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that feature’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded from the comparison entirely, so the
minimum is whatever was actually observed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value in a feature poisons that feature’s result, which comes
back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s smallest observed value.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Find the minimum of every numeric feature, skipping missing values (the
default).

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smallest}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smallest}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

     units  1
unit\PYGZus{}price  42
  discount  0.05
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s missing observation (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is simply excluded from the comparison —
its minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{42}} is the smallest of the five values that were actually observed, not a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smallest\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{smallest\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  101
     units  1
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely rather
than the minimum of their remaining observed values. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, with no
missing values, are unaffected either way.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/min:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}},
not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; text and time features are not
compared as an error, they are simply absent from the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}} reports the smallest \sphinxstyleemphasis{value}, not the case it came from — pair it with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}}}}}}} or a boolean mask built from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} if you also need the row that produced it.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise remainder (modulo). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}} shares the exact same
overload shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the arithmetic
family — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the scalar/frame/
Thread operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}} is the natural
companion to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}: together they satisfy
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x == y * x.floordiv(y) + x.mod(y)}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand (the divisor): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}
(aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
remainder after dividing by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}} are complementary: the floor\sphinxhyphen{}divided
quotient times the divisor, plus the remainder from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}}, reconstructs the
original value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its full overload shape, alignment semantics, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} behavior with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:dataframe-mode}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drop\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finds the most frequently occurring value in every compatible feature and returns a
new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}}}}}}}, this
method’s result is naturally a small table rather than one value per feature, because
a feature can have \sphinxstylestrong{more than one} mode when several values are tied for most
frequent.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature, plus every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
feature, participates — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode()}} is not restricted to numbers the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}} are, since “most common value” is meaningful for categories and timestamps
too. The result has one row per rank position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode\_1}}, …) up to however
many\sphinxhyphen{}way the widest tie in the frame is; features with fewer tied modes than that are
padded with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in their remaining rows.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{drop\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls whether a missing value can itself become “the mode”:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values never participate. Only observed values are
candidates, and a feature made entirely of missing values is a validation error
(there is no value to report).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: missing values are counted like any other value would be. If missing cells
outnumber every individual observed value in a feature, that feature’s mode becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — “the most common thing in this column is that it’s empty.”

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one row per rank position (labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode\_1}}, …) and one
column per participating feature, holding that feature’s mode(s). Features with
fewer modes than the widest tie in the result are padded with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{common}\PYG{p}{;}

the result’s row count is set by the \sphinxstyleemphasis{widest} tie in the frame, not by each feature
individually.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = true}}, only the two observed values are candidates —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"paid"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"shipped"}} each occur once, so both are reported as a tie. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = false}}, the four missing cells outnumber either observed value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} vs
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}), so the mode becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the most common thing in this column really is that
it’s empty.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode()}}’s result is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}}, because
the result can have more than one row per call when ties occur.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature type participates: numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — this is not restricted to numeric features the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}} are.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ties are reported in ascending sorted order (numerically for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, lexically for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}), never in original column order or insertion order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with no observed values at all (every cell missing, or a numeric feature
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = true}} and only missing cells) is a validation error.

\end{itemize}

has, without identifying which one is most common.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise multiplication. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}} shares the exact same
overload shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the
arithmetic family — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the
scalar/frame/Thread operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A common use is rescaling a feature (unit conversion, currency conversion, applying a
tax or discount rate) without hand\sphinxhyphen{}writing a loop over cells.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, multiplied against the current frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast
scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast
per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature multiplied by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the number of cases (rows) in the frame. This is the same count that appears
as the first number in a printed frame’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}N cs x M feat{]}}} footer, and the length
every case\sphinxhyphen{}aligned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} argument (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} side of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}, and similar methods) is checked against.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
The number of cases in the frame.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{final}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{84.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{88.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{72.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{s1}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{s2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{s3}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:output}}

3
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This matches the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}}’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}3 cs x 2 feat{]}}} footer when printed.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} counts rows, not distinct case labels — a frame is not required to have
unique case labels, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} can exceed the number of \sphinxstyleemphasis{distinct} labels
reported by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct()}}}}}}} on the case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} in the frame has exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} elements; this is an
invariant the frame maintains internally.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::nfeatures}}}}}}}: the companion count for columns instead of

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::ndistinct}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:dataframe-ndistinct}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ndistinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts each selected feature’s own distinct\sphinxhyphen{}value count independently, returning one
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} entry per feature, labeled by feature name. This is a per\sphinxhyphen{}feature count, not a
cross\sphinxhyphen{}feature distinct\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{combination} count — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct(\{"city", "product"\})}} reports
how many distinct cities and how many distinct products there are, each on its own,
never how many distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(city, product)}} pairs exist. For that, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}, which do build a composite key
across several features together.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features to count. Leave empty (the default) to count every feature on the
frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether a missing value counts as its own distinct “value” (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) or is excluded
from the distinct count entirely (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the default).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} entry per selected feature, labeled by feature name, named
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ndistinct"}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Count distinct values per feature on a small frame.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:output}}

     | id    city  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

1    | 2     Tema  
2    | 3     Accra 
3    | 4     Kumasi
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{counts}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ndistinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{counts}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  id  4
city  3
Name: ndistinct, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} distinct values (every row is unique); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} distinct values
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}} repeats, but that doesn’t add a fourth distinct
value). These are two independent, per\sphinxhyphen{}feature counts — not a count of distinct
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(id, city)}} combinations.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a per\sphinxhyphen{}feature count computed independently for each selected feature; it
never builds a composite cross\sphinxhyphen{}feature key the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}} do.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}}, a missing value counts as one additional distinct “value”
for that feature, rather than being excluded from the count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected feature name must exist on the frame; an unknown name throws.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::freq}}}}}}}: counts occurrences per distinct value (or
combination), rather than just the number of distinct values.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::nfeatures}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ncases}}}}}}}: the plain

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The negated counterpart of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}: elementwise “not equal”, returning a
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the same shape as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}} shares the exact same
overload shape as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}} — a scalar, a string, another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
broadcast by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the
operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (numeric scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (text value,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell differs from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared against a
missing value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ne:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne()}} is the logical negation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}, cell for cell, with the one
exception of missing\sphinxhyphen{}value cells, which stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} under both rather than flipping
to the opposite boolean.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its full overload shape and alignment semantics with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the number of features (columns) in the frame. This is the second number in a
printed frame’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}N cs x M feat{]}}} footer, and the length every feature\sphinxhyphen{}aligned
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} argument (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} side of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}, and
similar methods) is checked against.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
The number of features in the frame.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/nfeatures:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} always equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features().size()}} — the two are kept in sync by
construction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

the frame maintains internally.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::note}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:dataframe-note}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the dedicated text\sphinxhyphen{}operations accessor for the current frame — string
stripping, casing, length, pattern matching, splitting, padding, and more, one method
per operation. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}} itself does no work beyond validating the frame and
constructing the accessor: \sphinxstylestrong{every feature currently on the frame must already be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}, or it throws immediately. In practice this means selecting the text
feature(s) you want to operate on first, then calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note()}}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"city"\}).note().lower()}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.note()}} directly on a frame that
still has numeric or other non\sphinxhyphen{}text columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page previews the accessor’s most common entry points. Each accessor method gets
its own dedicated reference page under the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor}} API reference.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}} itself takes no parameters. See each accessor method’s own signature for what
it accepts.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor}}
A lightweight accessor bound to the current (all\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}) frame. Nearly every
method on it returns a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} with the text operation applied; the
source frame is never mutated.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Lowercase a text feature — after selecting it first.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/note:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature on the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note()}} is called on must already be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind;
select the text feature(s) first with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/feataxis::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feataxis().note()}}}}}}} if the source frame has other kinds mixed in.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The accessor’s methods each apply to every feature on the (already\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}only)
frame, returning a new frame with the transformation applied — some methods (like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.length()}}) change the resulting kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}} on a frame with no features at all, or a frame containing a non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
feature, throws before constructing the accessor.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::notnull}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:dataframe-notnull}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{notnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a same\sphinxhyphen{}shape frame of booleans marking exactly which cells were \sphinxstylestrong{observed}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the source cell has a value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it is null — the exact
complement of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}, cell for cell. It exists as its own named method
rather than forcing every caller to write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!isnull()}}\sphinxhyphen{}style negation, because “which
cells are usable” reads more directly than “which cells are not missing” at most call
sites (building a mask to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} on, for instance).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to check. Leave empty to check every feature on the frame; pass a subset
to restrict the resulting mask to just those columns.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A frame with the same case axis as the source and one boolean feature per checked
column, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} wherever that cell held an observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}null) value in the source.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Build a mask of which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} values are usable.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{price\PYGZus{}observed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{notnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{price\PYGZus{}observed}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=================
     | unit\PYGZus{}price
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

[6 cs x 1 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is the one missing value in this column.
A common next step is feeding this straight into {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.filter(orders.notnull(\{"unit\_price"\}).features("unit\_price"))}} keeps only the
rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is usable, without needing a separate comparison against a
sentinel value.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} are exact complements: for any cell,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} exactly where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Some codebases spell this \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notna()}}; in PlussMic, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}} is the name, and it does
not have a separate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notna()}} alias — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}} consistently.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}, this is a pure inspection method; it never mutates the frame or
changes any values.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::isnull}}}}}}}: the inverted mask (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where missing).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::dropnull}}}}}}}: drop rows based on a missingness rule directly,
without building the mask yourself first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::filter}}}}}}}: use a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} mask to select rows.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:dataframe-observe}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{observe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{observe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stop}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Previews a positional window of rows — either a single row, or a contiguous
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} range — without materializing a separate named helper call for each
shape. Internally, the single\sphinxhyphen{}row overload just calls the range overload with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(row, row + 1)}}, and the range overload is a thin wrapper around
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} that tags the resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} with the display
name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"observe"}}. It exists alongside {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}}
for the case those two don’t cover: peeking at rows from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{middle} of a frame by
position.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{row} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero\sphinxhyphen{}based positional row to preview, for the single\sphinxhyphen{}row overload. Equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{observe(row, row + 1)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} / \sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The inclusive start / exclusive stop positions of the row window to preview, for the
range overload — identical slicing semantics to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to

\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A view over the selected row window, with the original feature set and the
original case labels of the selected rows preserved (positions are not
renumbered).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/observe:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{observe(row)}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{observe(row, row + 1)}} — a one\sphinxhyphen{}row range under the hood,
not a separate code path.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both overloads use positional (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}based) row coordinates, never case\sphinxhyphen{}label
lookup — the resulting view’s row keeps whatever case label it already had, but
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{row}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} themselves always count by position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render = true}} allows the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} to auto\sphinxhyphen{}print in a temporary\sphinxhyphen{}value
context, the same convention \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} use.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::percentiles}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:dataframe-percentiles}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{percentiles}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{points}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.25}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.75}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes one or more quantile points for every numeric feature, returning a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} — not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — with one row per requested point and one column per
participating numeric feature. This is the one statistical reducer in this family
whose result is boxed and multi\sphinxhyphen{}column rather than a bare labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, because it
naturally produces a small table (points × features) rather than a single value per
feature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each requested point is interpolated linearly between the two nearest ranked
observations (the conventional definition used for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} as the median, and the same
interpolation {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}} itself uses internally). Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features
are skipped entirely; a frame with no numeric features raises an error, since there
would be nothing to tabulate.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{points} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.25, 0.5, 0.75\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantile points to compute, each in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1{]}}}. The default reproduces the quartiles
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} reports. Each point becomes one row of the result frame, labeled with a
percentage string (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.25}} becomes the row label \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"25\%"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.9}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"90\%"}}, and so
on) — the row order follows the order you pass the points in, not sorted order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations a feature must have before any of its
requested points are computed. A feature with fewer observed values than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}
reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for \sphinxstylestrong{every} requested point in that column — the check applies once
per feature, not once per point.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one row per requested point (labeled by percentage string) and
one column per participating numeric feature, holding that feature’s value at
that point.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} have all six values observed, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 6}} doesn’t affect

the ones that would have needed the missing observation.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike every other reducer documented alongside it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kurtosis}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentiles()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — because
its result is inherently a small table (points × features), not one value per
feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither computed as an
error nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Row labels are percentage strings derived from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{points}}, not the numeric point
values themselves — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.25}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"25\%"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a single statistic instead of a table of points, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}}
(equivalent to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} point) or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} for a broader summary
that includes the default quartiles alongside other statistics.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::median}}}}}}}: the single\sphinxhyphen{}point special case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}}) of this
method.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe}}}}}}}: reports the default quartiles from this method
alongside count, mean, std, min, and max.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mode::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mode}}}}}}}: the other numeric reducer in this family that returns a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} rather than a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}
