\subparagraph{DataFrame::pivot}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:dataframe-pivot}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pivot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull\PYGZus{}keys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reshapes long\sphinxhyphen{}format data into a wide table — one row per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}
value, one column per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} value, each cell holding the single
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} observation for that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pair. This is
the “no aggregation needed” reshape: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pair in
the source data must occur \sphinxstylestrong{at most once}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}} throws — “use pivot\_table
with an aggregation op.” {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}} is the sibling that
accepts (and requires you to name) an aggregation for when pairs repeat.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}} first checks for duplicate pairs via a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}} group, then
delegates to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table(..., GroupOp::Max, ...)}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}} is a safe no\sphinxhyphen{}op aggregation
when every group has exactly one member.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose distinct values become the output rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose distinct values become the new output columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose single value per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pair populates each
cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull\_keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, rows with a null \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} value are excluded
before pivoting. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a null key value forms its own row or column instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for explicit printing, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
to allow auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in a temporary\sphinxhyphen{}value context.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A new frame with one row per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} itself
as the first column, and one additional column per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}}
value. A cell for a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} combination that never
occurs in the source data is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Headphones}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Monitor}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Headphones}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Monitor}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::pivot: duplicate case/feature pairs found; use pivot\PYGZus{}table with an aggregation op
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(Accra, Laptop)}} occurs twice (orders \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{101}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{102}}) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}} has no rule for
combining two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} values into one cell, so it throws rather than silently picking
one. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}} with an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, and
so on) is the reshape to reach for once pairs can repeat.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}} throws if any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pair occurs more than
once in the source data — it never silently picks one observation or averages
them. Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}} with an explicit aggregation for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pair that never occurs in the source data becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the result, never \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull\_keys = false}} keeps a null \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} value as its
own row or column rather than silently dropping those cases.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::pivot\_table}}}}}}}: the aggregating sibling, required once
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pairs can repeat.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::group\_by}}}}}}}: the long\sphinxhyphen{}format equivalent, keeping every key
as its own row feature instead of spreading one key into columns.

\subparagraph{DataFrame::pivot\_table}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:dataframe-pivot-table}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pivot\PYGZus{}table}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{n}{GroupOp}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{op}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{GroupOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull\PYGZus{}keys}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                        }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reshapes long\sphinxhyphen{}format data into a wide summary table: one distinct value of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} per output row, one distinct value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} per output
column, and each cell holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} applied to every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} observation that
shares that row’s and column’s key values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} is closely related to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}}}}}}} — both aggregate
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} per key combination — but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}} keeps every key as its own row
feature (a “long” result), while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} spreads one key out across columns (a
“wide” result). Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} specifically when you want that
row/column cross\sphinxhyphen{}tabulation shape, for example to visualize or export a summary as a
matrix.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose distinct values become the output rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose distinct values become the new output columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature whose values are aggregated into each pivoted cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{op} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The aggregation applied within each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} cell — the same
operation set as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupSpec::op}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Count}}: the number of observations in the cell, including any that are
themselves null. Use this to answer “how many orders fell in this combination” rather
than to summarize \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}}’s magnitude at all.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Nunique}}: the number of \sphinxstyleemphasis{distinct} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} values in the cell.
Useful when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} is closer to a category or an ID than a quantity — for
example, counting how many distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{product}} values a customer bought per city rather
than summing an amount.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Sum}}: the total of every observed value in the cell, nulls skipped. This is
the natural choice when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} is a quantity that should accumulate, such as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{revenue}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Mean}}: the arithmetic average of the observed values in the cell, nulls
skipped. The default — most appropriate when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} measures a rate, price, or
score rather than something you want summed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Max}}: the smallest / largest observed value in the cell.
Useful for questions like “the latest order date” or “the lowest price seen” per
combination.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Std}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp::Var}}: the sample standard deviation / variance of the
observed values in the cell (divides by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}). A cell with only one
observation reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} here, since sample variance is undefined for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n = 1}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull\_keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, cases with a null \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} value are excluded
before pivoting. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a null key value forms its own row or column instead of
being dropped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for explicit printing, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} to
allow auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in a temporary\sphinxhyphen{}value context.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A new frame with one row per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} itself as
the first column, and one additional column per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} value.
Cells for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} combinations that never occur together in
the source data are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — the aggregation genuinely has no
observations to summarize for that cell, which is different from summarizing an
empty group as zero.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(city, product)}} pair that never occurs in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} — Accra never sold a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Monitor}}, Tema never sold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Headphones}}, Kumasi never sold a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Laptop}} — shows up as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}. That distinction matters downstream: summing a row of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s and real
numbers with a null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping reduction gives the true total, whereas a stray \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} would
silently (and wrongly) count as “zero units sold” for a combination that was simply never
observed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Order \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{107}} has no recorded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} (the case’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} cell is null via the validity mask
constructor). With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull\_keys = false}}, that order is not discarded — it forms its
own row keyed on a null \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}, keeping its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Laptop}} total of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}} visible. With the
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull\_keys = true}}, that same order would simply vanish from the pivoted
result with no trace, which is the right behavior when a missing key represents bad data
you want to exclude, but the wrong behavior when a missing key is itself a meaningful
group (an “unassigned” bucket, for example).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} never invents a value for an unobserved \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pair; missing cells are always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Follow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(0.0)}}}}}}} explicitly if a zero is the correct interpretation for
your data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If more than one row of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} shares the exact same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} key pair, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} aggregates across all of them into the single
resulting cell — this is exactly the scenario \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} exists for, as opposed to
a plain reshape that would need every key pair to be unique already.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a result that keeps every key as its own row feature instead of spreading one key
into columns, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}}}}}}} directly.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positions one feature relative to another named anchor feature, either inserting a
brand\sphinxhyphen{}new column there or moving an existing one — without having to restate the
frame’s entire column order the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder()}}}}}}}’s explicit\sphinxhyphen{}list
overload would. The first overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} may or may not already exist on the
frame: if it doesn’t, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{place()}} inserts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} as a new column next to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}};
if it does, the existing column is replaced in place with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s values and,
if it wasn’t already adjacent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}}, moved there. The second overload always
moves an existing feature (by name only, keeping its current values) relative to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor\_feature}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to insert or move. For the first overload, a name not already on the
frame inserts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} as new; a name that already exists replaces that column’s
values with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} and relocates it next to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor\_feature}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, first overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The column data to write at the target position. Its length must match the frame’s
case count (when the frame already has features).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{anchor\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The existing feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} is placed immediately before or after. Must already
exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{after} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} places \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} immediately \sphinxstylestrong{before} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor\_feature}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} places it
immediately \sphinxstylestrong{after}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} inserted or relocated next to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor\_feature}}; every
other feature keeps its relative order.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{profit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{35.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}profit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{place}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{profit}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{profit}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*after=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}profit}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Move an existing feature next to a different anchor.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{city\PYGZus{}first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{place}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*after=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==========================
     | city    id    sales
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Accra   1     100  
1    | Tema    2     120  
2    | Kumasi  3     90   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"city"}} already exists, so this overload just relocates it — its values are
untouched, only its column position changes, landing immediately before its anchor,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"id"}}, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{after = false}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the first overload, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} already exists on the frame, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} replaces
its current values in addition to relocating it — this overload can both rewrite
and reposition a column in one call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor\_feature}} must always already exist on the frame; an unknown anchor throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{place()}} only ever positions one feature at a
time, relative to exactly one anchor — reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder()}} when several features
need to move in the same call.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/place:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reorder}}}}}}}: move several features at once, including
before/after\sphinxhyphen{}anchor placement via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::insert}}}}}}}: insert a new feature by positional index rather
than by anchor name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::drop}}}}}}}: remove a feature entirely, the complement of
inserting one with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{place()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::plot}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:dataframe-plot}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotAccessor}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the 2D charting accessor bound to the current frame — line, step, area,
scatter, bar, histogram, box, violin, heatmap, and more, one chart kind per method.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}} itself draws nothing; it just binds the frame (and, optionally, shared
chart\sphinxhyphen{}wide defaults like a default x\sphinxhyphen{}feature or hue\sphinxhyphen{}feature) and hands back an
accessor whose methods each return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — a chart/figure object from
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} plotting library, which owns its own reference documentation (rendering
backends, themes, saving to PNG/SVG, and so on). This page previews entry into the
accessor; it does not re\sphinxhyphen{}document \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} or every chart kind.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFramePlotOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Chart\sphinxhyphen{}wide defaults shared across every plot drawn from the returned accessor —
a default x\sphinxhyphen{}feature, a default hue\sphinxhyphen{}feature, tick/label rotation, figure size, tight
layout, and more. Omit it to use the accessor’s built\sphinxhyphen{}in defaults.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor}}
An accessor bound to the current frame (and, if given, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}). Each of its
methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.line()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.scatter()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bar()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.hist()}}, and so on) builds and
returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure, ready to further customize or save.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Enter the plotting accessor and draw a line chart with default options.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{120.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{90.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}png}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{monthly\PYGZus{}sales.png}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales.plot()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor}} bound to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.line("amount", "month")}} draws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount}} against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}} and returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}, which
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_png(...)}} then writes to disk. No table is printed by any of this — the
result is a rendered figure, not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Share chart\sphinxhyphen{}wide options (a default x\sphinxhyphen{}feature) across every chart drawn
from one accessor.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}x\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accessor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accessor}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// uses \PYGZdq{}month\PYGZdq{} as x automatically}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} explicitly (as in Example 1) always takes precedence; the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} only fills in when a chart method’s own
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} argument is omitted.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}} never touches or copies the frame’s data beyond what the requested chart
needs to draw — it is a lightweight accessor, not a materialized copy.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every chart method returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}; that type’s own methods (theming,
sizing, legends, exporting) are documented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}}’s reference, not here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}}}}}}} instead for genuinely three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional charts (3D
scatter, 3D line); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}} covers only 2D chart kinds.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::plot3d}}}}}}}: the 3D counterpart to this accessor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts}}}}}}}: other dedicated accessors
entered the same way, previewed on their own pages.

\end{itemize}



\sphinxstepscope




\subparagraph{DataFrame::plot3d}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:dataframe-plot3d}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the 3D charting accessor bound to the current frame — 3D scatter and 3D line
charts, for genuinely three\sphinxhyphen{}axis data. Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}} itself
draws nothing: it binds the frame (and optional shared chart\sphinxhyphen{}wide \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}) and
hands back an accessor whose methods each return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure — the
same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} figure type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}}’s 2D accessor returns, documented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}}’s
own reference.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFramePlotOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Chart\sphinxhyphen{}wide defaults shared across every 3D chart drawn from the returned accessor —
the same options struct {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}}}}}}} accepts. Omit it to use the accessor’s
built\sphinxhyphen{}in defaults.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}}
An accessor bound to the current frame (and, if given, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}). Its methods
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.scatter()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.line()}}) each build and return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Enter the 3D plotting accessor and draw a 3D scatter chart.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot3d:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}} covers only genuinely three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional chart kinds (3D scatter, 3D
line); use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/plot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}}}}}}} for every 2D chart kind instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every chart method returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}; that type’s own methods are
documented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}}’s reference, not here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature named in a 3D chart call must be numeric — passing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature
as one of the three axes is not a supported combination.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise exponentiation. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow()}} shares the exact same
overload shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the arithmetic
family — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the scalar/frame/
Thread operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand (the exponent): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature raised to the
power of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the other arithmetic methods in this family, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow()}} always evaluates
feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature rather than as a single batched matrix operation internally —
this is an implementation detail with no observable effect on the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its full overload shape, alignment semantics, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} behavior with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::prep\_sql}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:dataframe-prep-sql}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{prep\PYGZus{}sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statement}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlPrepared}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{prep\PYGZus{}sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statement}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{SqlOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlPrepared}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Binds a SQL statement template — one containing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{param\_name\}}} placeholders — to the
current frame once, returning a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}} object you can \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(...)}}
repeatedly with different parameter bindings, without re\sphinxhyphen{}typing (or re\sphinxhyphen{}parsing) the
statement text each time. This is the reusable\sphinxhyphen{}query counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql().execute(statement)}}}}}}}, which parses and runs a statement in one shot
and is a better fit when a query only runs once.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statement} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SQL statement template, using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{param\_name\}}} for value placeholders (and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@ident\_name\}}} for identifier placeholders) that get bound at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(...)}} time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same execution options {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}}}}}}} accepts — additional joinable sources,
default parameter bindings, missing\sphinxhyphen{}parameter policy, row/memory/timeout limits, and
diagnostics toggles. Omitted params can still be supplied later at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(...)}}
time.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}}
A prepared statement bound to the current frame, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{statement}}.
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute()}} (using only whatever params were already in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}) or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(params)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(params, identifier\_params)}} to bind values and
run the query, returning a fresh \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} result each time.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Prepare a parameterized statement once, then execute it with two
different parameter bindings.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stmt}} is parsed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{statement}} only once, at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql()}} time. Each
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(\{...\})}} call just substitutes a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_sales}} value into that
already\sphinxhyphen{}prepared template and re\sphinxhyphen{}runs the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} filter — case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s row survives
both times (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{120}} is greater than both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{95}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{110}}), while case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s row
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales = 100}}) only survives the looser \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{95}} threshold. Both result frames keep the
original case labels of whichever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} rows matched.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The statement text itself is fixed once \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql()}} is called; only the bound
parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{values} can change between \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(...)}} calls, not the SQL text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute()}} (no arguments) re\sphinxhyphen{}runs the statement using only whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}
were already set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql()}} time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql()}} over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql().execute(statement)}} specifically when the same
query text will run many times with different bindings — the query is parsed once
instead of on every call.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::prod}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:dataframe-prod}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to the product of its values, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
whose entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} returns, but multiplying instead of adding. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are
skipped entirely, the same rule every other single\sphinxhyphen{}statistic reducer in this family
follows.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) multiplies down each feature’s cases,
producing one product per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} multiplies across each row’s
features instead, producing one product per case — for example, multiplying a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}
column by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} column row\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}row to get each row’s line total.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that reduction’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded from the product entirely, as if
they were never part of the multiplication.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value poisons the entire reduction it participates in,
which comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or per case
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), holding the product of that reduction’s values.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Multiply every numeric feature’s values, skipping missing values (the
default).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.228251417e+12
     units  240
unit\PYGZus{}price  8.438976e+11
  discount  2.4e\PYGZhy{}06
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s missing observation (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is excluded from the product, the same
way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}} treat that column’s missing value — the
product runs over the remaining five prices only. Note the scientific notation on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prod()}}’s outputs grow (or shrink) fast, and
the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{:.10g\}}} formatting every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} render uses switches to
scientific notation once a value’s magnitude crosses ten significant digits either way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.228251417e+12
     units  240
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} — the two features that each have
one missing value — come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} are
unaffected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} to multiply across a row’s features instead of down a
feature’s cases — here, computing each order’s line total as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units * unit\_price}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}totals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Feature}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}totals}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2400
1  227.5
2  1150
3  960
4  168
5  2
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} show the expected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units * unit\_price}} line total. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is missing, and with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}
the missing factor is simply excluded from that row’s product rather than poisoning
it, leaving only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) to multiply. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} as the second argument if a
missing price should invalidate the whole row’s total instead.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prod()}}’s result is labeled by feature name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or by case index
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced
from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither multiplied as an
error nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

754 behavior (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}), the same as any other floating\sphinxhyphen{}point multiplication in
the library.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::ptypes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:dataframe-ptypes}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ptypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DTypes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the coarse payload family of every feature in the frame — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — without the concrete scalar type underneath. Where
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}} tells you \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}} versus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}int64\textgreater{}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} only tells you it’s a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} at all. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} when you’re
routing logic by payload family (numeric work needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, text work needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
and so on) and don’t need the extra precision \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}} provides.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::DTypes}} object rather
than a raw map — it supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contains(name)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{at(name)}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator{[}{]}(name)}}, and range\sphinxhyphen{}based iteration over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(name, ptype)}} pairs,
and has its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}} for a quick printout.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DTypes}}
A feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}payload\sphinxhyphen{}family summary. Iterate it directly, or look up one
feature’s payload family with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes(){[}"feature\_name"{]}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes().at("feature\_name")}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewrites one feature’s values only at the rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, leaving
every other row’s value on that feature untouched — the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature, mask\sphinxhyphen{}driven
sibling of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}}}}}}} (which nulls out cells rather than replacing them with
a chosen value). Where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} is itself a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} rather than a scalar, each masked
row is replaced by \sphinxstylestrong{that same row’s own value} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} — not one shared
replacement broadcast to every masked cell. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} returns a new frame;
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put\_()}}}}}}} is the in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart that mutates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every value\sphinxhyphen{}type overload above also has a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask convenience
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put(feature, series\_mask, value)}}) that just wraps the mask in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} and
forwards to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask overload — the two mask types behave identically.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to rewrite. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean row mask. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} rewrites the corresponding row on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
leaves that row’s existing value unchanged. A masked\sphinxhyphen{}missing mask entry behaves like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement. A scalar (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, string, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}}) is broadcast to every
masked row identically. A full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} instead supplies a \sphinxstylestrong{different} replacement
value per row — row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} replaces row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}, wherever
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis when it doesn’t already
match exactly, the same alignment mechanism used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame identical to the source, except \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s masked rows have been
replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, string, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}}) is the same replacement for
every masked row; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} supplies a different replacement per row,
taken from that row’s own position in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} may be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} overloads are pure
convenience wrappers with identical behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} never changes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s kind; replacing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature requires a
string (or null) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, and replacing a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature requires a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (or null) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\end{itemize}

\item {}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}: rewrites one feature’s values at the
rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly and returning a reference
to it, instead of returning a new frame. Every parameter and replacement rule is
identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} — see that page for the full breakdown of scalar\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
replacement semantics; this page only covers what differs about mutating in place.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to rewrite in place. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean row mask, identical in behavior to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement, identical in behavior to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} — a scalar
broadcasts to every masked row, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} supplies a different value per row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis, identical to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s masked rows have been rewritten.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put\_()}} mutates and returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} by reference; it never allocates a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} value that shares the same underlying columns (via a prior
copy) does not see this mutation — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrame}}’s copies are
value\sphinxhyphen{}like, not aliased references to shared state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}} for the complete parameter and replacement\sphinxhyphen{}semantics
breakdown; every rule there (scalar vs. per\sphinxhyphen{}row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} replacement, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask
convenience overloads, kind constraints) applies identically here.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::put}}}}}}}: the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating counterpart, returning a new frame
instead of mutating in place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mask}}}}}}}: nulls out masked cells outright, rather than
replacing them with a chosen value.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::query}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:dataframe-query}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{expression}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter rows with a boolean expression written against DataFrame feature names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query(...)}} is the string\sphinxhyphen{}expression row filter for PlussMic. It lets you write one compact predicate instead of building a boolean mask by hand, which is especially useful when you are exploring data interactively or translating logic from notebook\sphinxhyphen{}style workflows into C++.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression itself is a small language evaluated against feature names, so you can
write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"units \textgreater{}= 10 and region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}"}} instead of assembling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df{[}(df.units \textgreater{}= 10) \& (df.region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}){]}}} by hand. The C++ equivalent of the
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}mask style is {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}} when the predicate
reads more clearly as a single self\sphinxhyphen{}contained string, and for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} when the mask is
more naturally built up from existing C++ expressions or reused across calls.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expression Input

\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat the query string as code\sphinxhyphen{}like input owned by the developer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not pass untrusted raw user input directly into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query(...)}} without validation or a safer higher\sphinxhyphen{}level policy layer around it.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{expression}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean filter expression to evaluate against each row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common patterns include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numeric comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{}= 10}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
string comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
combined predicates: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{}= 10 and region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}feature comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{} price}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spaced feature names via backticks: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciigrave{}First Name\textasciigrave{} == \textquotesingle{}Laurel\textquotesingle{}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result must be a row\sphinxhyphen{}level truth decision.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A filtered frame containing only the rows where the expression evaluates to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The returned frame preserves:
\PYGZhy{} the original feature set,
\PYGZhy{} the original feature order,
\PYGZhy{} the original case labels for rows that survive the filter.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::filter: filter rows from an explicit boolean mask instead of a query string.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::where: row filter using a boolean mask that has already been computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::case\_study: select rows by position, label, or mask when you do not want an expression parser.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression is evaluated row by row against the current frame. Feature names are available directly inside the query string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
String literals must be quoted. For example, write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == south}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}feature comparison is supported. For example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{} price}} compares the two features row by row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use backticks around feature names that contain spaces or punctuation, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciigrave{}First Name\textasciigrave{} == \textquotesingle{}Laurel\textquotesingle{}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method is for row filtering. It does not rewrite values, create columns, or mutate the current frame in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression is parsed and evaluated by PlussMic’s own small expression engine, not by
shelling out to an external interpreter — there is no dependency on Python, a SQL engine,
or any other runtime to use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}. The patterns documented above (numeric and string
comparisons, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{and}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{or}} combinators, quoted literals, and backtick\sphinxhyphen{}quoted feature
names) are the supported core; if a more elaborate expression does not parse the way you
expect, fall back to building the mask explicitly with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}}, which
accepts any boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} you can construct in ordinary C++.

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{radd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}: computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other + frame}} instead
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame + other}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmod}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rpow}} are the reflected counterparts of the eight forward
arithmetic methods, all scalar\sphinxhyphen{}only (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double other}}) — there is no reflected
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} form, since swapping which side is the “frame”
is unambiguous once a scalar is the other operand.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For addition specifically, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.add(other)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.radd(other)}} produce the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{same} result, since addition is commutative — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} mainly exists for symmetry
with the rest of the reflected family (where operand order genuinely changes the
result, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}}) and for call sites where “the scalar comes first”
reads more naturally.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar added to every numeric feature on the frame.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature increased by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All eight reflected methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}},

\item {}
