agree. For non\sphinxhyphen{}commutative operations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv}},

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rand}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}. Since logical AND is commutative,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.rand(other)}} is indistinguishable from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.land(other)}} in every observable
respect — same cell values, and (for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload) the same case labels
and title, both drawn from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}} itself, exactly as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} documents.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\{note\} Previously, the DataFrame overload inherited case labels from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
An earlier revision of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand(const DataFrame\&)}} computed the reflection as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other.land(*this)}}, which meant the result’s case labels and title came from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead of from the frame the method was called on — a real, verified quirk
that was documented here as a caution. That has since been fixed: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}} now zips
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} directly (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::rand()}} handling the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell operand
order internally), so the result’s structure always comes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} and every other method in this family. If you’re working against
an older build where this fix isn’t present, verify which behavior you’re actually
seeing before relying on either.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYGZsh{}\PYGZsh{} Parameters

**other**

`const DataFrame\PYGZam{}` or `const Thread\PYGZam{}` — identical shape requirements to
[`land()`](land.md): same feature names in order and same case count for the
`DataFrame` overload; one boolean thread matching `ncases()` for the `Thread` overload.

\PYGZsh{}\PYGZsh{} Returns

`DataFrame`
    A new frame holding the logical AND of each cell against the corresponding `other`
    value, with case labels and title drawn from the frame `rand()` was called on —
    identical in every respect to what [`land()`](land.md) would produce for the same
    arguments.

\PYGZsh{}\PYGZsh{} Examples

Example 1. `rand()` and `land()` produce identical results, values and case labels
both.

```cpp
using namespace pluss::table;

auto left = DataFrame(\PYGZob{}
    \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}a\PYGZdq{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}series(\PYGZob{}true, false, true\PYGZcb{}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool)\PYGZcb{},
    \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}b\PYGZdq{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}series(\PYGZob{}true, true, false\PYGZcb{}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool)\PYGZcb{},
\PYGZcb{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}note(\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}p\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}q\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}r\PYGZdq{}\PYGZcb{}));

auto right = DataFrame(\PYGZob{}
    \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}a\PYGZdq{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}series(\PYGZob{}true, true, false\PYGZcb{}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool)\PYGZcb{},
    \PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}b\PYGZdq{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}series(\PYGZob{}false, true, true\PYGZcb{}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool)\PYGZcb{},
\PYGZcb{}, pluss::make\PYGZus{}note(\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}x\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}y\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}z\PYGZdq{}\PYGZcb{}));

auto forward = left.land(right);
std::cout \PYGZlt{}\PYGZlt{} forward;
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Keep}\PYG{p}{,}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature’s values with their rank among that feature’s other
values — the smallest value gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending = true}}, the default), the
next\sphinxhyphen{}smallest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, and so on. The result is the same shape as the source frame;
ranks replace values in place, feature by feature, rather than being reduced to a single
summary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two things need a policy decision that plain sorting doesn’t: what happens when two
values are \sphinxstylestrong{tied}, and what happens to a \sphinxstylestrong{null}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rank()}} exposes both as explicit
parameters instead of picking a silent default you’d have to discover by testing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ties} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankTieRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How to resolve rank ties (equal values):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}}: tied values all receive the mean of the ranks they would have occupied
(two values tied for ranks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} both get \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.5}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}: tied values all receive the lowest of the ranks they would have occupied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Highest}}: tied values all receive the highest of the ranks they would have occupied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}: ties are broken by original row order — whichever tied value appears first in
the frame gets the lower rank.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dense}}: like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}, but without leaving a gap in the rank sequence afterward (the
next distinct value always gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{previous\_rank + 1}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{previous\_rank + count\_of\_ties}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankNullRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How to rank missing values: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}} leaves a null’s rank as null (it is excluded from
ranking entirely); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}} ranks nulls as if they were the smallest values; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bottom}} ranks
them as if they were the largest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} ranks smallest\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}largest (smallest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} reverses the order
(largest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{percentage} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, each rank is divided by the number of ranked observations, giving a
percentile\sphinxhyphen{}style rank in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, 1{]}}} instead of a raw integer\sphinxhyphen{}like rank.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature’s values replaced
by their rank under the requested policy. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default tie policy: tied values share the average of their ranks.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankTieRule::First}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ada}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{80}} (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}) beats \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Chen}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{80}} (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) purely

left unresolved. This is the policy to reach for when downstream logic needs a strict,
unambiguous ordering (assigning unique positions in a leaderboard, for instance) rather
than a statistically fair split.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rank()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with ranks; it does not add a new
column alongside the original. Keep the original values with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}}
first if you need both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankNullRule::Keep}} (the default) means a row with a null in the ranked feature simply
has no rank there — it does not consume a rank position, so the remaining values still
rank as if that row didn’t exist for this feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage = true}} is useful when you want a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1{]}}}\sphinxhyphen{}scaled competitive standing
(percentile rank) rather than a raw position number, without a separate division step.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sort\_values}}}}}}}: reorder rows by value, rather than
annotating each row with its rank in place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::percentiles}}}}}}}: a related but distinct question — the
value at a given percentile, rather than a value’s own rank.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}: computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / frame}} instead
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame / other}}. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rmul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul()}}}}}}}, the reflected and forward forms
genuinely disagree here, since division is not commutative.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
rdiv() and rtruediv() are the same operation
Just like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} are verified\sphinxhyphen{}identical at the
forward level, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rtruediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}}}}}}} are the same reflected
operation under two names — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}} for the side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side confirmation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar that the frame’s values divide.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} divided by every numeric
feature’s value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv(other)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / frame}}; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div(other)}}}}}}} computes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame / other}}. The two only coincide when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}}’s values and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} are equal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}} are verified to be the same operation, mirroring the
forward \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} identity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only accepts a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}}}}}} for why there is no
reflected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dividing by a frame value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} produces the usual floating\sphinxhyphen{}point division\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}zero
result (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, depending on the numerator), not an exception.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes feature names without touching a single value, dtype, or case label. Two
distinct shapes are supported, and picking the right one matters:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Targeted rename} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}}, or a collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(old\_name, new\_name)}}
pairs): rename one or a few specific features by name, leaving every other feature’s
name untouched. This is the overload to reach for almost all the time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Full\sphinxhyphen{}axis replace} (a plain list of names, with no pairing): replace \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature
name at once, positionally, left to right. The list you pass must have exactly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} entries, in the exact order the current features already appear — this
overload does not know or care what the old names were, it only knows position.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mixing these up is the most common mistake: passing a short list intending a targeted
rename will instead try to rename \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature positionally (and fail or misname
things if the count doesn’t match). Use the pair\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads unless you genuinely
mean “replace the entire schema in one shot.”


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{old\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Existing feature name to rename, for the single\sphinxhyphen{}rename overload.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Replacement name for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{renames} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, std::string\_view\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, std::string\_view\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(old\_name, new\_name)}} pairs, applied together. Features not named in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{renames}} keep their current name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}const char*\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A full replacement name list, applied \sphinxstylestrong{positionally} to every feature on the frame,
left to right. Must have exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} entries.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested names applied. Feature order, values, dtypes, and the
case axis are all unchanged — only names move.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The full\sphinxhyphen{}axis overload (a plain list, no pairing) requires the list length to match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} exactly. A shorter or longer list is a programming error, not something
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} pads or truncates for you.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} never changes values, dtypes, feature order, or case labels — it is a
pure schema\sphinxhyphen{}naming operation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an in\sphinxhyphen{}place variant on a single feature, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}}}}}}} (note the
trailing underscore, the project\sphinxhyphen{}wide convention for mutating siblings of a
non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating method).

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}}’s targeted single\sphinxhyphen{}name overload:
renames exactly one feature, mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly and returning a reference to
it, rather than returning a new frame. Values, dtype, and case labels are untouched —
only the feature’s name changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}, which offers several overloads (single pair, multiple pairs, or a
full positional\sphinxhyphen{}list replace), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} only supports the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature form —
there is no in\sphinxhyphen{}place equivalent of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}’s multi\sphinxhyphen{}pair or full\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}replace
overloads.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{old\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The existing feature name to rename. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement name. Must not already be used by another feature on the frame
(unless it is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}, which is a no\sphinxhyphen{}op).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}} renamed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}}.

Example 1. Rename one feature in place.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} throws if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}} doesn’t exist, or if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}} collides with a
different, already\sphinxhyphen{}existing feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renaming a feature to its own current name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name == new\_name}}) is a harmless
no\sphinxhyphen{}op.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For renaming several features at once, or replacing every feature name
positionally, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} only covers the
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature, in\sphinxhyphen{}place case.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Moves one or more named features into a new relative position, while every other
feature keeps its current relative order — without having to restate the frame’s
entire column list the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} reordering would. There are
two ways to describe a move:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A plain list of names (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"city"\})}}) moves those features together to the
\sphinxstylestrong{front}, preserving their relative order among themselves and the relative order
of everything else. This is shorthand for a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{placement = Front}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} (or several, applied left to right) supports front, back, before\sphinxhyphen{}an\sphinxhyphen{}
anchor, or after\sphinxhyphen{}an\sphinxhyphen{}anchor placement, and can select the features to move either by
an explicit name list or by a regex pattern matched against every feature name.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} in a multi\sphinxhyphen{}spec sequence sees the column order left behind by the
previous spec — later specs can reference columns by name regardless of where an
earlier spec moved them.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to move together to the front, preserving their relative order among
themselves and the relative order of every untouched feature. Shorthand for a single
front\sphinxhyphen{}placement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{spec} / \sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} / a range or list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more move instructions, each built via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move(...)}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move\_regex(...)}} and a placement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.first()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.last()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.before(anchor)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.after(anchor)}}). Several specs are applied in the exact order
given, each seeing the previous spec’s resulting order.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the moved feature(s) repositioned as described; every untouched
feature keeps its relative order (values, dtypes, and case labels are unchanged).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"a", "b"\})}} moves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}} together to the front, preserving the
relative order of every other feature — it does not mean “replace the entire
feature order with just these two.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move\_regex(pattern)}} selects every feature whose name matches
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} (ECMAScript regex), instead of naming them explicitly — useful when
moving a family of similarly\sphinxhyphen{}named columns (for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{move\_regex("\textasciicircum{}col\_2{[}1\sphinxhyphen{}4{]}\$")}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature named in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} must exist exactly once across the frame; an
unknown name, a duplicate within one spec, or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{before}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{after}} anchor that is
itself one of the moved features throws.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/place::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::place}}}}}}}: move (or insert) exactly one feature relative to
one anchor, a lighter\sphinxhyphen{}weight alternative when only a single feature needs to move.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::features}}}}}}}: select or drop features outright, rather than
just reordering them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::rename}}}}}}}: change feature names, a distinct operation from
reordering them.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::repeated}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:dataframe-repeated}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flags \sphinxstylestrong{every} row that belongs to a group sharing the same composite key across
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} — including that group’s very first occurrence, not just the ones after
it. This is exactly {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(features, false, false)}}}}}}} with its
display name changed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"repeated"}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} is what you reach for when you
want “is this row part of a repeated group at all,” rather than “is this row a
duplicate follower of an earlier one” (which is what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}} answers instead).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features form the composite key that defines a “group.” Leave empty (the
default) to compare whole rows across every feature.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, one entry per case, labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"repeated"}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} marks every
row belonging to a key that occurs more than once anywhere in the frame; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
marks a row whose key is unique.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Flag every row belonging to a repeated student group.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{student}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Ada}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Bola}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Ada}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Chen}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Bola}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==============
     | student
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Ada    
1    | Bola   
2    | Ada    
3    | Chen   
4    | Bola   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[5 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{groups}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{student}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{groups}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  true
2  true
3  false
4  true
Name: repeated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Ada"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Bola"}} each occur twice, so every row for either name is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}},
including case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} — their \sphinxstylestrong{first} appearances. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Chen"}} occurs only
once, so case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Compare against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default follower\sphinxhyphen{}only semantics on the
same data.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{followers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{student}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{followers}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  false
1  false
2  true
3  false
4  true
Name: duplicated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}) marks only the \sphinxstylestrong{second and later}
occurrence of each repeated name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} at cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, the first
appearances) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} marks \sphinxstylestrong{all} of them, first appearance included. The two
methods answer genuinely different questions: “which rows are extras I could drop”
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}) versus “which rows belong to a group that repeats at all”
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}}).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} is literally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(features, /*keep\_first=*/false, /*keep\_last=*/false)}} under a different display name — it never has its own
separate keep\sphinxhyphen{}policy parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing value in every selected feature is itself a valid “value” for grouping
purposes — two rows that are both missing on every selected feature count as
sharing a key, same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected feature name must exist on the frame; an unknown name throws.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::duplicated}}}}}}}: the keep\sphinxhyphen{}policy\sphinxhyphen{}driven sibling, for
marking only the extras after (or before) the first occurrence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::drop\_duplicates}}}}}}}: removes duplicate rows outright
instead of just flagging them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::freq}}}}}}}: counts \sphinxstyleemphasis{how many times} each composite key occurs,
rather than flagging individual rows.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finds a specific value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}) across compatible features and rewrites every matching
cell to a replacement value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}), returning the updated frame. The long overload list
looks intimidating, but it collapses into one rule: \sphinxstylestrong{the type of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} decides which
feature kind participates}. Pass a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} and only numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features are
searched; pass a string and only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features are searched; pass a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} and only that temporal kind is searched. Features of any other kind are left
completely alone, the same way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}} restrict themselves by dtype.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The other half of the rule concerns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} (of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}}), the
project’s null\sphinxhyphen{}sentinel constant: pass it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} to turn matched cells into missing
values instead of a replacement value, or pass it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} to replace \sphinxstylestrong{existing}
nulls with a concrete value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(pluss::null, 0.0)}} is a targeted, single\sphinxhyphen{}value
alternative to a broader {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(0.0)}}}}}}} call).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Note\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Timeline\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::TimeIndex\&}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value to search for. Its type selects which feature kind participates in the search;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} searches for existing missing values instead of a concrete value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to} (same family of types as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement value written wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} matches. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} to turn
matches into missing values instead of a concrete replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricts the search to an explicit feature subset. Leave empty to search every
compatible feature (every feature whose kind matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every matching cell rewritten to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}. Features that don’t match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type, and cells within compatible features that don’t match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s value,
are left exactly as they were.

===========================

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} arguments are matched up positionally: every occurrence of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from{[}i{]}}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to{[}i{]}}}, for every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}, in a single pass over the frame. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{101}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{103}} are renumbered to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9101}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9103}} respectively; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{102}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{104}} never
appear in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}, so they pass through unchanged. This is the overload to reach for when
you have a whole lookup table of value substitutions rather than a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}
pair — build the two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} from a mapping and pass them straight through, instead of
writing one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} call per pair.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type is the whole dispatch rule: a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} never touches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features, a
string never touches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features, and so on, regardless of what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} you
pass.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} narrows the search further, but never widens it beyond what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s
type already allows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} matches values exactly. It has no tolerance, rounding, or pattern\sphinxhyphen{}matching
behavior for numeric or string values — use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}}}}}} or a mask built with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} for anything more elaborate than an exact\sphinxhyphen{}value swap.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::reshuffle}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:dataframe-reshuffle}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{reshuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{uint64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomly permutes either the case order (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}, the default) or the feature
order (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}) of the frame, leaving the other axis and every value
untouched. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle(random\_state)}}}}}}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Case, random\_state)}} — the dedicated, more discoverable name for the case\sphinxhyphen{}axis case, which
is by far the more common one (train/test splits, breaking up any accidental
ordering before sampling, and so on).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} seeds the underlying random engine (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}}); passing the
same seed reproduces the same permutation on the same build, while omitting it draws
a fresh, non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducible permutation from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} each call. Because
the exact permutation a given seed produces depends on the C++ standard library’s
own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} implementation, this page verifies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}}’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{effect} — same
rows or features, same values, different order, reproducible given a seed — rather
than asserting one specific row order for one specific seed.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} permutes row order, keeping the feature order and every row’s own
values intact. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} permutes feature (column) order instead, keeping row
order and every feature’s own values intact.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::uint64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A seed for reproducible shuffling. Omit it (the default) for a non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic
shuffle seeded from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested axis permuted; the other axis and every
underlying value are unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} on the same build reproduces the same permutation;
it is not guaranteed to reproduce the same permutation across different platforms,
compilers, or standard library implementations, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}}’s exact
algorithm is implementation\sphinxhyphen{}defined.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} are mutually exclusive per call — a single call
only permutes one axis. Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}} twice (once per axis) to permute both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}}}}}}} is the more discoverable, case\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}only convenience for
the common case; reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Feature, ...)}} directly when you
specifically need to permute column order instead.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::shuffle}}}}}}}: the case\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}only convenience wrapper around
this method.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sample}}}}}}}: draw a random subset of rows, rather than
permuting the full set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reorder}}}}}}}: deterministic, explicit feature reordering,
rather than a random permutation.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:dataframe-rfloordiv}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rfloordiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}: computes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(other / frame)}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(frame / other)}}. Like the forward pair, this
is the one reflected arithmetic method whose result genuinely differs from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rtruediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}}}}}}} in value, not just in name — it always
rounds the quotient down after dividing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar that the frame’s values floor\sphinxhyphen{}divide.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} floor\sphinxhyphen{}divided by every
numeric feature’s value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The forward \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv(10.0)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(x / 10)}} instead: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2 / 10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3 / 10}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4 / 10}} are all less than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, so every case floors down to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — a very different
result from the reflected form’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} above. This is a concrete illustration
of why operand order matters for non\sphinxhyphen{}commutative arithmetic: reversing which side is
the numerator can move results from “always zero” to “always at least two”.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv()}} always rounds the quotient down to the nearest whole number, exactly
like the forward {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}, just with the operand order reversed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only accepts a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}}}}}} for why there is no
reflected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload.

\end{itemize}

where the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload’s case labels came from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead — that has
since been fixed, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}} shares the fix.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::round}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:dataframe-round}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{round}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{decimals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rounds every numeric feature to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals}} decimal places, cell by cell. With the
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals = 0}}, each value rounds to the nearest whole number. A null cell
stays null — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}} only ever changes an observed number’s precision, never invents
a value for a missing one.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{decimals} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of decimal places to keep. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} rounds to the nearest integer. A positive value
keeps that many digits after the decimal point (internally, the value is scaled by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10\textasciicircum{}decimals}}, rounded to the nearest whole number, then scaled back down).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature rounded to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals}} places. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) are left
exactly as they were.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every} numeric feature on the frame at once; there is no
per\sphinxhyphen{}feature selector. Round one feature at a time via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}} if only
some columns should change.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nulls pass through completely unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}} is not a substitute for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the numeric, whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}}’s
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/round::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::round}}}}}}} is a different,
unrelated method that rounds timestamps to a calendar unit.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rpow:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

every numeric feature’s value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rpow:notes}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rxor:what-it-does}}

The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}}. Since logical XOR is commutative,

See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the full explanation, including a note on a previous
revision where the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload’s case labels came from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead —
that has since been fixed, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}} shares the fix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a random subset of cases (or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, a random subset of
features) from the frame — either a fixed count (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}) or a proportion of the axis
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}}). Internally this is built on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}: a set of positions is drawn
by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} random\sphinxhyphen{}number engine, then those positions are taken in one
call, so the same shape guarantees \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} makes (original case labels preserved,
feature order preserved) apply here too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A note on reproducibility: passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} seeds the engine so the \sphinxstylestrong{same
seed on the same build (same compiler and standard library) reproduces the same
draw}. The draw itself, however, is produced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} / a uniform integer
distribution from the C++ standard library, and the exact sequence those algorithms
produce for a given seed is not fixed by the C++ standard — only the underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} engine is fully specified. In practice this means a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}
reproduces results reliably across runs on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{same} platform and toolchain, but the
specific rows two different compilers or standard library implementations draw for
the same seed are not guaranteed to match each other.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact number of items to draw from the selected axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{frac} (floating\sphinxhyphen{}point)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The proportion of the selected axis to draw, computed as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round(frac * axis\_size)}}. Values greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} (there
aren’t enough distinct rows to draw more than the total without repeating some).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{replace} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the same position can be drawn more than once:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default): every drawn position is distinct — equivalent to shuffling
the axis and taking the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}}\sphinxhyphen{}implied count).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: positions are drawn independently with replacement, so the same row (or
feature) can appear more than once in the result. Feature sampling
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis = Axis::Feature}}) does not support \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} — that combination is a
validation error.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which axis to sample from. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) draws rows. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}
draws columns instead, returning a frame with a random subset (or resampling, subject
to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}} restriction above) of the original features, each with all of its
data intact.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::uint64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit seed for the underlying random engine. Omit it (use one of the shorter
overloads) to seed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} instead, which draws fresh entropy each
call and is never reproducible run\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}run.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing the drawn subset, with the source frame’s feature order,
dtypes, and original case labels preserved for whichever rows/features were
selected.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} rows, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} allows drawing more than that — case

repeat, since with\sphinxhyphen{}replacement sampling can draw the same row more than once. The
specific repeats and their order are random and will differ run to run; what is fixed
is the shape (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} rows) and that every value in the output traces back to one of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}’s original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} rows. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, requesting more rows than
exist is not possible for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Output (one possible draw)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===========================
     | order\PYGZus{}id  unit\PYGZus{}price
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 101       1200      
1    | 102       45.5      
2    | 103       1150      
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac = 0.5}} over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} features draws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} of them — here, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}
happened to be chosen, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} are equally likely candidates on
another run. What is fixed is the shape: the result always keeps all \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} cases for
whichever features were chosen, since sampling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} only decides which
\sphinxstyleemphasis{columns} participate, not which rows.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}} is built on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}; a drawn position’s original case label
is preserved in the result, exactly as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} would preserve it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} reproduces the same draw on the same compiler/standard\sphinxhyphen{}library
build, but is not guaranteed to reproduce identically across different platforms —
don’t rely on a specific seed producing byte\sphinxhyphen{}identical results in, say, CI running a
different toolchain than a developer’s laptop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} is not supported for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} sampling; every feature draw
is always without replacement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}} values above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, since there is no way to draw
more distinct items than the axis contains.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::take}}}}}}}: the deterministic positional\sphinxhyphen{}selection primitive this
method draws random positions for.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::shuffle}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reshuffle}}}}}}}: a full
random reordering of the frame instead of a subset.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::head}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tail}}}}}}}: deterministic
positional alternatives when randomness isn’t what you need.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::save\_as}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:dataframe-save-as}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}as}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filepath}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Config}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{void}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A single format\sphinxhyphen{}switched write entry point: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} picks which dedicated
writer actually runs, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as("csv", ...)}} behaves exactly like calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} with the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as("json", ...)}} like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}}, and so on. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} is matched
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}},
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} — the exact same set of format names {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}}}}}} recognizes
on the read side, and every one of them is supported through this dispatcher (unlike
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}, whose non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overloads only cover \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}}
has no such asymmetry — every format is reachable regardless of how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}} is
supplied).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Useful when the destination format is only known at runtime (for example, chosen from
a file extension or a user\sphinxhyphen{}facing dropdown) rather than hardcoded at the call site.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target\_type} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Format selector: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}}, matched case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively. Any other value throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSS\_FAIL("DataFrame::save\_as: unsupported target type ...")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Forwarded as\sphinxhyphen{}is to whichever dedicated writer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} selects — the recognized
keys are exactly that writer’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} keys (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}}}}}}} for the
per\sphinxhyphen{}format key lists).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} matching is case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}
are accepted as interchangeable spellings — the same aliasing
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load(source\_type, ...)}}}}}}} use.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}}/positional overloads (which only support
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} and throw for the other three formats), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}} has no
such gap — every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config\_entries}} overload reaches all five formats.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An unrecognized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} throws immediately, before any file I/O is attempted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}} cannot write a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet Excel workbook — like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}}, it writes exactly one sheet per call.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load}}}}}}}: the read\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart, including the
overload\sphinxhyphen{}dependent format\sphinxhyphen{}support asymmetry that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}} does not share.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a delimited text file. The plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv(filepath)}} overload
covers the common case — comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, header row written, case labels \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} written
as their own column — while the fully positional overload exposes every formatting knob
CSV round\sphinxhyphen{}tripping tends to need: the delimiter, the missing\sphinxhyphen{}value marker, whether the
case axis should be exported as a real column, numeric formatting, quoting rules, line
endings, and text encoding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single detail worth deciding deliberately every time: \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}}. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
(the effective default via the filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only overload), the file contains only the
frame’s ordinary features — reloading it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}} gives you back a frame with a
fresh, auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..N\sphinxhyphen{}1}} case index, not the original one. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the current
case axis is written out as its own leading column (named via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}, or a default
name if you leave it unset), so a later \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv(..., case\_col = \textless{}that name\textgreater{})}} can
restore the exact case labels the frame had when it was saved.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{add\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the case axis is exported as its own column so case labels survive a
save/load round trip. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, only the ordinary features are written.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to write feature names as the first line of the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Field delimiter to write between values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{null\_rep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The literal text written for a missing value. The default is an empty field; pass
something like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NA"}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} if the consuming system needs missing values to be
visually unambiguous rather than an empty CSV field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column name to use for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases=true}}. Leave unset
to use a default name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{float\_format} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fmt}}\sphinxhyphen{}style format string applied to every floating\sphinxhyphen{}point value written. Leave unset
to use the library’s default numeric formatting (enough significant digits to round\sphinxhyphen{}trip
typical values without excess trailing digits).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{quotechar} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}"\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Character used to quote fields that contain the delimiter, the quote character itself,
or a line break.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{doublequote} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, an embedded quote character inside a field is escaped by doubling it
(standard CSV quoting); when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a different escaping convention is used instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{line\_terminator} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textbackslash{}n"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Line ending written between rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{decimal} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}.\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Decimal point character used when formatting floating\sphinxhyphen{}point values — set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}} for
locales that expect a comma decimal separator (note this then requires a non\sphinxhyphen{}comma
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{};\textquotesingle{}}}, to keep fields unambiguous).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{encoding} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"utf\sphinxhyphen{}8"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Text encoding used when writing the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::WriteCsvOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent settings expressed as a reusable config object, inline entries, or a typed
options struct, for callers who prefer not to spell out every positional parameter at
the call site.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing. Inspect the file on disk (or catch an
exception from the loader layer on a write failure) to confirm the result — there is
no in\sphinxhyphen{}memory object to print afterward.
