\sphinxAtStartPar
No case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column is written — reloading this file gives back a frame with a fresh
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2}} index rather than whatever case labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} had before saving (in this
example, they happen to coincide, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} itself uses the default index).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Export the case axis as its own named column.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}case.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*add\PYGZus{}cases=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*header=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{,}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{c+cm}{/*null\PYGZus{}rep=*/}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*case\PYGZus{}label=*/}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_with\_case.csv}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
case\PYGZus{}id,order\PYGZus{}id,city,units
0,101,Accra,2
1,102,Tema,1
2,103,Kumasi,4
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading this file back with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_csv("orders\_with\_case.csv", \textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}, std::nullopt, std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\{\}, std::string\{"case\_id"\})}}
restores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_id}} as the case axis instead of leaving it as an ordinary feature.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv}} never mutates the frame it is called on — it is a pure side\sphinxhyphen{}effecting write.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing values are written as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} (an empty field by default), never as the
literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} unless you set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} to that string explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float\_format}} when downstream tooling expects a fixed number of decimal places
(for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{:.2f\}"}} for currency\sphinxhyphen{}style output) instead of the default
significant\sphinxhyphen{}digits formatting.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a single worksheet of an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xlsx}} workbook. The sheet name defaults
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Sheet1"}} unless you supply one (via the positional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}} parameter, or the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}} field of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}). As with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}, the case axis
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} written as its own column unless \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} is turned on.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xlsx}} path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, positional overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Sheet1"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name of the worksheet to write within the workbook.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{add\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the case axis is exported as its own leading column, named via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} (or a default name if left unset) — the same convention
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} uses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to write feature names as the sheet’s first row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{null\_rep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Literal text written for a missing cell. Default is an empty cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column name for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases=true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::WriteExcelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent settings expressed as a reusable config object, inline entries, or the typed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} struct — recognizing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} (also
accepted under the legacy alias \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}})/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} fields as the
positional overload.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:examples}}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}out.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_out.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sheet1}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

| 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Save to a named sheet and export the case axis as its own column.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}case.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Orders}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*add\PYGZus{}cases=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                   }\PYG{c+cm}{/*header=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*null\PYGZus{}rep=*/}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*case\PYGZus{}label=*/}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_with\_case.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Orders}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
| case\PYGZus{}id | id  | city   | units |
| 0       | 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 1       | 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 2       | 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading this back with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_excel("orders\_with\_case.xlsx", "Orders")}} followed by treating
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_id}} as the case column (via a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadExcelOptions}} case\sphinxhyphen{}column setting)
restores the original case labels, the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}} pair does.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Save with a typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} struct.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WriteExcelOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sheet\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Regions}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}options.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_options.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Regions}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
| case | id  | city   | units |
| 0    | 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 1    | 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 2    | 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} wasn’t set here, the exported case column falls back to its default
name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one sheet is written per call — there’s no multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet write overload the way
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}} has multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet \sphinxstyleemphasis{read} overloads. Writing several
sheets into one workbook means saving to the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filepath}} multiple times with
different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}}s and workbook\sphinxhyphen{}append handling managed at the file\sphinxhyphen{}format
level, not through a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_excel()}} call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} mirror {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s convention exactly —
the case axis is opt\sphinxhyphen{}in, not written by default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} under the legacy field name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}} as well,
for compatibility with older call sites.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a JSON file, in one of three layouts controlled by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orient}}
config key:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}} (the default) — a JSON array of one object per case, each keyed by
feature name. This is also the layout {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} reads most
naturally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}}} — a single JSON object keyed by feature name, each value a JSON
array of that feature’s values across every case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}}} — a single JSON object with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}} array of feature names and a
parallel \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"data"}} array of row arrays. This is the other layout
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} recognizes on read.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output is pretty\sphinxhyphen{}printed with a 2\sphinxhyphen{}space indent by default; set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty=false}} for
compact, single\sphinxhyphen{}line output.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Recognized keys:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orient}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}} — see “What It Does” above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): whether to add newlines and indentation.
Passing an integer instead of a bool also works — any value greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} is
treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indent}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json\_indent}}} (integer, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}): number of spaces
per indent level, when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty}} is on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}):
export the case axis as its own field/column, the same convention
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} uses.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indexlabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): field name
for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}} is enabled.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}} is both the default write orientation and one of the two layouts
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}detects on read; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}} is the other.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}} is write\sphinxhyphen{}only — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}} does not currently parse a bare
column\sphinxhyphen{}keyed object back into a frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty=false}} for compact output with no added whitespace, useful when file
size matters more than human readability.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}} follow the same convention as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} — export the case axis as its own field so a later
reload can restore it.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a Parquet file via Apache Arrow’s Parquet C++ library —
compact, columnar, typed storage, the write\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires an Arrow + Parquet C++ build
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}} throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“built without parquet\sphinxhyphen{}cpp support”}
if PlussMic was compiled without the optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSSMIC\_HAS\_PARQUET\_CPP}} dependency.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination Parquet file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Recognized keys:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}):
export the case axis as its own column, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} convention.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indexlabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): column
name for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when the flag above is enabled.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Save with the plain filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only overload — no case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires PlussMic to have been built with Arrow + Parquet C++ support, exactly like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}}; otherwise every call throws immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}} follow the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}}’s equivalent fields.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are written using Arrow’s own Parquet type mapping from PlussMic’s inferred
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} dtypes — but recall from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}} that
reading the file back re\sphinxhyphen{}infers types from stringified values rather than trusting
the Parquet schema directly, so a save/load round trip is not guaranteed to preserve
the exact original precision (for example, a narrower integer width).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_parquet}}}}}}}: the read\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart, including
the schema\sphinxhyphen{}discarding re\sphinxhyphen{}inference behavior worth knowing about before round\sphinxhyphen{}tripping.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_csv}}}}}}}: the analogous CSV writer and the fuller
explanation of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} convention shared across writers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_as}}}}}}}: the format\sphinxhyphen{}switched entry point that can
dispatch to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}} via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type = "parquet"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a delimited text file — internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}} is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} with one difference: if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}} doesn’t explicitly
set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}, the field delimiter defaults to a tab (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}t\textquotesingle{}}})
instead of a comma. Every other writing behavior (missing\sphinxhyphen{}value representation,
quoting, encoding) is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle, recognizing the same keys
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overload does (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullrep}}, and so on).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} share the exact same writer; the only
difference is the tab\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}comma default delimiter, and only when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}} isn’t set
explicitly in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no dedicated positional overload the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}} has — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}
for anything beyond the plain filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The read\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}}}}}}}, does \sphinxstylestrong{not} default to a
tab separator — you must specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}} explicitly when reading a file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}}
wrote with its tab default.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose running/cumulative\sphinxhyphen{}statistic engine behind
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} — each of those four is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} with one fixed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Sum, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Product, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Minimum, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Maximum, ...)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} directly when you want to select the statistic dynamically (as a
variable rather than a fixed call name); reach for the four named convenience
methods otherwise, since they read more clearly at the call site.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which running statistic to compute down (or across) each numeric feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic::Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to accumulate along. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) runs down each feature’s
cases; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} accumulates across a row’s features left to right instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what happens once a null is encountered — identical semantics to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a null produces a null only at that case; the running
statistic is preserved underneath it and resumes normally at the next observed
value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first null poisons every case after it, all the way to the end of
that feature.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by
its running \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{statistic}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running statistic; it
does not add a new column alongside the original.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic::Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} are the only four supported
statistics; there is no running mean or running standard deviation available
through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:dataframe-se}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:signature}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{se}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ErrorTarget}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ErrorTarget}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to the standard error of its mean (SEM) — the sample
standard deviation divided by the square root of the observation count,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(variance / n)}}. This measures how precisely each feature’s sample mean
estimates the true population mean; a smaller \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{se()}} means the mean is measured with
more precision (either lower spread, more observations, or both).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Mean}} is currently supported — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}} exists as a forward\sphinxhyphen{}looking
parameter, and passing anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::se: only ErrorTarget::Mean is currently supported"}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one standard error per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s
features instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which statistic’s standard error to compute. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Mean}} is currently
implemented.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const StatisticOptions\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same structured policy {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}} accept:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): delta\sphinxhyphen{}degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom subtracted in the
underlying variance’s divisor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} is the sample variance feeding this
standard error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null
observations a feature needs before it gets a real result rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding
that feature’s standard error of the mean.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  0.7637626158
     units  0.6009252126
unit\PYGZus{}price  259.6124997
  discount  0.01378404875
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each entry is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(variance / n)}} using {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}}’s own results on this
identical dataset: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}’s variance is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5}} over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} observations, so its
standard error is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(3.5 / 6) ≈ 0.7638}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} each have one
missing observation (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}), so their standard errors divide by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(336993.25 / 5) ≈ 259.61}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/se:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{se()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, the same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}}’s results.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with fewer than two observed values has an undefined sample variance
(and therefore an undefined standard error) and reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, independent of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Mean}} is currently supported; passing any other target throws.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/select:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A static factory that builds a new frame by choosing, case by case, which candidate
frame’s row to use — the row\sphinxhyphen{}wise analogue of a chained if/else\sphinxhyphen{}if/else across several
whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}s at once. For every case (row), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} walks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}} \sphinxstylestrong{in
order} and uses the row from the first candidate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices{[}i{]}}} whose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions{[}i{]}}}
is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for that case; if none of the conditions are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for a case, that case’s
row comes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}} instead. The same set of conditions is applied
identically across every feature, so a single call reshuffles an entire frame’s worth
of columns in one pass rather than one feature at a time.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not an instance method — there is no frame to call it “on”. You supply
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}} up front, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} assembles the
result from scratch. Because of this, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} was previously missing from this
reference entirely; the header parser that catalogs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s methods didn’t
recognize this static, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}\sphinxhyphen{}based factory as a documentable method the way it
recognizes ordinary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} member functions. That gap is fixed here, but it’s worth
flagging as a real coverage hole in the automated tooling, not just a documentation
oversight.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Priority is positional: the first true condition wins
If more than one condition is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for the same case, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions{[}0{]}}}’s choice wins
— \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} does not use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} matching condition, and it does not merge or
average competing choices. See Example 2 for a worked demonstration where deliberately
overlapping conditions produce different results depending on which one is listed
first.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/select:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{conditions} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView::Of\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An ordered, non\sphinxhyphen{}empty list of boolean masks, one per candidate in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}}. Each
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} must be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}scalar\sphinxhyphen{}type thread with one value per case —
the same requirement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}} place on their operands (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} must have the same length; each
position pairs one condition with the candidate frame it “unlocks.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{choices} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView::Of\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One candidate frame per condition, evaluated in the same order as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}}. Every
choice must \sphinxstylestrong{exactly} match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}}’s case count, feature count, feature
names (in the same order), case labels, and structured case\sphinxhyphen{}axis metadata — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}
does not align or reorder candidates for you first. Only the participating \sphinxstyleemphasis{cell
values} are allowed to differ between candidates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{default\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame supplying both the fallback row for any case where no condition is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}},
and the structural template (feature names, order, case labels, case\sphinxhyphen{}axis metadata)
that every entry in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} is checked against.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/select:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}}’s structure (feature names and order, case
labels, title, case\sphinxhyphen{}axis metadata) and, for every case, the cell values pulled
from the first candidate in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} whose matching condition is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — or from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}} itself if no condition matched that case.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/select:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::select()}} this delegates to internally, the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} does \sphinxstylestrong{not} support scalar\sphinxhyphen{}like (single\sphinxhyphen{}row)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}} — every choice’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} must exactly match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value.ncases()}}. Broadcasting a single\sphinxhyphen{}row candidate across every case is a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::select()}}\sphinxhyphen{}only capability.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} entry is checked against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_value}} for feature names (in
order), case count, case labels, and case\sphinxhyphen{}axis metadata, and throws if any of them
disagree — quoting the exact checks: \sphinxstyleemphasis{“all choices must match default feature
order”}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{“all choices must match default case labels”}, and \sphinxstyleemphasis{“all choices must
match default structured case metadata”}. Only cell values may differ between
candidates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choices}} must have the same length, and at least one condition is
required — an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conditions}} list throws (\sphinxstyleemphasis{“at least one condition is
required”}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each condition \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} must be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — the same constraint
documented on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}. A numeric 0/1 column is rejected, not treated as
truthy.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same condition list drives every feature identically — there is no per\sphinxhyphen{}feature
condition list the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload has an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} choice.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{caution}{Caution:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A generator/coverage gap, not just a documentation gap
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} had no generated page at all prior to this entry — every other
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} method, even undocumented ones, at least had an auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated stub. If
you add other static, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}\sphinxhyphen{}based factory methods to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} in the future,
verify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{generate\_api\_reference.py}} actually discovers them before assuming a missing
page means the method doesn’t exist.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adds a new feature or replaces an existing one’s values, in two distinct styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.set(name) = value}} builder style} (the no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads):
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(name)}} returns a lightweight \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}} proxy bound to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}; assigning a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, or even a
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} to that proxy \sphinxstylestrong{mutates the calling frame in place} —
creating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} if it doesn’t already exist, or overwriting it if it does.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(\{"a", "b"\}) = \{...\}}} is the same idea for several features assigned together
in one batch (at most one reindex pass, rather than one per feature). A
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} right\sphinxhyphen{}hand side broadcasts a single scalar to every row.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The plain two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(name, value)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(names, values)}}):
ordinary, non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating functions that return a \sphinxstylestrong{new} frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}
created or replaced, leaving \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} untouched — the same convention as
every other non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_}}\sphinxhyphen{}suffixed method in this reference.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_(name, value)}}}}}}} is the mutating counterpart to the plain two\sphinxhyphen{}argument
overloads specifically — a third way to write “mutate in place” alongside the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlots}} builder style described above.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} / \sphinxstylestrong{names}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature name (or names) to create or overwrite.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} / \sphinxstylestrong{values}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement data. For the builder style, anything assignable to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, or a
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}); for the plain overloads, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (or a matching range
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}s for the multi\sphinxhyphen{}name overload).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a right\sphinxhyphen{}hand \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis when it
doesn’t already match exactly.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlots}}
A proxy bound to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}; assigning to it performs the mutation and creates or
overwrites the named feature(s) in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(Plain two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads) A new frame with the named feature(s) created or
replaced.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlots}}\sphinxhyphen{}returning overloads (no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} argument) are the only
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(...)}} calls that mutate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}; every overload that takes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}
directly as an argument is a plain, non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating function.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assigning a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}} broadcasts a single scalar to every row —
useful for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.set("flag") = ThreadValue(true)}}\sphinxhyphen{}style constant columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch\sphinxhyphen{}assigning with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(\{"a", "b"\}) = \{...\}}} performs at most one schema
reindex pass total, rather than one per feature — prefer it over several separate
single\sphinxhyphen{}name assignments when setting many features at once.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}}’s plain two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads:
creates or overwrites the named feature(s), mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly and returning
a reference to it, instead of returning a new frame. Every parameter is identical in
meaning to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}’s corresponding overload — see that page for the full breakdown;
this page only covers what differs about mutating in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note this is a \sphinxstylestrong{third} way to write “assign in place” in this API, alongside
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}}’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.set(name) = value}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}} builder style — both mutate
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, they just read differently at the call site. Pick whichever reads better;
neither is more “correct” than the other.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} / \sphinxstylestrong{names}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature name (or names) to create or overwrite in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} / \sphinxstylestrong{values}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (or a matching range of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}s for the multi\sphinxhyphen{}name
overload).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis when it doesn’t already
match exactly, identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with the named feature(s) created or overwritten.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/set_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_()}} mutates and returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} by reference; it never allocates a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}’s plain overload does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} value that shares the same underlying columns (via a prior
copy) does not see this mutation — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrame}}’s copies are
value\sphinxhyphen{}like, not aliased references to shared state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}} for the complete parameter breakdown and for the separate
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlots}} builder style (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.set(name) = value}}), which also mutates in
place but is a distinct code path from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_()}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::set}}}}}}}: the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating counterpart, plus the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LetSlot}}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::shape}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:dataframe-shape}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the frame’s dimensions as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(cases, features)}} pair — the row count first, then
the column count. It is the cheapest possible way to answer “how big is this frame”
without printing the frame itself or walking any column data: both numbers come directly
from the frame’s existing bookkeeping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape()}} is most useful as a quick assertion or log line in the middle of a pipeline —
confirming a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}} produced the row count you expected, or that a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} actually
narrowed anything — without the cost or noise of a full {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/show::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::pair\textless{}std::int64\_t, std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}
The first element is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} (row count); the second is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} (column
count). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::pair}} has no built\sphinxhyphen{}in stream operator, so print the two numbers
yourself (see the example) rather than trying to stream the pair directly.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shape:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape().first == ncases()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape().second == nfeatures()}} always — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape()}} is
a convenience pairing of those two accessors, not a separately computed value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape()}} reads existing metadata rather than scanning column data, calling it
repeatedly (for logging, assertions, or loop conditions) costs essentially nothing.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::shift}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift:dataframe-shift}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifts each selected feature’s values down (or up) by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions along the
case axis — case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s new value becomes whatever was at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i \sphinxhyphen{} periods}} before
the shift, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} filling in the positions that have no source row to pull
from. This is the standard “lag/lead” primitive: a positive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} produces a lag
(each row now shows an earlier row’s value; the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} rows become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}),
a negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} produces a lead (each row shows a later row’s value; the last
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|periods|}} rows become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload shifts every feature; the range overload restricts the
shift to the named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, leaving every other feature completely untouched.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How many positions to shift by. Positive values move values downward (lag):
case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} becomes case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i \sphinxhyphen{} periods}}’s old value, and the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} rows become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Negative values move values upward (lead), with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} filling the last
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|periods|}} rows instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features to shift. Only present on the range overload; every feature not
listed here is left completely unchanged. Omitting this argument entirely (the

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} (not the default) or an empty frame both return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} unchanged
rather than doing any work.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift()}} never reorders case labels — only the feature values move; the case
axis stays exactly as it was.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifting a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature fills the vacated positions with a missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}})
text value, the same missing\sphinxhyphen{}value convention used across every other kind.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/show:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prints the frame’s rendered text — the exact same box\sphinxhyphen{}table text
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/to_string::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_string()}}}}}}} produce — with a trailing newline
appended. The two overloads differ in where the output goes and, subtly, in whether
plain text is guaranteed at all:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show(os, options)}}} (explicit stream): always writes plain text —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os \textless{}\textless{} render(*this, options) \textless{}\textless{} \textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}n\textquotesingle{}}} — to whatever stream you pass. This is the
deterministic, always\sphinxhyphen{}plain\sphinxhyphen{}text overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show(options)}}} (no stream): resolves a display \sphinxstyleemphasis{backend} first. In a plain
terminal context, this also prints plain text to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}}. But if a GUI/web
viewer backend is resolved instead (depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.mode}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.backend}}
and the environment), it opens a native or HTML viewer window and \sphinxstylestrong{does not}
print anything to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} at all.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/show:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const display::DisplayOptions\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rendering and backend options — terminal width/height overrides, footer/case\sphinxhyphen{}index
visibility toggles, HTML viewer sizing, and a window title. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.mode}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.backend}} are what decide whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show(options)}} (no stream) prints plain
text or opens a viewer window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{os} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::ostream\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The destination stream for the explicit\sphinxhyphen{}stream overload. Always receives plain text
regardless of any backend setting.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/show:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the print (or opens a viewer window); no value is returned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show(os, options)}} is the reliable, deterministic overload for capturing or
redirecting output — it never opens a viewer window regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show(options)}} (no stream) may open a GUI or HTML viewer window instead of
printing to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}}, depending on the resolved display backend — do not rely on
it always producing text on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} in every environment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_string()}} returns the identical rendered text as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, without any
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show()}}’s stream\sphinxhyphen{}writing or backend\sphinxhyphen{}resolution behavior — reach for it when you
want the text itself rather than a printing side effect.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::shuffle}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:dataframe-shuffle}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{uint64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomly permutes row (case) order, leaving the feature order and every value
untouched. It is exactly {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Case, random\_state)}}}}}}} under
a more discoverable name — reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}} whenever “randomly reorder the
rows” is literally what you mean, which covers the large majority of cases
(breaking up incidental ordering before sampling, building a randomized train/test
split, and so on); reach for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}}}}}}} directly only when you
specifically need to permute the \sphinxstyleemphasis{feature} axis instead.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::uint64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A seed for reproducible shuffling. Omit it (the default) for a non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic
shuffle seeded from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}}}}}}}’s Notes
for why a given seed’s exact resulting permutation is not portable across builds.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same feature set and the same per\sphinxhyphen{}row values, in a
permuted row order.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
3
true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffled}} still has all \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} original rows — re\sphinxhyphen{}sorting it back by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} ascending
reproduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} exactly. As with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}}}}}}}, the specific row
order a given \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} produces depends on the standard library’s own
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} implementation, so it isn’t asserted here as a fixed, portable
sequence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. The same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} reproduces the same permutation within one build.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{second}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{equals}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{second}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two calls with the identical seed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}} produce the identical row order on the same
build — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}} is deterministic given a fixed seed, even though the exact
permutation itself is not part of this API’s portable contract.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}} never changes the feature order or any cell’s value — only row
position moves.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Omitting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} draws a fresh seed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} each call, so
two unseeded calls essentially never produce the same order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle(random\_state)}} is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Case, random\_state)}};
pick whichever name reads better at the call site.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::reshuffle}}}}}}}: the general form, supporting the feature
axis as well.

\item {}

permuting the full set.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::skew}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:dataframe-skew}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its (bias\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted) sample skewness — a measure of how
asymmetric the distribution of values is around its mean — returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose
entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names, the same shape
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}} return. A skewness of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} describes a
symmetric distribution; a positive value describes a right (long upper) tail; a
negative value describes a left (long lower) tail. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are skipped
entirely.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nulls are always excluded from the underlying moment computation regardless of any
parameter — there is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} toggle here, because skewness has a stricter
statistical floor instead: a feature needs at least \sphinxstylestrong{three} observed values before a
skewness is even mathematically defined (a sample of one or two points has no
meaningful notion of asymmetry). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} lets you raise that floor further, but it
can never lower it below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one skewness value per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s
features instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations a feature must have before it is assigned
a real skewness value at all. Passing a value below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} has no effect — the method
always enforces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(3, min\_count)}} — but passing a larger value raises the bar: a
feature with fewer than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} observations reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} even if it has the
statistically\sphinxhyphen{}required minimum of three.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s sample skewness.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the skewness of every numeric feature, the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness}\PYG{p}{;}
