\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  0
     units  0.4180715203
unit\PYGZus{}price  0.4534323226
  discount  0.256139086
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} because its six values are evenly spaced — a perfectly
symmetric run with no skew. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} are all positive
because each has a handful of low values pulled up by one or two much larger ones (a
right tail), computed over the observed values only: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s missing case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}}’s missing case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) are excluded from the moment computation, the same
null\sphinxhyphen{}handling every other statistic in this family applies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} above the statistical floor to require every case be
present.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  0
     units  0.4180715203
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} have all six values observed, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 6}} doesn’t change
their result. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} each have only five observed values — one
short of the demanded six — so both report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, even though five values is well
above the statistical minimum of three.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. See the hard floor in effect: a two\sphinxhyphen{}case frame can never produce a
skewness, no matter what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} is passed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness\PYGZus{}too\PYGZus{}small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skewness\PYGZus{}too\PYGZus{}small}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  NULL
     units  NULL
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature has at most two observed values in this two\sphinxhyphen{}case slice, below the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(3, min\_count)}} floor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}} always enforces — so every feature comes back
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, independent of what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} you pass.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither computed as an
error nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature whose values have zero variance (every observed value identical) reports a
skewness of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} rather than an undefined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0/0}} — the implementation detects a
zero second moment and short\sphinxhyphen{}circuits to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} instead of propagating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the corresponding measure of tail weight rather than asymmetry, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kurtosis()}}}}}}}, which shares the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} shape (with a
floor of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/skew:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/kurtosis::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::kurtosis}}}}}}}: the tail\sphinxhyphen{}weight counterpart to this measure of
asymmetry.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::std}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::var}}}}}}}: the second\sphinxhyphen{}moment statistics
this method’s third moment builds on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe}}}}}}}: a broader summary that does not include skew or
kurtosis, for those on a tighter statistical budget.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::slice}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:dataframe-slice}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stop}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a contiguous positional case range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} — every row from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} up
to, but not including, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. Both endpoints support Python\sphinxhyphen{}style negative indices
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means “the last case,” \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}} the second\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}last, and so on), and both are clamped
into range rather than raising, so it is always safe to pass generous or approximate
bounds. Case labels on the result are preserved exactly as they were on the source
frame — a slice never renumbers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(indices)}} for the computed contiguous index
range, so its result\sphinxhyphen{}shape guarantees (feature order, dtypes, case labels) are
identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}’s.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first case position to include. A negative value is interpreted relative to the
end of the frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last case), then the whole result is clamped into
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, ncases(){]}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case position to stop before (exclusive). Negative values are normalized the same
way as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}. If the normalized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} ends up before the normalized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, the
result is an empty (zero\sphinxhyphen{}case) frame rather than an error.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame holding the cases in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}}, in their original order, with
every feature and the source frame’s original case labels preserved.

having to know or compute the frame’s exact length first.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}} never renumbers case labels; the result carries the source frame’s
original labels for the surviving rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both endpoints are clamped, never an error — an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} degrades
gracefully instead of throwing, unlike a single out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range position passed to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}, which does raise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For “from the top” or “from the bottom” shortcuts, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}} read more clearly than an equivalent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}} call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an arbitrary (non\sphinxhyphen{}contiguous, reorderable, repeatable) set of positions, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}} instead.

\end{itemize}

\item {}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reorders the cases of a frame using one or more feature values as sort keys, and returns
the reordered frame. Every feature is carried along unchanged — only case order moves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two overloads cover the two shapes this need usually takes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{simple overload} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}) sorts by a list of
feature names with one shared direction and one shared null\sphinxhyphen{}placement policy applied
to every key. Reach for this when every sort key should behave the same way, for
example “sort by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{product}}, both ascending.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ArrangeSpec}} overload} sorts by an explicit list of per\sphinxhyphen{}column specs, each of
which can set its own direction and null\sphinxhyphen{}placement independently. Reach for this when
different keys need different treatment, for example “\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} descending, but
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} ascending, with nulls always sorted last regardless of key.”

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}ArrangeSpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An ordered collection of per\sphinxhyphen{}feature sort specifications. Earlier specs take priority
over later ones — ties on the first spec’s feature are broken by the second spec, and so
on, the same way a SQL \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY a DESC, b ASC}} works. Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ArrangeSpec}} typically
carries a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} name plus its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}} flags (see the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ArrangeSpec}} aggregate initializer in the example below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to sort by, in priority order, for the simple overload. All of them share
the single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}} policy passed alongside them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies to every key in the simple overload. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} sorts smallest/earliest values
first; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} reverses the order, largest/latest first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies to every key in the simple overload. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} places rows with a null in the sort
key after every row with an observed value for that key; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} places null rows first
instead.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same features and dtypes, reordered by the requested sort
keys. Case labels travel with their row, so a row’s case label after sorting is
still whatever it was on the source frame — only the row’s position changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Look at the leftmost, blank\sphinxhyphen{}header case\sphinxhyphen{}index column: it now reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5}}
instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}}. That column is the original case label traveling with each
row — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} reordered the rows, it did not relabel or renumber them. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}
(the missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}) sorted to the very end even in descending order, because
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last=true}} places null keys after every observed value regardless of sort
direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Sort by two keys with independent directions using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ArrangeSpec}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{by\PYGZus{}city\PYGZus{}then\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{ArrangeSpec}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{ArrangeSpec}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nulls\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows are grouped by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} alphabetically first (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}}), and within
each city group, ordered by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} from highest to lowest. This is the shape to
reach for whenever a “sort ascending” and a “sort descending” need to happen in the same
call — the simple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} overload cannot express mixed directions across keys.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} is a stable\sphinxhyphen{}feeling composition point: it reads naturally as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.sort\_values(...).head(3)}} for “top 3 by X,” or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.filter(mask).sort\_values(...)}} for “sort only the rows that matched.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simple overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}} apply identically to \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature
in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}. If even one key needs a different policy, use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ArrangeSpec}}
overload instead of trying to work around the shared\sphinxhyphen{}policy limitation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} does not deduplicate ties — rows with equal sort\sphinxhyphen{}key values keep their
relative source order (a stable sort), which matters when you chain multiple keys or
rely on tie order downstream.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::rank}}}}}}}: compute each row’s rank within a feature instead of
reordering the frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::head}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tail}}}}}}}: commonly chained after
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} to get a “top N” or “bottom N” slice.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::filter}}}}}}}: narrow down rows
before or after sorting.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::sql}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:dataframe-sql}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlAccessor}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SqlOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the frame’s built\sphinxhyphen{}in SQL accessor — a small, self\sphinxhyphen{}contained SQL engine that
runs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} statements directly against the frame (referenced in the statement as
the source table \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self}}), returning an ordinary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} result. Use this when a
transformation reads more naturally as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}} statement
than as a chained sequence of table verbs. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}} itself does no work beyond binding
the frame (and, optionally, execution \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}); the real work happens on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(statement)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql(statement)}}}}}}} is the sibling entry point for a statement
that will run many times with different bound parameter values — it parses the
statement once up front, rather than on every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute()}} call the way
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql().execute(statement)}} does each time it’s called fresh.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Execution options for the returned accessor: additional joinable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}}, default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{...\}}}\sphinxhyphen{}style placeholders, missing\sphinxhyphen{}parameter and
name\sphinxhyphen{}collision policies, row/memory/timeout limits, and diagnostics toggles. Omit it
entirely to use every default.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor}}
An accessor bound to the current frame (and, if given, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}). Call
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(statement)}} on it to parse and run a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} statement, returning a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Run a filtering \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} statement with the default options.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{120.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{90.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}sales}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SELECT id, sales FROM self WHERE sales \PYGZgt{} 95}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}sales}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==================
     | id    sales
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 1     100  
1    | 2     120  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[2 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} clause behaves like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}}}}}}’s filtering — case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales = 90}}) doesn’t satisfy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales \textgreater{} 95}}, so it’s dropped, while cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}
survive with their original case labels intact. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT id, sales}} projection
means \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} never appears in the result at all.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Pass an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{param\}}} placeholder value through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{SqlOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{target\PYGZus{}city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{matched}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sql}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SELECT * FROM self WHERE city = \PYGZob{}target\PYGZus{}city\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{matched}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
========================
     | id    sales  city
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
1    | 2     120    Tema
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[1 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{target\_city\}}} is substituted with the quoted string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}Tema\textquotesingle{}}} before the statement
runs, matching only case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT *}} keeps every column this time, unlike Example
1’s explicit projection.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}} returns the accessor only; it never executes a statement by itself — you
must call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(statement)}} to get a result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The calling frame is always available in the statement as the source table
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.sources}} can bind additional named frames for joins.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prep\_sql(statement)}}}}}}} instead when the same statement text runs
repeatedly with different parameter bindings, to avoid re\sphinxhyphen{}parsing it every time.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sql:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/prep_sql::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::prep\_sql}}}}}}}: the reusable, parse\sphinxhyphen{}once counterpart for a
statement executed many times with changing parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query}}}}}}}: a lighter\sphinxhyphen{}weight boolean\sphinxhyphen{}expression filter, for
when a full SQL statement is more machinery than the task needs.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::stack}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:dataframe-stack}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{stack}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{feature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{value}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Melts \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the frame into long format in one call: each original
case gets one output row per original feature, with a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}} column
recording which feature that row came from and a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}} column holding
the corresponding stacked value. The original case index (or, if the frame already
has named case labels, every one of those levels) and the new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}} column
together become the result’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stack()}} promotes them there rather
than leaving them as ordinary columns, which is what distinguishes it from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lengthen()}}}}}}} (a more configurable melt that keeps its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features}}
as plain columns and lets you choose a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_features}} subset instead of always
stacking everything).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because every feature’s values get concatenated together into one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}}
column, every feature on the frame must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind (and, for
numeric features, the same concrete dtype) — the same constraint
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lengthen()}}}}}}} places on its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_features}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"feature"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name of the new column (well, case\sphinxhyphen{}label level) recording each output row’s source
feature name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name of the new column holding each output row’s stacked value. Must differ from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases() * nfeatures()}} rows and a single remaining feature,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}}. The original case index and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}} are promoted into the
result’s (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis rather than kept as ordinary columns.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature on the source frame must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind (and, for
numeric features, the same concrete scalar dtype and platform), since their values
are concatenated into one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}} column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the source frame already has named case labels, every one of those levels is
carried into the result’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis alongside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}} — not just a
single default position column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lengthen()}}}}}}} instead when you want some columns to stay
as identifying features rather than being folded into the case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis, or when
only a subset of features should be stacked.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its standard deviation, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose
entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} return. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are skipped
entirely rather than coerced into a statistic that wouldn’t mean anything.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default this is the \sphinxstylestrong{sample} standard deviation: the sum of squared deviations from
the mean is divided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}, the conventional correction for
estimating a population’s spread from a finite sample. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload
lets you override that divisor explicitly via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} when you need the \sphinxstylestrong{population}
standard deviation instead (divide by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}), or require a minimum number of observations
before a feature’s result counts as valid.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one standard deviation per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s
features instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that feature’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded from the computation entirely, so
the standard deviation reflects only the observed values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value in a feature poisons that feature’s result, which comes
back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const StatisticOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A structured policy for the same reduction, exposing two fields the short overload
cannot reach:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the delta\sphinxhyphen{}degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom subtracted from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
in the divisor. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (the default under either overload) is the sample standard
deviation; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} is the population standard deviation, dividing by the full
observed count instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations
a feature must have before it is assigned a real result at all; a feature with fewer
observed values than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s standard deviation.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.870828693
     units  1.471960144
unit\PYGZus{}price  580.5111971
  discount  0.03082207001
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s one missing observation (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is excluded from the computation
entirely — its standard deviation is computed over the remaining five values, the same
way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} treat that column’s missing
value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.870828693
     units  1.471960144
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} — the two features that each have
exactly one missing value — come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, with no
missing values, are unaffected either way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload to compute the population standard
deviation instead of the sample standard deviation.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ddof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread\PYGZus{}population}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread\PYGZus{}population}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.707825128
     units  1.343709625
unit\PYGZus{}price  519.2249994
  discount  0.0275680975
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every value is slightly smaller than in Example 1: dividing by the full observed count
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}}) instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}}, the implicit default) always produces a
standard deviation that is less than or equal to the sample statistic. Reach for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} when the data in hand \sphinxstylestrong{is} the entire population of interest, not a sample
drawn from a larger one.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/std:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}},
not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither computed as an error
nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with fewer than two observed values has an undefined sample standard
deviation and reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, independent of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the corresponding variance (the squared statistic, no square root applied), see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}}, which shares the exact same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}}
shape.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise subtraction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}} shares the exact same
overload shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}, and the rest of the arithmetic family — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s
“What It Does” for the full explanation of the scalar/frame/Thread operand shapes and
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters. Unlike addition, subtraction is not commutative, so
operand order matters: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a.sub(b)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a \sphinxhyphen{} b}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b \sphinxhyphen{} a}}. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}} when you specifically want \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other \sphinxhyphen{} a}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}’s shape driving
the result.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, subtracted from the current frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast
scalar), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast
per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}: controls alignment and missing\sphinxhyphen{}value
handling for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overloads.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature reduced by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{DataFrame::sum}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:dataframe-sum}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to a single total, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose entries
line up with the frame’s numeric feature names — a column\sphinxhyphen{}wise sum, one number per
feature. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) are skipped entirely
rather than coerced into a total that wouldn’t mean anything.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note the return type: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. It behaves like a
labeled, one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional result — printed the way a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} prints, with each
feature name as its row label and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype:}} footer — not like the boxed, multi\sphinxhyphen{}column
table that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}returning methods produce.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) sums down each feature’s cases,
producing one total per feature — this is the usual reading, and the one shown below.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} sums across each row’s features instead, producing one total per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that feature’s total:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are ignored; the total is the sum of whatever was
actually observed for that feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value in a feature poisons that feature’s entire total,
which comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s total.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Sum every numeric feature, skipping missing values (the default).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{totals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{totals}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  621
     units  17
unit\PYGZus{}price  2757.5
  discount  0.4
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s total (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2757.5}}) is the sum of its five \sphinxstyleemphasis{observed} values — case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}’s
missing entry simply didn’t contribute, rather than forcing the whole total to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, which have no missing values, sum normally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{totals\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{totals\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  621
     units  17
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} — the two features that each
have exactly one missing value — come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely, because at least one input
to their total was missing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} are unaffected, since neither had any
missing values to begin with.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}’s result is labeled by feature name, not by case — printing it looks like a
small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result at all; they are not summed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or
reported as an error, they are simply absent from the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a summary that also frees you from committing to one specific statistic, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}}, which reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum}}\sphinxhyphen{}adjacent statistics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}},
quartiles) all at once.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::tabelize}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:dataframe-tabelize}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{static}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{tabelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Catalog}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{k}{static}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{tabelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Catalog}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TabelizePolicy}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{policy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reverse of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindelize()}}}}}}}: rebuilds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} from a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::kindle::Catalog}}’s keyed collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}s, aligning them back into one
shared table. Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} key becomes one output feature, keyed by that same
name; the frame’s case labels are reconstructed from the streams’ own attached
labels according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{policy}}. This is a \sphinxstylestrong{static} factory method — call it as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tabelize(catalog)}}, not on an existing frame instance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When every stream in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{catalog}} already carries the exact same set of case labels
(as is true right after {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindelize()}}}}}}} with its default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{attach\_labels = true}}), the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TabelizePolicy}} reconstructs the original frame
exactly — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tabelize()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindelize()}} round\sphinxhyphen{}trip.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{catalog} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::kindle::Catalog\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The catalog to convert. Must be a defined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}; an undefined one throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::tabelize requires a defined Catalog"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{policy} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::kindle::TabelizePolicy\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how streams are aligned back into one shared table when their label sets
don’t already match exactly. Key fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Align}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inner}}): how to reconcile streams whose label sets
differ — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inner}} (only labels common to every stream), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}} (exactly one
stream’s labels), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Outer}} (union of every stream’s labels), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Strict}} (every
stream’s labels must already match the anchor exactly).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_by}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Label}}): align by label value, or by plain
position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pos}}) — falls back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pos}} automatically if any stream lacks labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FillPolicy}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Null}}): how to fill a cell with no matching
source row — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Null}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_scalar}}, or forward/backward fill.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_label\_feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, also adds the
reconstructed case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread as its own extra feature, named by
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"label"}}).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one feature per catalog key (in the catalog’s key order), plus
one extra \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}}\sphinxhyphen{}named feature when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{policy.include\_label\_feature}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tabelize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tabelize()}} is a \sphinxstylestrong{static} method — call it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tabelize(catalog, ...)}}, there is no non\sphinxhyphen{}static instance overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TabelizePolicy}} reconstructs the original frame exactly only when
every stream in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{catalog}} shares the same label set; streams with differing label
sets require choosing an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} policy to control how gaps are
resolved.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_label\_feature}}’s collision handling mirrors
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/kindelize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindelize()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{materialize\_label}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{policy.collision}} decides
whether a name clash with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}} throws, gets suffixed, or overwrites.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::tail}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:dataframe-tail}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{tail}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new frame containing the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases (rows) of the current frame, in
their existing order, with every feature preserved — the mirror image of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}, which takes from the top instead of the bottom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} is a read\sphinxhyphen{}only, non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating view: it does not change case order, does not
drop or rename features, and does not recompute anything. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}}, case labels on the result are \sphinxstylestrong{not} the surviving rows’
original labels renumbered from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — they are preserved exactly as they were in the
source frame, so the last three rows of a six\sphinxhyphen{}row frame are still labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of cases to keep, counted from the bottom. Defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} rows. Values larger
than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} are clamped to the full frame instead of erroring.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default) gives you a quiet view
you print explicitly; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} allows the view to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render itself when used as a
standalone temporary expression.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A view over a new frame holding the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases and every feature of the
source frame, in the source frame’s feature order and with the source frame’s
original case labels.

The row labels are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} — the original positions in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} — not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}},

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Ask for more rows than the frame has.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{whole\_frame}} is equivalent to the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} clamps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} rather than raising, exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} does.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the top of a frame instead of the bottom, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head(n, render)}}}}}}},
which has an identical signature and clamping behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case labels are preserved verbatim from the source frame — if you need a fresh
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}based index on the result, combine this with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}}}}}} or
a reset step rather than expecting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} to renumber for you.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} never triggers a copy of the underlying column storage beyond what is
needed to build the smaller result frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::take}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:dataframe-take}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{take}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indices}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new frame built from exactly the case positions listed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}}, in
exactly the order given. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}} doesn’t need to be
contiguous or ascending — you can reorder rows, reverse a frame, or repeat a row
multiple times by listing its position more than once. This is the general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose
row\sphinxhyphen{}selection primitive several other methods ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}}}}}}}) are built on top of internally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every requested position is resolved with Python\sphinxhyphen{}style negative\sphinxhyphen{}index support (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}
means the last case), but — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s clamping behavior — an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range
position (after negative normalization) is a validation error here, not silently
clamped. Case labels on the result follow the same positions and order as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}}:
row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} keeps its original label \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} even if it now appears first in the result.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{indices} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case positions to select, in the exact order the result should have. Negative
values are interpreted relative to the end of the frame. The same position may appear
more than once — the corresponding row is duplicated once per occurrence.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one row per entry in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}}, in that exact order, holding
every feature of the source frame and the original case label of each selected
position.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/take:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}, an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range position in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}} (after negative\sphinxhyphen{}index
normalization) is a validation error, not silently clamped.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} is the primitive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}} all delegate to internally, so its result\sphinxhyphen{}shape guarantees
(feature order, dtypes, original case labels) apply to all of them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Repeating a position produces a row\sphinxhyphen{}level duplicate in the result, including a
duplicated case label — useful for bootstrapped resampling or building a synthetic
frame from an existing one’s rows.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tally:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts how many rows share each distinct combination of values across \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}},
returning a compact frame with one row per distinct combination plus a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count"}}
column — sorted by count descending, ties broken alphabetically by the key values
ascending. This is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}returning sibling of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}
packs the key columns into one composite \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} label, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}} keeps each
key feature as its own separate output column, which reads more naturally when
there’s more than one key feature to inspect.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every key column in the result is rendered as text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}), regardless of the
source feature’s original dtype — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}} builds its composite key by stringifying
every value first, the same convention {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}} use.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tally:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, required on that overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features form the key whose distinct combinations are counted. The
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally(feature, ...)}}) is shorthand for a one\sphinxhyphen{}element list.
The no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} overload counts over \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} highest\sphinxhyphen{}count rows after sorting. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the default) keeps
every row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, a row with a missing value in any key feature is excluded before
counting. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a missing key value contributes the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}
to that row’s key instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tally:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
One row per distinct key combination, one column per key feature (always
rendered as text) plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count"}}, sorted by count descending (ties broken
alphabetically by key ascending).

3    | Tema   A        90     1

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[5 cs x 4 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every combination of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(city, product, sales)}} is unique here, so every row’s count
is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, and the tie\sphinxhyphen{}break sort falls back entirely to alphabetical key order.
Notice \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}’s text\sphinxhyphen{}comparison ordering within the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} group: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"100"}}
sorts before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"95"}}, because tally’s key comparison is lexicographic (character by
character) on the stringified value, not a numeric comparison — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"1"}} is less than
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"9"}} as the very first character, regardless of the numbers’ actual magnitude.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/tally:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Key columns in the result are always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (text), even when the source feature
was numeric — sorting and tie\sphinxhyphen{}breaking both happen on the stringified value, which
can order numbers lexicographically rather than numerically (see Example 3).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} truncation happens \sphinxstylestrong{after} sorting by count descending, so it always
keeps the highest\sphinxhyphen{}count rows, never an arbitrary prefix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}}, a missing key value becomes the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}
rather than being excluded from the tally.

\end{itemize}
