\subparagraph{DataFrame::view}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:dataframe-view}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stop}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} row range wrapped in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, the same renderable
wrapper {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}} return. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view(start, stop)}} uses
the exact same slice normalization as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} — both endpoints support
Python\sphinxhyphen{}style negative indices, both are clamped into range, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} is exclusive on
both ends, positive or negative. The only thing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}} adds on top of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}} is
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} toggle: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view(start, stop, render)}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} dressed up in
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first case position to include. A negative value counts backward from the end of
the frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last case), then the result is clamped into range — identical
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} handling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case position to stop before (exclusive), positive or negative — identical to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} handling. If the normalized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} ends up before the normalized
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, the result is an empty (zero\sphinxhyphen{}case) frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A view over a new frame holding the cases in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} and every feature of
the source frame, with the source frame’s original case labels preserved.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} handling is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s in every respect
— negative\sphinxhyphen{}index normalization, clamping, and an exclusive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. The only
difference between the two methods is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} toggle and the fact that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}
always returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} rather than a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case labels on the result are the source frame’s original labels, never renumbered
— same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter works exactly as it does on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where(bool\_mask, ...)}} literally
delegates to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter(bool\_mask, ...)}} for both the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} mask
overloads, keeping only the rows where the mask is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} and dropping the rest.
Note this is \sphinxstylestrong{not} numpy/pandas \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.where()}}’s replace\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}place semantics (which
keeps every row and only replaces individual masked\sphinxhyphen{}out \sphinxstyleemphasis{values}) — for that kind

\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean mask whose length must equal the frame’s case count. Rows where the mask
is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} are kept; rows where it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) are dropped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alignment options controlling how a case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}bearing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} mask is matched
against this frame’s own case labels before filtering.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing only the rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} is a pure alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — anything documented there
(mask\sphinxhyphen{}length validation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}mask handling, case\sphinxhyphen{}label preservation) applies
identically here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is \sphinxstylestrong{not} numpy/pandas\sphinxhyphen{}style \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.where()}} replace semantics — it drops rows
rather than replacing individual masked values while keeping every row. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}} for masked, in\sphinxhyphen{}place\sphinxhyphen{}style value replacement within one feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kept rows retain their original case labels; the result is never re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{abs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the elementwise absolute value of a numeric thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::abs()}} is the sign\sphinxhyphen{}stripping numeric helper for one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional data. Use it when magnitude matters more than direction, such as absolute error, distance\sphinxhyphen{}from\sphinxhyphen{}target, or symmetric\sphinxhyphen{}threshold preprocessing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/abs:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/abs:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A numeric thread containing the absolute value of each element.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/abs:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::clip: cap values into a range instead of removing sign.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::pow: apply power transformations after magnitude cleanup when needed.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/abs:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This method is for numeric threads. Text and temporal payloads are not valid inputs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. The current thread is left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/abs:examples}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlignOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Realign one thread to a target label thread using positional, case\sphinxhyphen{}label, or feature\sphinxhyphen{}label rules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::align(...)}} is the typed column\sphinxhyphen{}level alignment surface behind many higher\sphinxhyphen{}level DataFrame operations. Use it when you are working with one extracted column directly and you need to reorder or relabel it against another label vector before comparison, arithmetic, export, or manual reconstruction.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target\_labels}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Target label vector that defines the output order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its interpretation depends on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.align}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Caselbl}}: treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_labels}} as the desired case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Feature}}: treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_labels}} as the desired feature\sphinxhyphen{}label axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}: validate strict positional compatibility without doing label\sphinxhyphen{}based remapping.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alignment policy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} exposes two public fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}: chooses the matching rule.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}: strict positional alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Caselbl}}: match by case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Feature}}: match by feature labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Both}}: not supported on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}: optional numeric fill scalar for newly introduced gaps.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
New thread whose values and label provenance reflect the requested alignment mode.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Caselbl` gathers values by case label.
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Feature` gathers one value per feature label.
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Pos` keeps positional matching strict.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::align: frame\sphinxhyphen{}level alignment for several features at once.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::label: use label().set(…) to attach explicit labels before aligning by label.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Both}} is a DataFrame\sphinxhyphen{}oriented concept and is rejected for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is omitted, unmatched target labels produce missing output entries. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is provided, newly introduced numeric gaps are filled with that scalar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}} does not broadcast. It expects compatible lengths and preserves the current thread’s value order and visible labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return whether every value in a boolean thread is true.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::all(...)}} is the scalar truth reduction for one thread. It is the right tool when one falsey element should invalidate the whole column\sphinxhyphen{}level condition.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing\sphinxhyphen{}value policy for the reduction.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: ignore missing boolean positions while reducing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: missing boolean payloads are not supported for this reduction path.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
One scalar truth result.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This method expects a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payload. It is not a general numeric reduction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nullable boolean input requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull=true}}.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::astype(...)}} is the direct dtype\sphinxhyphen{}conversion surface on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. Use it when imported data need normalization, flags stored as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0/1}} should become booleans, or downstream kernels expect a more specific scalar dtype.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dtype}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Target scalar dtype.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common choices include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Bool}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Int64}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Float64}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose the smallest dtype that still supports the downstream operations you plan to run.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread with the requested dtype conversion applied.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::as\_series: drop down to the Series payload when you need broader low\sphinxhyphen{}level numeric control.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::astype: cast several frame features at once.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the direct scalar\sphinxhyphen{}dtype conversion route. It is best for numeric Series\sphinxhyphen{}backed threads.

\subparagraph{Thread::bfill}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:thread-bfill}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill::doc}}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill missing values by borrowing the next observed value in the thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::bfill(...)}} is the one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill helper. Use it when each missing position should inherit from the next valid observation below it in the same thread.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of consecutive missing positions to fill per run.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}: unlimited backward fill.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positive integer: fill at most that many missing positions in each consecutive run.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread with backward\sphinxhyphen{}filled values.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::ffill: propagate the last observed value forward instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::bfill: backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill several frame features together.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Trailing missing runs stay missing because there is no later observed value to borrow.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute custom\sphinxhyphen{}window statistics on one thread by supplying explicit per\sphinxhyphen{}row bounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::bounded(...)}} is the one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional version of custom windowing. It is the right tool when fixed rolling widths are not expressive enough and each row should choose its own window.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bounds}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback that generates the per\sphinxhyphen{}row window boundaries.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It receives the thread size and active \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowOptions}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends}}, one pair per output row.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each row’s window is interpreted as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Window statistic to compute inside each row’s bounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common values include \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional window policy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Important fields include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}: minimum observed values required for a valid output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}: degrees of freedom for variance\sphinxhyphen{}style statistics.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered}}: centering hint for methods that honor it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}}: interval\sphinxhyphen{}closure policy for methods that honor it.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

One output value per input row after applying the requested window statistic.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bounds callback returns half\sphinxhyphen{}open intervals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}} for each output row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowOptions::min\_count}} controls how many observed values must be present before one row’s result becomes valid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return whether each element falls between two bounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::btw(...)}} is the interval\sphinxhyphen{}membership surface on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. It supports scalar numeric bounds, scalar temporal/string bounds, and rowwise lower/upper threads. This makes it useful for grading bands, date windows, threshold rules, and per\sphinxhyphen{}row tolerance envelopes.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{a}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower scalar numeric bound for the numeric\sphinxhyphen{}scalar overloads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{b}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upper scalar numeric bound for the numeric\sphinxhyphen{}scalar overloads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{lo}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower bound.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In scalar temporal/text overloads, this is one lower literal bound.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In rowwise overloads, this is the lower\sphinxhyphen{}bound thread used element by element.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{hi}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upper bound.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In scalar temporal/text overloads, this is one upper literal bound.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In rowwise overloads, this is the upper\sphinxhyphen{}bound thread used element by element.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{inclusive}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shared boundary\sphinxhyphen{}closure shorthand.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: both boundaries are closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: both boundaries are open.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this when both sides should share the same closure rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_left}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the lower boundary is included.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the lower boundary is closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the lower boundary is open.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_right}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the upper boundary is included.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the upper boundary is closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the upper boundary is open.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean thread containing one interval\sphinxhyphen{}membership result per element.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::ge and Thread::le: spell out the two comparisons manually when you want the lower and upper tests separately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::filter: use the boolean result as a row mask inside a frame workflow.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The overload family supports three bound styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numeric scalar bounds,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temporal/text scalar bounds,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rowwise lower/upper threads.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you use the two\sphinxhyphen{}boolean form, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_right}} independently control whether each boundary is closed or open.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The one\sphinxhyphen{}boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inclusive}} shorthand differs by overload family in the current API. The examples below show the actual behavior for each family, which is why this method deserves more careful reading than simpler comparison helpers.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert a numeric thread into interval labels defined by explicit bin edges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::bucketize(...)}} is the one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional interval bucketing helper behind histogram\sphinxhyphen{}style feature engineering, grading bands, and coarse segmentation rules.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bins}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Strictly increasing interval edges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.0, 20.0, 40.0, 60.0\}}} defines three buckets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{labels}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional explicit bucket labels.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leave empty for default labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pass explicit labels such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{10, 20, 30\}}} when later logic expects custom codes.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{right}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Right\sphinxhyphen{}closure policy.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: intervals are right\sphinxhyphen{}closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: intervals are left\sphinxhyphen{}closed and right\sphinxhyphen{}open.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_lowest}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the first interval includes its lower boundary.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: values exactly equal to the first edge can enter the first bucket.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first lower boundary stays open.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A numeric thread of bucket labels, with missing output where the source value falls outside the provided bin range.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::bucketize: bucketize selected numeric frame features while preserving the rest of the table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::btw: perform interval\sphinxhyphen{}membership tests without collapsing values into bucket labels.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} output buckets you need \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} bin edges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit labels are useful when downstream rules expect domain codes instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} is stronger than simple lowercase conversion. It is the text\sphinxhyphen{}normalization route to prefer before equality checks or membership checks that should ignore case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this when you need ordering or equality information between two entries without materializing a full boolean thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the calendar\sphinxhyphen{}field projection for timeline and time\sphinxhyphen{}index threads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when your temporal thread already carries full timestamps but the downstream computation needs just the calendar day.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Thread::describe}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Summarize one thread instead of carrying every original value forward.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} adapts to the payload family: numeric threads get numeric descriptive statistics, while note threads get count/unique/top/freq style summaries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the direct per\sphinxhyphen{}column analogue of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe()}} when you already know which one thread you want to inspect.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned view.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: keep explicit control over when the summary is printed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: allow the returned view to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in temporary display contexts.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}
Compact summary view of the current thread.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric series and note\sphinxhyphen{}backed text threads follow different summary contracts, so the output shape depends on the payload family.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For numeric threads, the statistics are ordered as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For note threads, the summary is frequency\sphinxhyphen{}oriented: observed count, number of unique values, most frequent value, and its frequency.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:output}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return distinct values in stable first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this when you want the unique observed values themselves, not just the count.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike a sorting operation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct(...)}} preserves the encounter order of the first surviving representatives.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether missing entries should be removed before distinctness is computed.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: ignore null entries,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: keep at most one null entry in the output.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This flag matters when missingness itself is meaningful and you want a single null representative preserved among the distinct values.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
Thread containing one representative of each distinct value, ordered by first appearance.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct(...)}} is value\sphinxhyphen{}returning, not count\sphinxhyphen{}returning. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct(...)}} when you only need the number of distinct values.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div(...)}} is the named thread\sphinxhyphen{}level division surface behind \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}\sphinxhyphen{}style arithmetic when you want a method in a chain or you want the overload family documented explicitly.

\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the direct thread\sphinxhyphen{}level route when you want only the observed values carried forward.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}} operates on the thread validity mask. Plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} values inside a numeric series are not dropped unless they are represented as missing by the thread mask.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build a boolean mask that marks duplicate entries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the thread\sphinxhyphen{}level inspection route behind duplicate\sphinxhyphen{}aware filtering and counting workflows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It tells you which entries are duplicate followers under the keep policy you selected.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the first observed occurrence in each duplicate group should be treated as the surviving reference entry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default keep\sphinxhyphen{}first route, the first appearance of a value stays unmarked and later repeats are marked duplicate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the last observed occurrence in each duplicate group should be treated as the surviving reference entry instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With this route, earlier repeats are marked duplicate and the final appearance is left unmarked.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(...)}} reports duplicate membership only. It never removes entries by itself.

\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{encoding}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extract one or more regex capture groups from a note\sphinxhyphen{}backed thread into a DataFrame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract(...)}} is the structured regex parsing surface for text columns. Use it when one note column contains several embedded fields and you want each capture group broken out into its own feature.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regular expression with one or more capture groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only capture groups become output features. Surround the pieces you want to extract with parentheses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional feature names for the capture groups.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
leave it empty to receive generated names such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_1}}, …

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pass one name per capture group when you want semantic output feature names

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
Frame with one note\sphinxhyphen{}backed feature per capture group.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Rows that do not match the regex stay present in the output, but the unmatched capture\PYGZhy{}group cells are marked missing.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::matches: boolean regex test when you only need a mask.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::split: delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}based decomposition instead of regex capture groups.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pattern must contain at least one capture group. A regex with no capture groups throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} is supplied, its length must match the number of capture groups exactly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output features are note\sphinxhyphen{}backed because regex capture groups produce text fragments.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Thread::label}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:thread-label}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadLabelAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the Thread label machinery for inspecting and manipulating 1D case labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::label()}} is the 1D foundation for label handling. DataFrame label machinery is built above this because a DataFrame case axis is itself a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this surface for new code instead of reaching for lower\sphinxhyphen{}level case\sphinxhyphen{}label helpers directly:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().values()}} returns the current label values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().has()}} reports whether the thread is defined and can expose labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().set(labels)}} returns a copy with explicit labels attached.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().range()}} returns a copy with explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..n\sphinxhyphen{}1}} labels materialized.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().reset()}} returns a copy with explicit labels cleared.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().align(target, options)}} delegates to Thread alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().unite(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intersect(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{symdiff(...)}} provide Index\sphinxhyphen{}style set operations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().find(targets)}} returns exact\sphinxhyphen{}match positions and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} for missing targets.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().pos(value)}} returns all matching positions for one label and throws when absent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().slice(start, stop)}} returns an inclusive label\sphinxhyphen{}value slice.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().fillnull(...)}} returns a copy whose labels have missing values filled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().isnull()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().notnull()}} inspect label missingness.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadLabelAccessor}}
Lightweight 1D label accessor bound to the source thread.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().values()}} returns default range labels when the thread has no explicit labels, matching the Pluss hybrid alignment model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().range()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().reset()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().align(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().fillnull(...)}} are non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. They return new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().values()}} returns the frame’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread. Thread \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label()}} is where 1D relabeling and 1D label alignment live.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set operations preserve label payload dtype when the two label vectors are compatible: same Series dtype stays unchanged, mixed numeric Series labels upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}, Note labels stay Note, and Timeline/TimeIndex labels stay temporal. Incompatible mixed label payloads fall back to Note labels through comparable string keys.

\subparagraph{Signature}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build a boolean mask that marks every entry whose value appears more than once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} differs from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}} marks duplicate occurrences according to a keep policy, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} marks the whole repeated group.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
Boolean\sphinxhyphen{}like thread with one value per entry indicating whether that value belongs to a repeated group.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}A, B, A, C, B{]}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}true, true, true, false, true{]}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(...)}} when you want pandas\sphinxhyphen{}style duplicate follower semantics such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}false, false, true, false, true{]}}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a cumulative statistic such as running sum, product, min, or max down the thread.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic}
Supported values:
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}: Compute a cumulative sum down the feature.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}: Compute a cumulative product down the feature.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}: Compute the running minimum down the feature.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}: Compute the running maximum down the feature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls}
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, a null output remains null only at that case and later cumulative values resume; when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, every output after the first null is null.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/select:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this to reduce the current object to the rows or fields that matter for the next step.

\subparagraph{Practical Behavior}
\label{\detokenize{atlas_api_reference:practical-behavior}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate\_over\_frames(...)}} hands the full frame vector to your reducer and expects one output object back.

\subsubsection{Advanced Thread, UDF, Text, and Delegation API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{advanced_thread_api_reference:advanced-thread-udf-text-and-delegation-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{advanced_thread_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Outputs on this page are exercised by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plussmic\_table\_statistics\_window\_tests}}. Built\sphinxhyphen{}in numeric work stays in Series kernels; scalar and case callbacks are explicit UDF boundaries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Full Unicode normalization and case conversion use the Unicode backend discovered while building the SDK. A build without that backend still handles ASCII exactly and fails explicitly for non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input.

\subsubsection{Time\sphinxhyphen{}Series Accessor Guide}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:time-series-accessor-guide}}\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} surface for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} for numeric time\sphinxhyphen{}series values. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tl()}} for datetime/timeline
values.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:api-signature}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTsAccessor}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} TimeSeriesAccessor}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTsAccessor}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compatibility overloads still accept feature names, but preferred public code is
selection\sphinxhyphen{}first: select the value feature(s), then call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} with no feature
names.


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}} after selecting numeric value features when you want transforms returned as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.\\
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ts()}} when you want transforms returned as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} for one column.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::ts()}} when you want the same transform delegated to every frame in an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.

\paragraph{Common Pitfall}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:common-pitfall}}

If you call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\textbackslash{}"col\textbackslash{}").ts()...}}, you are on the \sphinxstylestrong{Thread} surface and the return type is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Timeline (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{tl}}) and Batched DataFrame Operations}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:timeline-tl-and-batched-dataframe-operations}}\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page covers the Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native timeline surface and the batched numeric
delegation path added for multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature DataFrame operations.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:api-signature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tl() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} ThreadTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(feature: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(features: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(features: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{} = \{\}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(feature: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(features: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(features: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{} = \{\}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} is the datetime/timeline surface. It is separate from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}}
extracts and transforms datetime payloads, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} remains the time\sphinxhyphen{}series
analytics surface for returns, lag/lead, rolling blocks, resampling, and
alignment.


\paragraph{Inputs}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:inputs}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}: one Timeline or TimeIndex feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: zero or more Timeline/TimeIndex feature names. Empty selection
is valid only after an intentional selection where every feature in the
current frame is Timeline/TimeIndex, for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"event\_time"\}).tl()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}: calendar/time unit accepted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} rounding methods, such as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}, or compatible CodeH units.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}}: signed number of frequency steps to shift.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}}: shift/period frequency such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"year"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineLocalizeOptions}}: option struct with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.fold}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.nonexistent}} fields.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:output}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} with selected features replaced
by the transformed result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Atlas\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} after applying the DataFrame operation
to each frame.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Options}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit}} controls epoch extraction:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Nanos}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Micros}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Millis}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Seconds}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineLocalizeOptions}} supports C++20 designated initializers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimelineLocalizeOptions}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{UTC}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nonexistent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{raise}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:examples}}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{clip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

Notes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\subsubsection{Hierarchical Cases}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:hierarchical-cases}}\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hierarchical cases are PlussMic’s structured case\sphinxhyphen{}axis engine. They are the
Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native equivalent of a pandas MultiIndex on rows, but the public language
uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case hierarchy is stored as typed case\sphinxhyphen{}label metadata. Display labels may
look like joined strings, but operations use the structured case\sphinxhyphen{}label payloads.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:api-signature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(options: SetLabelOptions) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(feature\_name: string\_view, drop\_feature: bool = false) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(feature\_names: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}, drop\_features: bool = false, separator: string\_view = "\textbackslash{}x1F") \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().has() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} bool}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().names() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} vector\textless{}string\textgreater{}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().part(name: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Thread}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().part(position: int64) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Thread}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::case\_study(pick: CasePick) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().sort(options: SortLabelOptions) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::group\_by(keys: LabelGroup, specs: RangeView\textless{}GroupSpec\textgreater{}, dropnull\_keys: bool = true, render: bool = false) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameView}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().rename(renames: RangeView\textless{}LabelRename\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().order(names: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::unstack(label: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}


\paragraph{Options}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: features promoted into structured case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: removes promoted features from the ordinary feature axis when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verify}}: checks for duplicate full structured keys when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}: sorts by the selected case labels after construction when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}: display\sphinxhyphen{}label separator only; structured operations do not depend on it.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: select by one named case label.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}: select by several named case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}}: select by the full structured key in case\sphinxhyphen{}label order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: drops matched case labels after selection when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SortCaselblOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}}: case\sphinxhyphen{}label names used for typed stable sorting. Empty means sort by the flat case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}: sort direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}: null ordering.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LabelGroup}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}}: group by one case label.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}}: group by several case labels.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResetLabelOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: discards case labels when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}: replacement feature names for materialized case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}: fallback name prefix when case\sphinxhyphen{}label names are empty.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnstackOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}}: case label moved into feature names.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: drops remaining case\sphinxhyphen{}label materialization from ordinary features after rebuilding the case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}: sorts unstacked feature labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}: joins value\sphinxhyphen{}feature names and unstacked labels when several value features exist.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A hierarchical case axis is typed. Numeric case labels remain numeric, text case labels remain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, and timeline case labels remain temporal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(...)}}, transforms, and feature reordering preserve case\sphinxhyphen{}label metadata.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_study(CasePick)}} supports partial\sphinxhyphen{}label and full\sphinxhyphen{}key lookup.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by(LabelGroup\{...\})}} groups by case labels without requiring those labels to exist as ordinary features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack(...)}} rejects duplicate output cells. Aggregate first when multiple rows map to the same output cell.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stack(...)}} moves feature names into the case hierarchy and preserves homogeneous typed values.

\end{itemize}

Runs a SQL query against the current frame and returns the result as a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row rounded
\sphinxstyleemphasis{up} to the nearest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} boundary, in local wall time — same feature name,
still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} (second), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"m"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}
(minute), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}} (hour), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}} (day). Cannot be
empty.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature ceiled to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

out.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/epoch:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with its Unix epoch
value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}, as a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature name, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/epoch:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Nanos}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of the fixed\sphinxhyphen{}duration units: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nanos}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Micros}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Millis}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Seconds}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Days}}. Passing a span\sphinxhyphen{}only unit (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Weeks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} — the calendar\sphinxhyphen{}relative units meant for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{span()}}}}}}}, not a fixed epoch count) throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/epoch:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature replaced by an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} Series
of epoch counts in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/epoch:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default unit is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nanos}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Seconds}} — calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epoch()}} with no
argument on the same data above would return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1704067210000000000{]}}}
instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only fixed\sphinxhyphen{}duration units are accepted (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nanos}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Micros}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Millis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Seconds}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Days}}); passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Weeks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} throws, since
those units only make sense as a calendar\sphinxhyphen{}relative distance between two
timestamps — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{span()}}}}}}} for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row (or one already null on the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}) displays as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}, not a sentinel epoch value.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::floor}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:dataframetimelineaccessor-floor}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{floor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unit}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row rounded
\sphinxstyleemphasis{down} to the nearest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} boundary, in local wall time — same feature
name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} (second), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"m"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}
(minute), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}} (hour), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}} (day). Cannot be
empty. Sub\sphinxhyphen{}day units coarser than these (weeks, months) aren’t supported.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flooring happens in \sphinxstylestrong{local wall time} (per the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}’s current
timezone), then maps back — so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor("D")}} aligns to local midnight, not
necessarily UTC midnight, if the timezone isn’t \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} cannot be empty, and only accepts the fixed clock units listed above
— there’s no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"W"}} (week) or calendar\sphinxhyphen{}month unit here; see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/period::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{period()}}}}}}} for month/year truncation instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} (displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}) regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with a custom text
representation built from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature
name, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strftime}}\sphinxhyphen{}style format string. Recognized tokens: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%Y}} (4\sphinxhyphen{}digit year),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%m}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%d}} (2\sphinxhyphen{}digit month/day), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%H}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%M}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%S}} (2\sphinxhyphen{}digit hour/minute/second),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%f}} (9\sphinxhyphen{}digit zero\sphinxhyphen{}padded nanoseconds), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%z}} (UTC offset as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+HH:MM}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}HH:MM}}
— never a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%a}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%A}} (abbreviated/full weekday name), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%b}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%B}}
(abbreviated/full month name), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%\%}} (a literal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}}). Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}}
sequence, or any character outside a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}} token, is copied through literally.

outright rather than silently producing an empty string for every row.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} cannot be empty — an empty pattern throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%f}} always emits all 9 nanosecond digits, zero\sphinxhyphen{}padded — there’s no way to
ask for fewer digits (e.g. milliseconds only) directly; slice the resulting
text with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}}}}}}} accessor methods if you need
fewer digits.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%z}} always renders as a signed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HH:MM}} offset (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"+00:00"}}), never the
bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Z"}} suffix some ISO\sphinxhyphen{}8601 tooling uses for UTC.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row (or one already null on the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}) displays as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/hour:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with its hour\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}day
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{23}}), as a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature name, same row order.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/hour:returns}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}

hour\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}day.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

underlying instant.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/index:signature}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{require\PYGZus{}sorted}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/index:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} feature with an equivalent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} —
same feature name, same row order, same displayed values. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} is the
monotonic time\sphinxhyphen{}axis type other parts of the library (like duration\sphinxhyphen{}based
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts().resample()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts().rolling(duration)}}) expect. A feature already
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind is passed through unchanged.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/index:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{require\_sorted} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default), every value must be non\sphinxhyphen{}decreasing and non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}},
or the call throws. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, the conversion happens without checking
order or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} — but the result may then misbehave in code elsewhere that
assumes a genuinely monotonic \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/index:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} feature converted to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reinterprets every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{current} clock
reading as a naive local wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}}, and converts it to

underlying instant} (unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}}, which only relabels display).
The row is then displayed under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}}, so its wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock text looks
unchanged even though the instant it now represents has shifted.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:parameters}}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}}’s Notes — and cannot be empty), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}; during the

daylight offset and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold = 1}} resolves to the standard offset), and

when a row’s local reading falls in the daylight\sphinxhyphen{}saving \sphinxstyleemphasis{spring\sphinxhyphen{}forward} gap,

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{localize()}} changes the underlying instant; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}} never
does.} Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{localize()}} only when the current ticks are naive local
readings that have never been anchored to a real instant; reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}
when the ticks are already correct and you just want a different display
timezone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}} only accepts the same four names as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}} — anything else
throws — and cannot be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold}} only matters for the one hour of wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time that repeats during
a fall\sphinxhyphen{}back transition; outside that window it has no effect.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nonexistent}} only recognizes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"shift\_forward"}} as an actual handling
strategy; every other value (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"raise"}} included) throws for a
spring\sphinxhyphen{}forward\sphinxhyphen{}gap reading, regardless of what the string itself says.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{freq} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"y"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"yr"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"year"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"years"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"annual"}} (truncate to January 1st,
00:00:00 of the row’s year), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mo"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mth"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"months"}} (truncate to
the 1st of the row’s month, 00:00:00), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"days"}} (floor to local
midnight), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hr"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hours"}} (floor to the hour),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"t"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minutes"}} (floor to the minute), or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"seconds"}} (floor to the second) — case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive.
Cannot be empty.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/period:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature truncated to the start of its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} period.
